articles.title: Il existe un malware qui vole vos données et demande à des IA comme Claude combien vous valez exactement
articles.text:
Un nouveau malware pour Windows demande à une IA combien valent ses victimes. Baptisé VOLTA, cet voleur d'informations, ou infostealer, fait analyser les données volées par Claude, et prévoit même d’autres modèles en cas de refus.
Un malware qui vole vos données, puis demande à une intelligence artificielle de calculer votre valeur marchande, voilà qui a de quoi choquer, mais qui fin 2026, n'est même plus étonnant. Quoi qu'il en soit, VOLTA, le nom de cet infostealer, ne se contente plus de piller un ordinateur, il fait aussi juger son butin par une machine. Autrement dit, un voleur d'information disons traditionnel vole des données et les envoie au pirate, qui doit ensuite trier lui-même ce qu'il a récupéré. VOLTA ajoute une étape, car avant d’envoyer quoi que ce soit, il fait analyser ce qu’il a volé par une IA, qui dit au pirate ce que la victime « vaut » et ce qui est le plus rentable à exploiter.
Repéré par Cisco Talos dans un rapport publié le 31 octobre 2026, ce programme pour Windows fouille jusque dans vos reçus de commande pour reconstituer votre quotidien, avant de soumettre le dossier à un modèle de langage. Et si l'IA sollicitée a le mauvais goût de refuser la besogne, il frappe simplement à la porte d'à côté, vers d'autres modèles.
Un infostealer trop curieux, qui lit jusqu'à vos tickets de caisse
Sur le papier, VOLTA coche toutes les cases du voleur de données classique. Il se nourrit de tout, qu'il s'agisse des cookies des navigateurs, mots de passe, cartes bancaires enregistrées, phrases de récupération de portefeuilles crypto, sessions Telegram, Discord, Steam ou Roblox, et ce jusqu'aux profils Outlook, Thunderbird et Slack. Il emporte aussi les jetons de connexion Microsoft, les clés SSH et d'accès au cloud, des captures d'écran, et le mot de passe de chaque réseau Wi-Fi enregistré sur le PC, en clair. Les portefeuilles crypto protégés par un mot de passe ? Figurez-vous qu'il tente de les craquer sur place.
C'est ensuite que les choses deviennent franchement intrusives. Muni de vos propres accès, VOLTA ouvre votre boîte Gmail pour y dénicher les reçus d'Amazon, PayPal, Uber Eats, DoorDash, Grubhub et Walmart, histoire de confirmer votre adresse postale. Il réclame directement l'historique de vos commandes à Uber Eats et DoorDash, avec vos propres sessions, enrichit votre profil Discord grâce au jeton dérobé et fait même estimer la valeur de votre inventaire Roblox par un site spécialisé. Votre dernier burger livré devient un peu comme une pièce à conviction.
Toutes ces trouvailles finissent dans une véritable fiche de police, enregistrée sous le nom Identity_Report.txt. On y retrouve tout un tas d'éléments, avec votre localisation et votre adresse, votre employeur et le nom de domaine de votre entreprise, comme celui de votre adresse mail professionnelle, votre année de naissance probable et les quatre derniers chiffres de votre carte bancaire. Mais aussi les espaces de la messagerie de groupe Slack auxquels vous êtes connecté, le nom d'auteur que les logiciels de bureautique glissent discrètement dans vos documents, ou encore la trace d'une sauvegarde d'iPhone sur le PC. Shane Barney, responsable de la sécurité des systèmes d'information chez Keeper Security, nous alerte en nous disant que « VOLTA montre que l'IA est utilisée pour évaluer la valeur des identités volées ». Car ce dossier a un premier lecteur, et vous allez voir qu'il n'est pas humain.
Une IA promue analyste du crime
Le dossier est transmis à un grand modèle de langage en passant par OpenRouter, qui est une plateforme qui donne accès à de nombreuses intelligences artificielles du marché. La consigne est de se comporter en analyste du renseignement forensique et de rédiger une évaluation de la cible. Le rapport attendu détaille ce que vaut la victime, ses biens étant classés selon leur potentiel de monétisation, de faible à élevé, puis juge sa prudence numérique, mots de passe compris. La « température » du modèle, qui règle sa part d'improvisation, est fixée très bas, à 0,2, signe, selon Talos, que l'auteur mise sur des réponses précises et constantes, plutôt que sur la créativité.
L'IA doit aussi jouer les détectives en reliant des indices dispersés. Si un mot de passe reprend votre nom, votre adresse ou le nom de votre ancienne université, par exemple, elle est censée le repérer, c'est une information précieuse pour un pirate. On ne lui demande donc plus seulement de trouver des données, mais d'en tirer des conclusions. Talos parle d'« effort displacement », un déplacement de l'effort. Le tri fastidieux des données volées, jusqu'ici fait à la main par un humain, est confié à la machine. Shane Barney le résume d'une formule : « l'IA remplace l'analyste humain ». Les chercheurs le soulignent, le malware ne vole ni plus vite ni davantage. Il épargne surtout du travail à l'escroc, qui reçoit un dossier argumenté plutôt qu'une montagne de fichiers bruts.
Le détail le plus savoureux porte sur la gestion des refus. Le modèle appelé par défaut est Claude Opus 4.6, d'Anthropic. Le malware guette dans sa réponse des formules comme « I can't », pour Je ne peux pas, ou « I'm not able », Je ne suis pas capable, et, s'il en repère une, il se tourne vers Kimi K2, de Moonshot AI, puis vers Gemini 2.5 Flash, de Google. On comprend donc que l'auteur du logiciel malveillant s'attendait à buter sur des garde-fous. Il a donc prévu des modèles plus petits, et plus conciliants. Talos ne dit pas, en revanche, si l'une de ces IA a effectivement accepté la besogne.
L'IA reste d'ailleurs en option ici. Pour y accéder, l'acheteur du malware doit fournir sa propre clé d'API, une sorte de code d'accès aux modèles d'IA. Sans elle, VOLTA vole et transmet les données comme n'importe quel infostealer, simplement sans le tri.
Un malware en kit, et les réflexes pour lui fermer la porte
L'autre élément notable, c'est que VOLTA a tout, selon Talos, d'un produit vendu clé en main. Son code prévoit en effet six emplacements que l'acheteur remplit à la compilation, dont sa clé d'API et son canal Telegram. Ces paramètres sont chiffrés, mais de façon surtout cosmétique. Un client même peu aguerri reçoit ainsi les fiches de ses victimes dans sa messagerie, en plusieurs archives : le butin brut d'abord, puis le verdict de l'IA, consigné dans un fichier AI_Analysis.txt. Aucun serveur n'appartient à l'attaquant, et l'appel à l'IA passe par la connexion internet de la victime, depuis sa propre machine. Le programme, lui, finit par s'effacer.
Si vous pensiez que le risque s'arrêtait à la vie privée des victimes, ce qui est déjà beaucoup, VOLTA va encore plus loin, car il touche aussi les entreprises. Parmi les données volées figurent notamment des jetons Microsoft, les espèces de badges numériques qui gardent une session ouverte sans redemander le mot de passe, des clés d'accès au cloud et des espaces Slack. De quoi ouvrir la porte des systèmes d'une société. Shane Barney rappelle que les infostealers servent souvent de première étape à une attaque par rançongiciel ou à un chantage aux données, car « un identifiant ou un jeton de session volé peut se faire passer pour l'accès d'un utilisateur légitime ».
L'expert cyber recommande le zero trust, qui consiste à ne jamais accorder sa confiance par défaut à une connexion, et le moindre privilège, qui limite chaque accès au strict nécessaire. Il invite aussi à « traiter chaque identifiant et chaque session présents sur un terminal comme une cible de grande valeur ». Talos conseille enfin de surveiller les lancements de Chrome en mode invisible, sans fenêtre à l'écran, puisque c'est par ce biais que VOLTA contourne le chiffrement qui protège notamment les cookies de Chrome.
Pour les particuliers, il y a quelques bons réflexes à adopter. Il ne faut par exemple jamais stocker sa phrase de récupération crypto dans un simple fichier. Il est nécessaire d'activer la double authentification pourtant où il n'y est pas encore et, au moindre doute, déconnecter toutes ses sessions et changer ses mots de passe. Si une phrase de récupération a fuité, Talos recommande de transférer les fonds vers un nouveau portefeuille créé sur un appareil hors ligne. Pensez aussi que même effacé, VOLTA peut laisser derrière lui un journal, volta_debug.txt, dans le dossier AppData, qui liste ce qui a été dérobé et indique si l'appel à l'IA a abouti. Pour le coup, mieux vaut le conserver. Les voleurs ont appris à déléguer ; aux victimes d'apprendre à verrouiller désormais.

articles.title: Epic Games regala 11 juegos por tiempo limitado: cómo reclamarlos en pocos pasos
articles.text:
Epic Games ofrece 11 juegos para PC sin costo por tiempo limitado, con títulos de carreras, plataformas, puzles, combates medievales y terror. La promoción se divide en dos plazos: Sorry We’re Closed puede reclamarse hasta el jueves 5 de noviembre de 2026, mientras que otros 10 juegos estarán disponibles hasta el domingo 8 de noviembre.
No se requiere una suscripción ni una compra previa. Solo hay que tener una cuenta gratuita, acceder a la ficha de cada juego y completar el pedido a costo cero. Una vez que el título se incorpora a la biblioteca, queda asociado de forma permanente a la cuenta, incluso cuando vuelva a tener precio.
Cuáles juegos se pueden reclamar gratis en Epic Games
La lista incluye 10 títulos, que aparecen con un descuento del 100% hasta el 8 de noviembre de 2026. Son propuestas de menor escala, con géneros variados y partidas orientadas a la conducción, la habilidad, el cálculo o la acción.
- Balloon Strike.
- Dark Mystery.
- Funtoon’s World.
- Gladiator: Blades of Fury.
- Highway Driving.
- Math Fun.
- Maze: The Amazing Labyrinth.
- Mountain Racing.
- Quiztopia: The Ultimate Trivia.
- Super Kids Racing: Mini Edition.
A esa selección se suma Sorry We’re Closed, una aventura de terror y supervivencia. Su plazo es más acotado: la promoción termina el jueves 5 de noviembre de 2026.
Qué juegos de carreras, plataformas y acción incluye la oferta
El acceso gratuito reúne varios títulos centrados en partidas rápidas. Highway Driving propone carreras en tres dimensiones con distintos vehículos, modalidades y desafíos para desbloquear contenido.
Mountain Racing, en tanto, traslada la conducción a caminos de montaña con pendientes, curvas y obstáculos. Super Kids Racing: Mini Edition incorpora 50 niveles, 50 vehículos, cinco entornos y multijugador local a pantalla dividida.
En el apartado de acción aparece Gladiator: Blades of Fury, un juego de combate medieval en tercera persona con 20 guerreros de cuatro clanes: bárbaros, asesinos, caballeros y enanos. Cuenta con siete escenarios, distintas dificultades, modo torneo y compatibilidad con mandos de Xbox. Para quienes prefieren plataformas, Funtoon’s World presenta 25 niveles, monedas, monstruos y varios personajes seleccionables.
Cuáles opciones existen para quienes prefieren puzles, lógica y preguntas
Dark Mystery combina plataformas y rompecabezas. El jugador controla a Furry, que debe avanzar por un mundo oscuro para encontrar a su reina desaparecida. El recorrido incluye 35 niveles con trampas, obstáculos y desafíos de lógica que abren el camino hacia nuevas zonas.
Además, la selección incorpora juegos de cálculo y orientación. Math Fun plantea ejercicios matemáticos y operaciones para resolver contra reloj.
Quiztopia: The Ultimate Trivia reúne preguntas de ciencias, geografía, inglés, matemáticas y cultura general, con distintos niveles de dificultad. Maze: The Amazing Labyrinth lleva la propuesta a 50 laberintos con rutas y obstáculos que exigen encontrar la salida.
De qué trata Sorry We’re Closed
Sorry We’re Closed es el juego con la fecha límite más cercana. La historia sigue a Michelle, una joven afectada por la maldición de un demonio obsesionado con el amor. Sus decisiones influyen en el destino de varios personajes, dentro de un universo que mezcla demonios, ángeles y elementos sobrenaturales.
Asimismo, la protagonista cuenta con un tercer ojo que permite observar dos realidades, hallar secretos y detectar puntos débiles de los enemigos. La exploración usa cámaras fijas, en una referencia a los títulos clásicos del terror de supervivencia, mientras que los enfrentamientos se desarrollan en primera persona.
Cómo reclamar los juegos gratuitos en Epic Games
El proceso requiere iniciar sesión en la Epic Games Store desde el navegador o el programa de escritorio. Después hay que buscar el juego elegido, abrir su ficha y pulsar la opción “Obtener”. La plataforma mostrará un pedido con valor de cero, que debe confirmarse para completar la incorporación a la cuenta.
No se debe descargar los juegos en ese momento. Tras confirmar el pedido, los títulos quedan guardados en la biblioteca y podrán instalarse más adelante desde cualquier computadora compatible.

articles.title: 'It's a slap in the face to post this': Nvidia's new Steam demo is a virtual unboxing of a GeForce 8800 GTX — but with an RTX 5080 GPU recommended to run it, gamers feel like it's a bad joke
articles.text:
Nvidia's new Steam demo lets you virtually install a GeForce 8800 GTX in a Windows Vista PC — but it has enraged many gamers
What GPU pricing crisis?
- Nvidia has a new interactive demo out on Steam
- It offers a virtual unboxing of a GeForce 8800 GTX…
- …but you need an RTX 4070 to run it, and the recommended GPU is an RTX 5080
- Some gamers feel that it's a 'slap in the face' for several reasons
Can't afford a new GPU thanks to the ever-worsening RAM crisis? Well, Nvidia wants to take you back to the days when a graphics card didn't destroy your bank balance, courtesy of a new demo on Steam where you get to unbox and install a GeForce GPU from 2006.
The Verge spotted the interactive demo entitled 'GeForce 8800 GTX — 20 Years of a Legend' which can be grabbed for free on Steam.
It was developed by Dylan Browne, an Unreal Engine artist who was commissioned by Nvidia, and the demo is rendered in Unreal Engine (unsurprisingly). The idea is that you can: "Step into a 2006-era PC gaming room, unbox the GeForce 8800 GTX, inspect it up close, and install it in an era-accurate PC tower."
On the face of it, that's a rather fun idea — and it's smartly implemented to be fair, including revisiting Windows Vista on a CRT monitor — but if you start to think about it more deeply, this exercise seems more than a little tone deaf in the current PC components climate.
Have a watch of Nvidia's illustrative clip below first off, before we move on to discuss this one.
Analysis: ragebait, greed, and a lot of other accusations from gamers
One of the most obvious sticking points here is the requirements to run this demo. What Nvidia GPU will you need to take part in a virtual unboxing? Here's a clue: it certainly won't run on a GeForce 8800 GTX. In fact you'll need an RTX 4070 at the minimum, and the recommended GPU as per the Steam specs is a… wait for it… RTX 5080. (You must have 32GB of RAM, as well, at minimum).
And this comes at a time when the RAM crisis has made that RTX 5080 soar in price to over double its MSRP in the US, and with hefty inflation evident in all countries (over 50% in the UK for example). Don't even start with the RTX 5090, and as we've seen, even lower-end graphics cards are being hit hard with price hikes.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
As one Redditor put it neatly (with the swearing removed): "A 5080 for an unboxing simulator. They are just laughing in our faces."
Another in that thread replies to say: "Ragebait? You are not able to afford a real graphics card — here, take this virtual one?"
Speaking of rage, there's quite an outpouring of it in the comments for Nvidia's YouTube video (the one embedded above), such as: "Great job, today consumers have no chance to be able to afford new high end gaming video cards in favor of greed and AI money. A 5090 is $10-15k, and a 5080 is $2k or more — it's a slap in the face to post this tbh."
Nvidia has a clear priority for AI, data centers and profits over consumers and gaming GPUs – and it's a business, that's where the money lies, we get that. Shareholders for-the-win and so forth, but given that, the thoughtlessness of this little PR nugget is pretty staggering really.
What sort of reaction did Nvidia expect it would get? Okay, there are some Redditors reminiscing about the good old days of 2006, and the 8800 GTX that they owned. However, many more are simply bitter (or indeed incandescent) that Nvidia appears to be reminding us of better times, having done a good deal to cause the GPU pricing pain which is now prevalent thanks to chasing AI profits. While asking for a high-end, now ridiculously expensive, Blackwell GPU to run the demo (at the recommended level).
The GeForce 8800 GTX was $599 as a top-end monster GPU when it arrived, and if you want an RTX 5090 these days, you'll pay over 15x that amount. I would think that Nvidia would want to do anything but take a nostalgic trip back to the days of relatively affordable high-end graphics cards at this point in time.
Maybe Team Green should have saved this one for the card's 25th anniversary. Will the RAM crisis be over by then?

articles.title: Nvidia bloquée en Chine : des puces s’accumulent à Hong Kong faute d’autorisation d’importation
articles.text:
Les puces NVIDIA sont les plus courues dans le domaine de l'intelligence artificielle. Mais pourtant en Chine, beaucoup dorment dans des entrepôts !
Pendant longtemps, avec les contraintes à l'exportation imposées par les États-Unis, tout le monde en Chine utilisait des canaux illégaux pour acquérir les meilleures puces NVIDIA - pendant que Pékin fermait plus ou moins les yeux. Mais depuis, en Chine, le pouvoir cherche de plus en plus à soutenir les spécialistes locaux, au point d'arriver même à des situations assez cocasses.
Près de 600 000 puces avancées de NVIDIA entreposées à Hong-Kong, dans l'attente d'une autorisaiton pour entrer en Chine
Qui aurait cru que des puces NVIDIA attendraient en masse à la frontière chinoise, espérant une autorisation des autorités ? C'est pourtant la situation actuelle, selon une information communiquée par Reuters.
Près de 600 000 puces sont ainsi entreposées à Hong-Kong, le passage de la frontière étant conditionné par des autorisation d'import de masse que Pékin est réticent à donner. Résultat, les puces H200, qui sont l'avant-dernière génération des puces NVIDIA, attendent - quand de l'autre côté, les géants chinois de l'IA auraient bien besoin de ces composants pour accroître leurs capacités de calcul.
La Chine pousse pour que ses entreprises locales fassent appel à des solutions locales
Toujours d'après la même source, la porte n'est pas complètement fermée. Plusieurs entreprises chinoises auraient ainsi obtenu les derniers mois l'autorisation du gouvernement d'importer 10 000 puces H200 chacune. Celles-ci font ainsi souvent appel à des intermédiaires, qui leur font payer des prix très forts pour des serveurs de H200, et pour les serveurs Blackwell qui réussissent à passer.
Du côté de Pékin, on essaye de mettre en balance les besoins immédiats des géants de la tech avec la volonté toujours plus affirmée de favoriser les alternatives locales, comme Huawei. Ainsi, si le gouvernement chinois a promis de débloquer des H200 à ses entreprises, il leur a aussi demandé de privilégier à l'avenir les options chinoises pour ce qui est de l'inférence dans les modèles IA.
Source : Reuters

articles.title: ThreatsDay: Apache OFBiz RCE, DreamHost Breach, DeFi Site Hijacks + 17 More Stories
articles.text:
How much damage can someone do without breaking much? Quite a lot, it seems. A stolen login can open doors across several systems. A trusted setting can be used to lock people out. Even a simple file copy can reach places it shouldn't. And while new tools are helping find security holes faster, some important systems are still taking months, sometimes over a year, to get patched. Not exactly a great match.
The stranger part is how little some attacks now need. Ransom demands without encrypted files. Fake websites that look real enough to steal money. AI tools picking up dangerous instructions while trying to help. Even the attackers are making mistakes in their own code.
This week's stories are a reminder that the biggest problems don't always come from clever tricks. Sometimes the easy way works just fine. Here's what else happened.
The threats change every week. Subscribe, and we’ll alert you when each new ThreatsDay Bulletin is out.
- 
  
  AI Accelerates Zero-Day Discovery The U.K. National Cyber Security Center (NCSC) has warned that the widespread availability of AI-powered cyber tools has "almost certainly" led to a significant increase in the discovery of zero-day vulnerabilities. "Defensive AI-cyber tools have reduced the window of a vulnerability moving from zero-day to an n-day vulnerability, and have made patching a quicker process," NCSC said. "However, without correct and widespread configuring of this technology, many systems are still vulnerable to attackers using AI-cyber tools to identify and exploit system weaknesses. Additionally, an organisation’s internal patching and testing processes will need to evolve to meet the pace of accelerating vulnerability discovery. Attackers have subsequently displayed less caution over losing an access to achieve an objective, as the cost to replace is minimal."
- 
  
  Critical Systems Face Prolonged Exposure An analysis of roughly 383,000 CVEs disclosed from 1999 through September 2026 has found that the median time to patch a vulnerability exceeds a year for network appliances. About 2,000 CVEs (roughly 0.5%) have been linked to real-world exploitation. "The median vulnerability is patched in about two weeks on Windows workstations but in more than a month on Windows Servers," Microsoft said. "It stretches to 10+ weeks on Linux Servers and for applications running on macOS, and beyond a year on network appliances. That gap is the threat actor's window, widest on the critical systems that stay exposed the longest." The tech giant also said threat actors disproportionately target flaws that maximize impact and exposure and enable system takeover, particularly remote code execution, privilege escalation, and authentication bypass.
- 
  
  $4.5 Million Fraud Network Busted Authorities have arrested seven people allegedly involved in an investment fraud scheme that claimed potential victims in more than 50 countries, according to Europol. The operation caused estimated losses of at least $4.5 million. The "crime-as-a-service" offering was run by a company from Cyprus and Israel, and allegedly provided cybercrime groups with an assortment of trading websites and fraudulent call centers tasked with tricking victims into transferring their savings. These call centers operated from Albania, Kosovo, and North Macedonia. "More than 100 servers were seized and seven suspects arrested during coordinated action on 3 November 2026," Europol said. "Authorities searched 17 locations and seized servers, other evidence and assets." Like other fraudulent investment schemes, the operation leveraged deceptive advertisements to funnel people towards fraudulent investment platforms, promising them substantial, quick returns from cryptocurrency trading and foreign currencies. Although victims were encouraged to transfer a small amount, they displayed illusory gains to push them into transferring increasingly large sums. The operators resorted to delaying tactics to block payments when they attempted to withdraw their funds. "Behind seemingly legitimate platforms, supposed brokers used fictitious profits and sustained psychological pressure to persuade victims to invest more," Europol said. "Personal data collected through this process was sold to criminal groups operating call centers. Operators then contacted potential victims with supposed investment opportunities, turning their initial interest into repeated demands for money."
- 
  
  $250K Bounty for Critical Cloud Flaws Google has expanded its Cloud Vulnerability Reward Program (VRP) with a new top-tier reward for high-impact architectural security flaws, allowing researchers to earn $250,000 for Root-in-Cloud bugs, including tenant-isolation bypasses and complex cross-service logic flaws that let attackers gain full administrative control over arbitrary Google Cloud organizations. "To earn this premier reward, you must demonstrate full administrative control, the equivalent of 'roles/owner' or complete IAM control, over arbitrary Google Cloud organizations or projects with no prior access or special project setup," Google said. "Additionally, valid vulnerability reports demonstrating remote code execution (RCE) in underlying Google production infrastructure (Borg) or achieving root-in-prod will automatically be evaluated by the Google Cloud VRP panel for root-in-cloud eligibility."
- 
  
  Edge Blocks Scam Notification Abuse Microsoft has announced that its Edge browser will now automatically disable notifications from sites that push scam or scareware notifications, such as fake virus warnings or security alerts. "As of last month’s rollout of Edge 156, when Microsoft Defender SmartScreen or Scareware blocker detects a scam that was pushed through a notification, Edge will automatically disable notifications from the site that sent it," Microsoft said. "The next time Edge starts, an information bar explains what happened. If you believe a site was blocked incorrectly, you can review sites with blocked notifications and unblock them from Edge Settings, keeping you in control."
- 
  
  University Cryptojacking Charges Two Canadian men, Ryan James Roach, 35, and Mathiew James Stubbings, 41, have been indicted in the U.S. for hacking multiple U.S. universities and using the access to mine cryptocurrency. Both have been charged with conspiracy to obtain information from a protected computer and to cause damage to a protected computer, obtaining information from a protected computer, and intentional damage to a protected computer, which carry a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison and a $250,000 fine. "Between June 2016, and December 2019, Roach and Stubbings conspired to engage in a scheme to hack into computers, steal login credentials, and secretly mine cryptocurrency for financial gain," the Justice Department said. "They used virtual private servers in multiple countries, which were registered under false names. These servers transmitted malware and mining software to victim computers and stored stolen login credentials. Victims of the scheme included educational institutions in New York, Tennessee, North Carolina, and Massachusetts."
- 
  
  Ransomware Extortion Without Encryption Cybersecurity researchers have detailed an encryptionless extortion attack involving PAYLOAD ransomware targeting a manufacturing organization in the Middle East. "The threat actor obtained domain admin-equivalent control of the organization’s Active Directory environment and authored a malicious Group Policy Object (GPO) named PAYLOAD, linking it at the domain root," Kaspersky said. "Through that single object, the actor delivered ransom notes, hijacked the desktop wallpaper and lock screen, enforced a logon banner, and disabled the local administrator account across every domain-joined Windows workstation — all without dropping a ransomware binary or encrypting any data. The only ransomware we found in this incident was a PAYLOAD sample targeting ESXi on Linux servers." The attack represents a convergence of two trends: Living-off-the-land abuse of trusted AD infrastructure and a surge in extortion-only incidents.
- 
  
  AI Sandbox Escape Exposes Sensitive Files A vulnerability impacting Docker Sandboxes (CVE-2026-103916) could have been exploited to bypass file access restrictions, potentially exposing cloud credentials and other sensitive files on a developer's machine through a routine copy command. "The command used to copy files between a sandbox and the developer's computer (sbx cp) does not enforce these access restrictions," Endor Labs said. "An agent can exploit this weakness using what is known as a symbolic link, essentially a shortcut that points to another file or folder. By placing a malicious shortcut inside an approved workspace, the agent can trick a subsequent copy command into accessing files outside the sandbox's approved boundaries." The issue has been addressed in Docker Sandboxes version 0.51.0.
- 
  
  Smart TVs Keep Tracking After Opt-OutDoes Opting Out of ACR Work? A new study has revealed that smart TVs running operating systems from Samsung, Vizio, and Roku continue to transmit data to automatic content recognition (ACR) endpoints even after users opt out of tracking in the devices' settings. "Opting out fully worked on only four operating systems. On Samsung and Vizio, traffic consistent with ACR kept flowing, and Roku's opt-out doesn't cover its own streaming service," according to a group of academics from Northeastern University. "VIDAA OS sends ACR data to servers run by Unruly over MQTT without encryption, so anyone on the network path between the TV and those servers can read it."
- 
  
  Cryptographic Proof for AI Outputs Anthropic has revealed that it's working on an open-source system called FlashProve to cryptographically verify an AI response came from a given model. "FlashProve is a system for provable inference of large Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language models," Anthropic said. "FlashProve involves two parties: the model provider (the prover) and a user (the verifier). It is split into two phases: In the offline phase, the prover publishes a commitment to the model weights, which is a short fingerprint to pin down one exact choice of weights while the weights themselves remain hidden. The later inference claims will be checked against that commitment, i.e., the weight model committed to in this phase. In the online phase, upon requests from the verifier (i.e., prompts and the corresponding output tokens), the prover produces a proof file proving the following statement: The committed model produces these output tokens when evaluated. Anyone who holds the commitment, the prompt, and the reply can check it, without the weights and with limited compute power, and be convinced that the committed weights, run on this prompt, produce exactly these tokens."
- 
  
  FTP and Webmail Credentials Exposed DreamHost has warned of a data breach after an unauthorized third party gained access to the server that runs its web-based File Manager at files.dreamhost.com between August and October 23, 2026. "The unauthorized third party exploited a vulnerability in that software and was able to access the FTP/SFTP usernames and passwords of individuals who logged into this File Manager between approximately August 2026 and October 23, 2026," the company said. "The unauthorized third party was also able to reach certain webmail systems, which may have exposed the session information (the data that keeps a user signed in, including session credentials) of a limited number of webmail users. We believe this was a deliberate attack, and our team worked around the clock to contain it." DreamHost said the attacker may have accessed the credentials used to access the File Manager or webmail, along with the contents of emails and files in the FTP/SFTP server. There is no evidence that the attacker accessed control panel login information or customer billing details.
- 
  
  Pre-Auth RCE and Account Takeover The maintainers of Apache OFBiz have addressed 46 security flaws, including CVE-2026-68524, which could result in pre-authentication remote code execution, and CVE-2026-109928, which enables full account takeover due to an incorrect authentication algorithm implementation. The issues have been patched in Apache OFBiz 24.09.08.
- 
  
  Ransomware Encryption Flaws Exposed Cybersecurity researchers have uncovered encryption weaknesses in the updated HYFLOCK ransomware builds. The ransomware operation began to publicly name victims in October 2026, although evidence indicates that the group first appeared in underground forums in March 2026. As of writing, the group has listed 13 victims. "The October 17 build successfully encrypted files, registered a scheduled task, accessed network-share resources, and attempted to interfere with system recovery," Check Point said. "In an earlier October version, researchers identified a processing defect that could permanently discard portions of a file, potentially preventing complete recovery even with the correct decryption key. The October 17 build exhibited another issue. Larger files had only their first 4,096 bytes encrypted, leaving additional content accessible beyond that initial section."
- 
  
  Customer Identity Data Accessed DigiCert said it has identified an event involving unauthorized access to one of its business systems that stores information shared by customer representatives to validate their identity. The company said its certificate operations were not impacted. "Most of the data was limited to business contact information for customers: names, business email addresses, phone numbers, and business addresses," DigiCert said. "A small minority of customer accounts included additional personal data in the form of a customer-provided document such as a driver's license, passport, utility bill, or other document with name and address. The access could not write records, act as a validation approver, or issue certificates."
- 
  
  DeFi Hijack Drains $138K Threat actors have hijacked a little over a dozen DeFi websites registered with Name.com, including Flap, Kintsu, Pickle Finance and Origami Finance, ultimately stealing about $138,000 in assets. The sites have been found to be rigged with a malware kit that tricks visitors into approving transfers out of their wallets once they connect them to the compromised site. Vercel said it's aware of nine domains associated with the platform that were impacted. "Over about 45 minutes on Oct 31 (UTC), an account within an associated support team made changes to the nameservers associated with 15 domains registered with name.com," Name.com said in a post-mortem. "The domains were directed to a malicious page hosting Step Drainer malware."
- 
  
  Stolen Cloud App Credentials Abused Todyl has disclosed that an unknown threat actor has been abusing stolen Microsoft Entra ID application credentials and Azure DevOps identities to access MSPs' Microsoft 365 and Azure environments, reaching at least 27 organizations. "About 45 app registrations at roughly 18 organizations were targeted, and more than 33 of them authenticated successfully," Todyl said. "Through those apps the actor has reached 27 organizations so far, including the MSPs' downstream clients in government, energy, food and agriculture, transportation, construction and engineering, legal, education and nonprofits. It has run searches across about 25 tenants, downloaded 81 files and accessed around 2,279 mailbox items." The sign-in activity has originated from the IP address 199.19.77[.]84.
- 
  
  Syrian Hacker Gets 42 Months Ahmad Umar Agha (aka Th3Pr0), a Syrian national tied to the Syrian Electronic Army (SEA), has been sentenced to 42 months in prison in the U.S. for his involvement in an expansive hacking conspiracy organized and led by members of former Syrian President Bashar Al-Assad regime between Aug 2011 and January 2014. "To spread the former Syrian government's propaganda, Agha hacked approximately 47 Western media entities, businesses, non-governmental organizations (NGOs), and U.S. and allied government entities," the Justice Department said. "In one instance, Agha’s actions caused a flash crash in the U.S. stock market, resulting in a temporary $136 billion loss in the value of stocks making up the Dow Jones Industrial Average." Agha and his alleged accomplice, Firas Dardar, were first charged in June 2014. Dardar remains at large.
- 
  
  Malicious AI Search Results Steal Crypto A new piece of malware has been observed targeting AI agents creating cryptocurrency wallets. "A GitHub repository posing as a Solana starter kit, which ranks as the top result when an agent searches for one, contains malware that gives an attacker remote control of the victim's machine, including the crypto wallets on it," AIR Security said. The activity has been codenamed SolanaCry. The attack builds upon the foundation of Web Hole, where an AI agent, in its quest for finding answers to a problem, can inadvertently run a command suggested by an attacker and perform malicious actions. "To get a payload into search results, an attacker has two options," AIR said. "The first is to build a site of their own and grow its reputation with SEO, backlinks, content, time, until the search engine treats it as relevant and trusted. Once it ranks, they change the content and drop in the payload. The second is easier: find dead sites that still show up as ranked results, and use those to deliver it."
- 
  
  Android Banking Malware Spreads Thousands of Android phones belonging to retail banking customers in the Middle East, Turkey, and Africa (META) region have been compromised with the Mirax trojan between March and September 2026, leading to estimated losses worth millions of U.S. dollars. "Where unauthorized international transfers were reported, funds were sent to accounts abroad, some of which are suspected to be mule accounts," Group-IB said. "The campaign uses dynamically generated package names and impersonates 'Google Play Services' to evade user suspicion and signature-based detection." Like most Android malware, Mirax is used to facilitate device takeover (DTO) fraud by abusing Android's accessibility services. "With it, the attacker is able to see and control the compromised device in real time: reading credentials, intercepting one-time codes, capturing the PIN to unlock the device later, opening a banking app and moving money out to newly added beneficiaries and mule accounts abroad," Group-IB said. Campaigns using Mirax have been attributed to Aquafina, a threat actor known to be active since March 16, 2026.
- 
  
  AI Model Bypasses Task Instructions Irregular's evaluation of Zhipu AI's open-weight model GLM-5.3 across 13 offensive cyber scenarios using CyScenarioBench has found that the model "did not refuse any of the tested offensive tasks" and "repeatedly reached correct answers while violating explicit task instructions." The AI security company said these violations can be interpreted as a form of reward hacking. "Crediting the answer alone could mislead capability assessments and deployment decisions, while rewarding it during training could reinforce these instruction violations," it added.
One thing stands out this week: attackers don't always need to be smarter than the systems they're targeting. They just need to find what was missed, left open, or trusted a little too much. And with AI making some of that searching easier, the time between finding a problem and using it is getting shorter. Patching still matters, but so does checking whether the controls already in place actually work.
That's it for this week. Some of these problems have fixes. Others need a closer look at how people, tools, and systems are allowed to work together. The next big headache may not come from a new bug at all. It could be something that's been sitting there for years, waiting for someone to notice. See you next week.

articles.title: Aprende a programar mensajes en WhatsApp con hora y fecha de envío
articles.text:
WhatsApp comenzó a desplegar una de las funciones más esperadas por sus usuarios: la posibilidad de programar mensajes para que se envíen automáticamente en una fecha y hora determinadas. La herramienta permite dejar preparada una comunicación sin necesidad de estar pendiente del teléfono o de utilizar aplicaciones externas para concretar el envío.
La novedad resulta útil para distintas situaciones cotidianas, como enviar un saludo de cumpleaños a medianoche, recordar una reunión, coordinar una actividad o responder un mensaje laboral fuera del horario de oficina sin interrumpir el descanso de otra persona.
La función está llegando de manera progresiva y algunos usuarios ya pueden utilizarla, especialmente quienes participan en las versiones beta de WhatsApp para Android y iPhone. Aunque Meta, propietaria de la aplicación, todavía no ha realizado un anuncio oficial sobre su disponibilidad general, los primeros despliegues permiten conocer cómo funciona.
Una de sus principales ventajas es que el destinatario recibe el mensaje como cualquier otra comunicación. Es decir, no aparece una etiqueta que indique que fue programado ni una notificación especial que revele que el remitente lo escribió con anticipación.
Cómo programar mensajes de WhatsApp desde el celular
La herramienta permite establecer una fecha y una hora para enviar un mensaje desde dispositivos Android y iPhone. El procedimiento se realiza directamente dentro de la conversación y no requiere instalar programas adicionales.
Para utilizarla, es necesario seguir estos pasos:
- Abrir WhatsApp e ingresar al chat individual o grupal al que se desea enviar el mensaje.
- Escribir el texto que se quiere compartir. También se pueden adjuntar fotografías o archivos, según las opciones disponibles en la versión de la aplicación.
- Mantener presionado el botón verde de envío, en lugar de tocarlo una sola vez.
- Esperar a que aparezca el menú de programación con las opciones de calendario y horario.
- Seleccionar la fecha y la hora exactas en las que se desea enviar el contenido.
- Confirmar la programación para que el mensaje quede agendado.
Una vez completado el procedimiento, WhatsApp se encarga de realizar el envío automáticamente cuando llegue el momento elegido. De esta manera, el usuario no necesita abrir nuevamente la conversación ni recordar que tiene una comunicación pendiente.
La función puede utilizarse para organizar mensajes personales y laborales, especialmente cuando se necesita contactar a alguien en un horario específico.
Cómo programar mensajes desde WhatsApp Web
La programación también contempla a quienes utilizan WhatsApp desde una computadora mediante la versión para navegadores. Esto permite preparar comunicaciones mientras se trabaja, sin tener que recurrir al celular.
El procedimiento es sencillo:
- Ingresar a WhatsApp Web desde el navegador y abrir la conversación correspondiente.
- Escribir el mensaje en el campo de texto habitual.
- Identificar el ícono de reloj ubicado junto al botón de envío.
- Hacer clic para desplegar la ventana de programación.
- Elegir la fecha y la hora en las que se enviará el mensaje.
- Confirmar la operación para dejarlo agendado.
Esta alternativa resulta práctica para quienes utilizan WhatsApp como herramienta de trabajo y necesitan organizar comunicaciones con clientes, compañeros o proveedores.
¿El destinatario sabe que el mensaje fue programado?
Una de las dudas que puede surgir con esta actualización es si la persona que recibe el mensaje puede identificar que fue escrito con anticipación.
La respuesta es no. Según el funcionamiento reportado de la herramienta, el destinatario recibe la comunicación de la misma manera que cualquier mensaje enviado en tiempo real. No aparece una advertencia que indique que fue programado ni una marca especial que permita distinguirlo.
Esto significa que la función está pensada para facilitar la organización del remitente sin modificar la experiencia de quien recibe el contenido.
Para qué sirve programar mensajes en WhatsApp
Además de los cumpleaños y recordatorios, esta herramienta puede ayudar a mejorar la convivencia digital. Por ejemplo, una persona puede redactar una comunicación laboral durante la noche y programarla para que llegue al inicio de la jornada siguiente.
De esta manera, evita interrumpir los horarios de descanso de sus contactos y mantiene una mejor organización de sus conversaciones.
También es recomendable aprovechar la programación para enviar mensajes completos, con toda la información necesaria. En lugar de dejar un saludo aislado como “Hola” para iniciar una conversación, conviene incluir directamente la consulta o el pedido.
Así, el destinatario puede comprender el motivo del contacto cuando reciba la notificación, sin necesidad de esperar un segundo mensaje para conocer el propósito de la comunicación.
Por ahora, la disponibilidad de esta característica depende del despliegue progresivo de WhatsApp. Por eso, quienes todavía no encuentren las opciones de calendario y horario deberán esperar a que la actualización llegue a su cuenta.

articles.title: Etsy is finally cracking down on AI in product listings
articles.text:
‘Every listing must include at least one photo of the actual item’: Etsy is finally cracking down on AI images and text in listings — and apparently this is just the start
Etsy is finally cracking down on misleading listings
- Etsy has updated its Seller Handbook to include new guidance on how AI can be used
- Products must include at least one unaltered listing image that shows the actual product
- AI can still be used for some purposes, but misleading images will hopefully start to disappear
In the wake of Just Eat’s AI generated food image fiasco, Etsy has decided to update its policies to prevent AI being used to generate or edit images, create guides, or use bots to generate listings.
The new guidelines, enacted in October, are part of an effort to crack down on images, recipes, and instructions that have been partially or fully AI generated that could mislead customers — and it could help cut down on the torrents of AI slop that have infiltrated the internet.
“You, our seller community, have told us you’re concerned about your work appearing alongside items that use AI in misleading ways, and that it’s becoming harder for buyers to recognize your role in creating your items,” the announcement states. “We're taking an important first step to address these challenges.”
Etsy changes AI usage rules
The steps Etsy is taking include changes to how products are physically presented in images, how AI can be used to edit images, and how functional guides are written.
For a start, Etsy now requires at least one of the listing images to be a real photo of the actual item being sold with on a real background without any edits or alterations made. But this image doesn’t have to be the first image potential customers will see when viewing your listing.
But if you’re wondering about non-physical purchases — such as artwork printed by a third-party — Etsy will allow unedited mock ups from manufacturers for print-on-demand services to be used as the ‘real’ product photo. As for audio and digital downloads, Etsy says the imagery cannot mislead customers.
Don’t worry, AI editing is still allowed in some circumstances such as to change lighting and exposure or to resize an image. Backgrounds can also be AI generated as long as the actual product isn’t changed in any way, but using AI to alter the actual product by changing colors, condition, or features of an item is now a hard no in Etsy’s books.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Finally, when it comes to other products commonly listed for crafters or cooks, Etsy is changing how they can be written. Written work for instructions, patterns and recipes have to be fully written by the seller with an image representing the real results. So for a knitting pattern or bread recipe, the image must show the finished product.
To enforce better detection of AI generated or misleading content, Etsy says it is “investing in tools to better identify authentic versus misleading images and detect and remove listings that use AI to create fraudulent inventory.”
The platform is also expanding categories to include misleading AI imagery when reporting listings, which will be used to “help us better understand how members perceive potential AI misuse.”
If you are currently using AI generated images for products on Etsy, you still have some time to update listings and won’t face immediate enforcement. The company says it will “provide tips to help you accurately represent your items and meet our photo expectations,” with guidance also provided to sellers with existing AI edited listings.

articles.title: Meta supprime un tiers de ses effectifs en France : ce que prévoit le plan de départs
articles.text:
Meta s’apprête à réduire sensiblement ses effectifs dans l’Hexagone. Le groupe de Mark Zuckerberg prépare pour cela un plan de départs volontaires qui pourrait concerner jusqu’à une centaine de salariés (sur les 300 que compte sa filiale française).
La course à l’intelligence artificielle chez Meta a visiblement un coût bien humain. Selon les informations rapportées par La Lettre, Meta préparerait une importante restructuration en France, sous la forme d’une rupture conventionnelle collective négociée depuis cet été. Un dispositif qui doit permettre aux salariés volontaires de quitter l’entreprise dans des conditions financières bien définies.
Jusqu’à 100 départs volontaires, avec des conditions financières bien précises
Concrètement, Meta France compte actuellement environ 300 salariés. Le plan envisagé pourrait concerner jusqu’à une centaine de postes, soit près d’un tiers des effectifs français. Attention toutefois, il ne s’agit pas d'un plan de licenciements secs, mais bien d’une rupture conventionnelle collective, qui repose sur le volontariat, et qui doit faire l’objet d'un accord avec les représentants du personnel.
Pour convaincre les candidats au départ, Meta proposerait une indemnité équivalente à 2,15 mois de salaire par année d’ancienneté. À cela s’ajouterait un congé de mobilité de dix mois, rémunéré à hauteur de 80% du salaire brut.
Ce n’est pas une première pour la filiale française puisqu’en 2023, lors d’une précédente rupture conventionnelle collective, 88 salariés avaient déjà quitté l’entreprise. Le nombre de salariés prêts à accepter cette nouvelle proposition n'est pas encore connu.
L’IA au cœur des ambitions de Zuckerberg… mais aussi des restructurations
Cette réduction des effectifs français s’inscrit dans un mouvement beaucoup plus large chez Meta. Fin août, le groupe avait annoncé un plan mondial concernant 8 000 salariés, soit environ 10% de ses effectifs. Le géant américain avait même initialement envisagé une réduction pouvant atteindre 60% de son personnel.
Depuis plusieurs mois, Mark Zuckerberg réorganise profondément son entreprise, avec une volonté affichée de réduire les niveaux hiérarchiques et d’améliorer la productivité.
C’est évidemment l’intelligence artificielle qui occupe désormais une place centrale dans cette stratégie, avec des investissements colossaux dans les infrastructures et les nouveaux modèles.
Comme nous l’évoquions récemment sur Clubic, Meta cherche notamment à lever jusqu’à 97,5 milliards de dollars pour financer ses ambitions dans l’IA. Une opération financière d’une ampleur plus que considérable, alors que Zuckerberg entend également préserver son contrôle sur le groupe, malgré une participation minoritaire au capital.
Meta promet ainsi un avenir professionnel transformé par l’IA, et tant pis si cette transition s’accompagne, dans l’immédiat en tout cas, d’une réduction de ses effectifs.

articles.title: Is Your Exposure Management Platform Leaving You Exposed? Five Tests to Find Out
articles.text:
A critical finding can move through several security tools and still leave the organization exposed.
The vulnerability has a severity score, and a ticket has reached the queue. Progress then depends on information the finding may lack: who owns the system, whether attackers can reach it, what protection exists, and how a change could affect the business.
Each missing detail creates another investigation, another handoff, and another delay.
An exposure management platform should connect discovery with a clear priority, an appropriate response, and evidence that protection has improved.
Continuous threat exposure management (CTEM) connects this work through scoping, discovery, prioritization, validation, and mobilization. These five tests establish whether a platform can support that process across infrastructure, identities, sensitive data, and external threats.
Security teams often have several records of the same asset. A cloud platform identifies an instance, an endpoint tool records its hostname, and an inventory lists an owner who has changed roles.
Cyber asset attack surface management (CAASM) connects those records, helping reveal stale information, missing ownership, and protection gaps.
The resulting view needs enough detail to support action: the asset’s owner, business purpose, assessment history, and security coverage. A system with no reported vulnerabilities should be distinguishable from one never assessed.
Disagreements between sources also need to remain visible. If an endpoint tool reports an active server while the inventory marks it retired, source records and update times help teams resolve the conflict.
| Figure 1. CAASM connects source records with asset ownership, security coverage, and exposure context. | 
External discovery adds another perspective. External attack surface management (EASM) helps uncover what assets make accessible from the outside, including shadow IT, forgotten subdomains, and exposed services that internal tools never see.
EASM and CAASM work best together: CAASM maps what you know you own, while EASM validates that picture from the attacker’s point of view and surfaces what’s missing. Every unmanaged asset EASM finds can be fed back into CAASM, closing coverage gaps and giving each asset an owner. EASM also covers brand exposure, extending discovery to phishing sites, fraudulent profiles, and brand impersonation, so the same external view that finds your unknown assets also finds the lookalikes attackers build to target your customers and employees.
Read CAASM Was Never Meant to Stand Alone to see how asset intelligence supports the decisions and actions that follow discovery.
2. Explain Which Exposures Require Action First
Prioritization depends on understanding what an exposure actually puts at risk. A customer-facing application may carry the same severity score as an isolated development system while presenting very different business risk.
Prioritization should connect:
- Reachability and exploitability: Whether attackers have a usable path to exploit the weakness.
- Threat activity: Whether attackers are targeting the vulnerability or technology.
- Business impact: What the system supports and what compromise could affect.
- Existing protection: Whether relevant controls cover the system and are enforced.
Those conditions change. New exploitation activity may accelerate a response, while a disabled protection may invalidate an earlier assessment.
External threats need similarly specific reasoning. A fraudulent support account approaching customers may require rapid disruption; an abandoned company profile may first need ownership review.
See what the 2026 Exposure Gap Report reveals about prioritization and remediation performance.
3. Validate the Exposure and the Proposed Response
A clear priority can still stall when the system owner lacks confidence in the proposed change.
Validation needs to establish what the exposure allows and how the response could affect operations.
Identifying vulnerable software, confirming reachability, and demonstrating exploitability establish different things. A platform should distinguish observed evidence from analysis and untested assumptions. Attack-path relationships also need supporting evidence and clear limitations.
The proposed response requires separate assessment. A patch may depend on application testing and a maintenance window. An intrusion prevention system protection may require observation in Detect mode before enforcement.
Evidence should address the action’s scope, dependencies, false positives, performance impact, and recovery options. Following a proposed change through this assessment reveals what the platform establishes and what teams must investigate themselves.
4. Carry Safe Remediation Through Existing Workflows
Knowing what to fix first is great, but only if the fix happens quickly. The permanent patch often waits on testing, approval, and a maintenance window, and the exposure stays open the whole time. That’s true whether the weakness is on an internet-facing server or a phishing site targeting your customers.
Speed comes from confidence. Teams hesitate when they can’t say what an action will touch. When the platform already knows the asset, its owner, the active threat, and the controls in place, that hesitation disappears. Many Check Point Exposure Management customers remediate safely within one hour, because the context is complete and the safety checks are built in.
To test this, take one real finding and follow it from priority to protection:
- Owner: Is the right person assigned automatically?
- Safety: Is the action validated before it runs, including its impact and a way back?
- Execution: Does it run through the controls you already have, whether a virtual patch, a configuration change, or a takedown?
- Confirmation: Is the result verified, with the permanent fix still tracked?
Interim protection buys time, but it shouldn’t replace the long term fix.
| Figure 2. Safe remediation connects observation, validation, action, and confirmation. | 
Speed holds up at scale. Between January 1 and October 26, 2026, an airline group completed more than 1,500 takedowns of profiles impersonating its airlines and support teams, combining analyst review with automated remediation.
And when an action fails, the exposure should stay visible with a clear next step.
Read Safe Remediation: Confident Remediation in Production to see how validation, execution, and confirmation work together.
5. Show What Changed and What Remains
A completed action needs evidence of the resulting state.
A patch may miss unavailable systems. A policy update may exclude an intended asset. A takedown request may be accepted before the account disappears.
Verification should establish whether the vulnerability remains, protection is enforced, or malicious content has been removed. Monitoring should identify recurrence.
Reporting must distinguish removed vulnerabilities, interim mitigations, completed takedowns, and accepted risk. Each leaves different responsibilities outstanding.
Mean time to remediate (MTTR) requires agreed starting points, completion criteria, and treatment of temporary protection.
Tracking assignment, approval, execution, and verification separately reveals delays.
Recurring findings, failed actions, and aging mitigations can expose operational problems another scan will not resolve.
Apply the Tests Across Vendors
Platforms approach these requirements from different foundations. The five tests provide a consistent basis for evaluating coverage, evidence, and action.
Check Point Exposure Management combines internal asset intelligence, external discovery, threat intelligence, and brand protection with prioritization, exploitability validation, and safe remediation. It spans infrastructure weaknesses, phishing, and brand impersonation, supporting action through existing controls and takedown workflows.
Bring Intelligence Through to Safe Action
The five tests follow an exposure from discovery to a confirmed response. Each stage should give the next team enough reliable information to act while keeping unresolved work visible.
Check Point Exposure Management carries asset and threat context into responses to vulnerabilities, control gaps, and external threats. Proposed actions are evaluated before enforcement, with approved responses coordinated through supported Check Point and third-party technologies.
That connection helps organizations strengthen protection while accounting for production constraints and building on existing investments. It creates a traceable path from an identified exposure to an evaluated, implemented, and confirmed response.

articles.title: Rockstar está bloqueando cuentas de fanáticos de GTA 6: subir spoilers es un riesgo
articles.text:
Rockstar Games confirmó que retirará videos con contenido de la trama de Grand Theft Auto VI que se compartan en redes sociales, incluso después de que el juego llegue a las tiendas. La medida busca frenar la filtración de finales, giros narrativos y escenas clave antes de que los propios jugadores puedan descubrirlos por su cuenta.
La decisión forma parte de la política de publicación de materiales con derechos de autor de la compañía, actualizada por última vez en enero de 2025. No se trata de una norma creada en exclusiva para GTA VI, sino de un reglamento general que ya aplicaba a títulos como GTA V y Red Dead Redemption 2, aunque su aplicación cobra un peso diferente de cara al estreno del próximo juego de mundo abierto.
Qué contenido queda prohibido publicar sobre GTA 6
La política distingue entre gameplays extensos y clips aislados centrados en la narrativa. Según el documento, están permitidas las partidas completas, los videos tipo Let’s Play narrados y los análisis que incluyan escenas dentro de un contexto más amplio.
El problema surge cuando el material se publica de forma independiente. La compañía detalla textualmente que no se permite “publicar videos que muestren el final del juego, una combinación editada de escenas cinemáticas y/o diálogos de la trama del juego, o cualquier otra revelación importante en la historia”.
Rockstar Games aclara además que “está bien mostrar escenas cinemáticas como parte de una partida más larga (o en un video tipo ‘Let’s Play’ narrado), pero los videos aislados de las cinemáticas del juego serán eliminados”.
¿Qué pasa si alguien sube un clip con el final de GTA VI? Según la política oficial de Rockstar, ese contenido puede ser eliminado sin importar si el juego ya está a la venta, porque la norma no fija una fecha límite a partir de la cual los spoilers dejen de considerarse una infracción.
Filtraciones previas y “unboxing” anticipado
El reglamento también cubre el material que circule antes del lanzamiento oficial, fijado para el 19 de noviembre de 2026. La compañía advierte que “no se permite ningún tipo de material filtrado antes del lanzamiento” y que cualquier publicación proveniente de copias filtradas será retirada “independientemente de cómo se haya obtenido el juego”.
Esto incluye de forma expresa los videos de “unboxing anticipado”, es decir, aquellos que muestran el juego o su empaque antes de la fecha de venta. La medida responde en parte a los antecedentes recientes de GTA VI, que ya atravesó filtraciones de imágenes de gameplay no autorizadas y que, según un representante de la compañía, resultaron “desgarradoras” para el equipo de desarrollo.
Entretenimiento interno y el “truco de Nueva Zelanda”
Otro punto de la política apunta al llamado entretenimiento dentro del juego: programas de televisión, actuaciones de comedia propias de la saga Grand Theft Auto o las películas mudas de Red Dead Redemption. La compañía señala que prefiere que los fans disfruten de ese material “en el contexto del mundo del juego”, por lo que si se publica de forma aislada será marcado para su eliminación.
La norma también pone en la mira a quienes intenten adelantarse al lanzamiento global mediante el conocido “truco de Nueva Zelanda”, que consiste en cambiar la región de la consola para acceder antes al juego aprovechando el horario de ese país. Rockstar no contempla excepciones para quienes jueguen de forma anticipada por esta vía: si el material que comparten contiene spoilers, puede ser retirado igual que cualquier otro.
Sanciones contra trampas en el futuro multijugador
La política no se limita a los spoilers narrativos. Take-Two Interactive, editora de la saga, también prohíbe los contenidos que fomenten trampas o abusos técnicos, una restricción pensada de cara al modo multijugador de GTA VI. Entre los ejemplos mencionados figuran la obtención ilegítima de puntos de experiencia o dinero, la duplicación de objetos, la venta o regalo de cuentas y el aprovechamiento de fallos técnicos o exploits.

articles.title: AmneziaVPN's latest update rolls out location sorting to streamline server selection alongside several technical improvements — here's what you need to know
articles.text:
AmneziaVPN's latest update rolls out location sorting to streamline server selection alongside several technical improvements — here's what you need to know
- AmneziaVPN's latest update adds location sorting, favorites, and a browser proxy for desktop
- At a more technical level, the update brings log separation, server patching, and design tweaks
- Roadmap hints at seamless location switching and domain-based split tunneling
Amnezia VPN version 5.1.0.6 is now available, bringing location sorting to the forefront of its Premium service. For users comparing it against the best VPN options, this update addresses one of the most frequent user requests as the number of available server locations continues to grow.
With over 50 Premium locations now active, the previous flat list had become difficult to navigate. The new version introduces filtering options that let users organize countries by geographic region or alphabetically.
Navigation features
The latest update places a “Filters” button to the right of the search field, offering two organization modes.
Users can group countries by world region – with alphabetical ordering within each section – or maintain a single alphabetical list spanning all locations. A search bar enables quick lookup by country name.
Users may also mark up to 15 frequently used locations as favorites by tapping a star icon. This feature works across both the main location screen and the Config Files section.
However, favorites are stored locally on each device and tied to the subscription key. This means favorite selections made on a phone will not sync to a desktop computer, though the settings persist through app updates and device restarts.
Browser proxy for desktop users
Amnezia has also introduced a local proxy option for Premium subscribers using Windows, macOS, or Linux. The Xray proxy runs at 127.0.0.1 on port 10808 by default, routing browser traffic through Premium servers without establishing a full system-wide VPN tunnel.
The feature requires the CensorTracker browser extension to function. It operates for a single subscription at a time and automatically stops when the main VPN connection activates. This suits users seeking selective browser routing without affecting other applications on their machine.
Additional improvements
The update also separates app logs from tunnel logs, giving users clearer visibility before sending diagnostic data to support.
Connection handling for Self-hosted servers using XHTTP and XMUX protocols has been refined, alongside fixes for mobile operator connectivity.
The Switzerland P2P location now supports bidirectional traffic, with Universal Plug and Play (UPnP) protocols enabled there – handy for hosting game servers, for example. Self-hosted users also gain a one-click button for updating server packages, and some interface tweaks lay groundwork for a redesign due in the next release.
What comes next
Users can check for updates within the app under Settings > About Amnezia VPN. Desktop installations apply the update automatically, while mobile users can download from the App Store or Google Play.
Looking ahead, Amnezia has outlined several planned improvements. These include seamless location switching without disconnection, domain-based split tunneling for desktop users, better stability when managing large domain lists, and more transparent Self-hosted server management.
As internet restrictions evolve around the world, tools like Amnezia VPN continue iterating to remain effective. This update signals a focus on usability alongside security – a balance that’s particularly important for users relying on these services for daily access to information.

articles.title: 11.11 d’AliExpress : la Garmin Forerunner 255 tombe à 228,93€
articles.text:
Lancée en 2022 à 349,99 €, la montre de running de Garmin a depuis vu arriver la Forerunner 265, puis la 570 lancée à 549,99 €. Pour le 11.11, la Garmin Forerunner 255 descend à 228,93 € sur AliExpress avec le code CLU13 : GPS multibande et suivi de la récupération sont au rendez-vous, mais la fiche du vendeur mérite d’être lue de près.
Présentée par Garmin en juin 2022, la Forerunner 255 est une montre GPS pensée pour la course à pied et le triathlon, avec un boîtier de 46 mm et un écran couleur de 1,3 pouce. Elle est proposée à 228,93 € au lieu de 279,83 € sur AliExpress avec le code CLU13, soit 50,90 € d’économie et plus de 120 € sous son prix de lancement. Elle vise les coureurs qui veulent un plan d’entraînement et des indicateurs de récupération sans payer le prix des modèles récents. Si vous attendez surtout de la musique au poignet ou un écran tactile, la suite vous aidera à trancher.
La Garmin Forerunner 255 passe à 228,93 € au lieu de 279,83 € sur AliExpress, avec le code CLU13 à saisir au moment de payer.
Pourquoi choisir la Garmin Forerunner 255 ?
- Un entraînement qui s’adapte : Le widget de course propose des séances quotidiennes calées sur la date de votre objectif, et Garmin Coach accompagne la préparation d’un 5 km, d’un 10 km ou d’un semi-marathon.
- Une récupération mesurée : Le statut VFC suit la variabilité de votre fréquence cardiaque pendant le sommeil, et le rapport matinal résume chaque jour votre nuit, la météo et la séance suggérée.
- Un GPS pour les parcours exigeants : Le mode multibande améliore la précision là où le signal se dégrade, avec jusqu’à 16 heures d’autonomie dans ce mode et 30 heures en GPS seul.
Du 10 km au premier triathlon, une montre qui guide les séances
Au quotidien, la Forerunner 255 joue le rôle de coach : programmez une course dans Garmin Connect et la montre vous propose chaque jour une séance adaptée, avec une prévision de performance et la météo du jour J. PacePro calcule la stratégie d’allure selon le dénivelé du parcours, ce qui évite de partir trop vite sur un marathon vallonné. Le profil triathlon enchaîne natation, vélo et course d’une seule pression sur un bouton, et l’étanchéité 5 ATM, soit 50 mètres, couvre la piscine comme l’eau libre.
Elle convient aux coureurs réguliers qui visent un chrono et aux triathlètes débutants, attentifs à leur récupération autant qu’à leurs allures. Les 14 jours d’autonomie en mode montre connectée espacent les recharges, et Garmin Pay permet de payer depuis le poignet. Elle est moins pertinente pour écouter de la musique sans smartphone : chez Garmin, le stockage d’environ 500 morceaux et le Wi-Fi sont réservés à la version Music, alors que la fiche AliExpress mentionne 4 Go et le Wi-Fi. Vérifiez donc la référence exacte avant de commander.
Face aux Forerunner 165 et 570, une place à part dans la gamme
Dans notre test de la Forerunner 570, nous rappelions que la Forerunner 165, pensée pour les débutants, se passe de GPS double fréquence, tandis que la 570 a été lancée à 549,99 €. À 228,93 €, la Forerunner 255 conserve le GPS multibande, le profil triathlon et les mesures Firstbeat, comme la VO2 max et la charge d’entraînement, pour moins de la moitié de ce prix. En contrepartie, elle appartient à la génération 2022, que Garmin a renouvelée depuis. Pour élargir la comparaison à d’autres marques, notre comparatif des meilleures montres connectées pour le sport passe en revue les alternatives du moment.
✅ Les points forts
- Des séances proposées selon votre objectif de course

- Pas de musique embarquée sur la version standard

- Génération 2022, la gamme a été renouvelée depuis
Pour le 11.11, la Forerunner 255 s’affiche à 228,93 € avec le code CLU13 : un détour par la fiche permet de confirmer la version proposée.
À 228,93 €, la Garmin Forerunner 255 réunit l’essentiel de ce qu’un coureur attend d’une montre d’entraînement : des séances proposées selon votre objectif, un suivi sérieux de la récupération et un GPS multibande. Elle convient particulièrement à celles et ceux qui préparent un 10 km, un semi ou un premier triathlon et veulent progresser avec méthode. La remise de 50,90 € sur le prix barré compte moins que l’écart avec la Forerunner 570, lancée à plus du double.
Si vous tenez à la musique au poignet, à un écran tactile ou aux dernières nouveautés de Garmin, mieux vaut regarder ailleurs. La description mélangeant deux versions, lisez les avis sur le vendeur et les conditions de garantie avant de valider le panier. Cette vérification faite, la Forerunner 255 offre une base solide pour structurer vos entraînements cet hiver.
