articles.title: Why Magnetic Sensor Selection Has Become a System Architecture Decision - EE Times
articles.text:
Kiloampere busbars, 2,000 V solar platforms, hollow-shaft robot joints and nanoamp standby budgets are pulling magnetic sensing in directions no single sensing principle can follow.
Ask a traction inverter designer, a robotics engineer and someone building a battery-powered water meter what they need from a magnetic sensor, and you will get three answers with very little overlap.
The inverter designer is measuring current across an enormous range, from a few amperes in control circuits to several hundred amperes or more in the traction inverter and battery main circuit, carried on busbars that will never pass through a PCB. A colleague on the photovoltaic and storage side faces a twist on the same problem: those platforms are moving toward 2,000 V, so the sensor package itself now has to provide the creepage and clearance that used to belong to a separate module. The robotics engineer wants encoder resolution approaching optical performance, but the center of the joint is reserved for cables, so the sensor has to work off-axis. And the meter designer mostly cares about one figure: how much current the sensor draws while it waits, because that decides how many years the battery lasts.
These are all magnetic sensing problems, and they do not share a best answer. Hall, AMR, TMR, inductive and fluxgate techniques each have a regime where they are the right physics and others where they are a compromise. That turns sensor selection into an architecture decision, weighed against power budget, field strength, accuracy, interference, mechanical integration, isolation and cost all at once. It also means the range of technology a supplier can draw on starts to matter as much as any single datasheet.
NOVOSENSE has built its magnetic sensor business on that premise, covering all five principles across current, angle, position, speed and switch functions. Yole Group ranks the company fourth globally by magnetic sensor shipment volume and first among Chinese suppliers. Shipments exceeded one billion units in 2025, with cumulative volume above 4.6 billion. For a design engineer, though, the more useful question is how the selection logic works in practice.
Matching the Sensing Principle to the Requirement
Hall effect is still the foundation. It is the most mature technology in the NOVOSENSE portfolio and the most versatile, supporting switches, latches, current sensors, angle sensors and linear position sensors. Planar and vertical Hall elements together enable 2D and 3D detection, and because the elements and their conditioning circuitry can share a single silicon die, the packages are compact and reliable. Hall is also forgiving. Its wide linear range and resistance to saturation simplify designs in strong fields or crowded electromagnetic environments, and in appliances, consumer electronics and smart-home products that have no need for nanoamp-level power, it is usually the better system choice on cost and maturity.
TMR takes over where Hall runs short of sensitivity or power headroom. Its strengths are high sensitivity, low noise and very low power consumption. NOVOSENSE’s TMR switch solutions draw as little as 200 nA while sampling above 1 kHz, which suits battery-powered utility meters and industrial equipment that need both long battery life and fast response. TMR also handles weak fields and longer sensing distances better than Hall. AMR fills out the magnetoresistive side of the portfolio with low-power switching, high-resolution angle encoding and automotive wheel-speed sensing.
Inductive sensing removes the permanent magnet altogether, although NOVOSENSE is quick to point out that losing the magnet is rarely the goal in itself. “What matters more are the resulting system-level characteristics,” the company says. With no magnet, the sensor is inherently insensitive to external fields, which suits compact designs sitting near high currents, motors or power electronics, and inductive technology can reach higher angular accuracy than existing Hall or magnetoresistive approaches. The price is integration effort. An inductive design needs a matching target rotor, coil or PCB structure, usually takes more space than a compact Hall solution and is rarely a drop-in replacement for an existing magnetic encoder.
Fluxgate covers the precision end of current sensing. Here NOVOSENSE supplies the signal-conditioning ASIC and the customer designs the probe, windings and module, so final performance depends on the whole assembly. A well-executed fluxgate system typically reaches the 0.5 percent accuracy class, with particular strength in offset stability and low-current detection, which is why it appears in battery management, on the grid side of photovoltaic inverters, in energy storage and in leakage-current detection.
NOVOSENSE Magnetic Sensor Technology Lineup
Table 1 summarizes how the five principles line up. When a customer arrives with a requirement rather than a technology preference, NOVOSENSE first asks what the measurement is for and whether a production-proven solution already exists in a comparable system or adjacent industry. For new applications, the team works through range, accuracy, response time, power, interface, installation space, environment, EMC, reliability, functional safety, cost and production constraints. “The technology is selected according to these system constraints rather than a predetermined preference for Hall, AMR or TMR,” the company explains. The answer often surprises the customer. A solution proven in AGVs or robot vacuum cleaners, for example, might be adapted for a robotics program to reduce cost or implementation complexity.
Table 1. Magnetic sensing principles at a glance
| Principle | Where it fits best | Design considerations | Typical applications | 
| Hall effect | Mature and cost-effective; wide linear range and resistance to saturation; element and conditioning on one die; differential designs reject stray fields | Lower intrinsic sensitivity; not suited to nanoamp-level power budgets | Switches and latches, integrated and linear current sensing, automotive angle, 3D and linear position | 
| AMR | Low-power switching, high-resolution angle encoding, wheel-speed sensing | Performance depends on element materials and process maturity; NOVOSENSE can also supply the conditioning ASIC for a customer element | Automotive wheel speed, angle encoders, low-power switches | 
| TMR | Highest sensitivity and low noise; switch current as low as 200 nA with sampling above 1 kHz; weak-field and long-distance detection | Hall remains more cost-effective where nanoamp power is unnecessary and more tolerant of strong fields | Battery-powered meters, low-power switches, industrial level sensing; angle and position in development | 
| Inductive | No permanent magnet; inherently insensitive to external fields; highest angular accuracy (MT6901 typical INL ±0.02°) | Requires a matching target rotor, coil or PCB structure; larger than compact Hall; rarely a drop-in replacement | Robot joints, high-end servo, precision machinery, inductive proximity switches | 
| Fluxgate (conditioning ASIC) | System accuracy in the 0.5 percent class; offset stability; low-current detection | Customer designs probe, windings and module; performance depends on the full assembly | BMS, photovoltaic inverter grid side, energy storage, leakage-current detection | 
The Development Chain Behind the Breadth
Five sensing principles only help if each one is backed by more than a sensing element. What an engineer actually receives, accuracy over temperature and over the life of the part, is a property of the whole chain: element, signal-conditioning ASIC, package, calibration and production test.
Asked which link was hardest to build, NOVOSENSE pointed to the sensing elements. AMR and TMR elements demand long-term work on materials, physical mechanisms, manufacturing processes and reliability, and relatively few suppliers have real capability there. Calibration is the other link that separates products, since errors have to be characterized across temperature, field or angle and compensation parameters programmed into each device.
Three-temperature calibration shows what that means on the production floor. Each device is stabilized at low, room and high temperature, a known current or field is applied, offset and sensitivity errors are measured, and compensation coefficients are calculated, written to the part and verified. That is how high-precision NOVOSENSE current sensors reach approximately 1 percent accuracy across the operating temperature range. It is not free. Anyone who has watched a tester wait out a cold soak will know where the time goes: cooling and thermal stabilization take longer than heating, so temperature cycling often consumes more test time than the electrical measurements. NOVOSENSE is also candid that calibration retention over the operating life cannot be reduced to one universal number. It depends on the product, element, package and stress conditions, and it is confirmed through product-level reliability qualification and lifetime assessment.
The same chain lets NOVOSENSE supply only the conditioning ASIC when a customer brings its own AMR or TMR element, handling amplification, compensation, waveform conditioning and interface conversion, including SPI output. Around the silicon, the company supports customers with circuit design, magnetic-field simulation, mechanical assessment and system debugging.
Current Sensing: From Amperes to Kiloamperes
The current-sensing portfolio divides at roughly 200 A. Below that point, integrated sensors route current through a conductor inside a PCB-mountable package, with measurement ranges extending to ±400 A. Above it, linear sensors work with external magnetic structures, taking total coverage to about 2,000 A.
The boundary comes mainly from package current-carrying capability and system architecture. Conductor cross-section, power dissipation, temperature rise, PCB current capacity and safety requirements all cap what an integrated part can handle, and beyond roughly 200 to 300 A, designers move the main current onto a busbar anyway. In EV traction systems running from several hundred to more than 1,000 A, a linear sensor with an external magnetic structure simply fits the architecture better. The line is moving, though. The market is already asking for integrated solutions in the 300 to 400 A range, and even at the same measurement range, a package that carries more current brings lower on-resistance, lower loss and less temperature rise.
For integrated devices, the package is an engineering variable, not a footprint preference. Compact QFN and SOP packages serve 12 V, 24 V and 48 V systems with moderate isolation needs, while wide-body and ultra-wide-body packages serve on-board chargers, DC-DC converters and 400 V to 800 V battery platforms. Bandwidths reach 1 MHz and 2 MHz for fast overcurrent response.
The NSM2051 takes that idea furthest. Aimed at emerging 2,000 V photovoltaic and storage platforms, its key change lies in the package rather than the die. An ultra-wide-body outline extends creepage and clearance to 15 mm and supports a basic-insulation working voltage of 2,800 VDC and 2,000 Vrms while remaining PCB mountable. Isolated current sensing moves onto the board in place of a larger conventional module, reducing system size, external module count and assembly steps.
Above the integrated range, the external magnetic structure sets the tradeoffs. A C-core is the mature option. It concentrates the field from the target current and shields against some external interference, generally giving the best stray-field immunity and accuracy. NOVOSENSE C-core solutions have been adopted by major Chinese automotive manufacturers, and the NSM203x linear sensor pairs with an external C-core and busbar for traction measurement. The U-shaped magnetic concentrator trades some of that margin for compactness. The NSM2025 redirects the horizontal field into the vertical plane so the sensor mounts directly on the PCB, with approximately 1.5 percent full-temperature accuracy, roughly 270 kHz bandwidth, a typical 2 µs response time and operation from −40°C to 150°C.
Coreless designs, now sampling, go furthest on size, weight and system cost and avoid core saturation and hysteresis entirely. The honest tradeoff is greater sensitivity to ambient fields, crosstalk from adjacent conductors and installation tolerance. Coreless works when sensor and busbar are designed together, using busbar slotting, differential placement, tolerance control, crosstalk compensation and magnetic-field simulation. Put simply, the busbar drawing matters as much as the sensor datasheet.
GaAs Hall current sensors are also sampling, aimed at designs where drift is the limiting error. GaAs elements deliver lower sensitivity drift and better full-temperature accuracy than silicon Hall, but because the element and conditioning ASIC are fabricated separately and joined through multi-chip packaging and wire bonding, cost is higher than for a single-die silicon device. Targets include high-accuracy industrial current sensing, battery management, and photovoltaic and energy-storage systems.
Position, Angle and Speed: Resolution in Constrained Mechanics
For industrial motion, NOVOSENSE combines conditioning ASICs with Hall, AMR and inductive encoders, and the lineup is easiest to read as a ladder of accuracy. NOVOSENSE’s encoders support both on-axis and off-axis installation in robot joints, servo systems and motors. The MT6835 offers up to 21-bit resolution and is a practical replacement for optical encoders at 19 bits and below, already used in general-purpose servo motors, battery and food-processing equipment, 3D printers and other automation systems. In those applications, customers weigh cost, environmental robustness, reliability and installation complexity alongside angular accuracy.
For 19- to 23-bit requirements, the MT6901 inductive encoder is the next rung. Compared with Hall-based solutions, it delivers higher system-level accuracy, with typical INL of ±0.02° and angular error held below ±0.07° from −40°C to 125°C. Because it needs no permanent magnet and is insensitive to external fields, it keeps that accuracy next to motors and high-current conductors. Compared with high-accuracy optical encoders, it offers lower system cost along with the environmental robustness of a non-optical design, making it a strong fit for robotic joints, high-end servo systems and precision machinery. Optical encoders still lead above 23 bits of effective resolution, in precision cutting and machining, high-end metrology and laboratory calibration, and they remain the reference used to test other encoder technologies.
The NSM350x solves a mechanical problem as much as an electrical one. Robot joints use hollow shafts so power and communication cables can run through the center, simplifying cable management and shrinking the joint, and an encoder sitting on the axis blocks that path. The NSM350x moves the sensing elements off-axis and reads a dual-track magnetic ring, using a Vernier algorithm that compares the two tracks to recover single-turn absolute angle at up to 22-bit resolution. It supports 1.28 mm, 1.5 mm and 2.0 mm magnetic pitches and 16, 32 and 64 pole pairs. Typical INL is ±0.3° after simple self-calibration and ±0.1° after constant-speed self-calibration. That second figure carries a process requirement: the customer has to provide stable constant-speed rotation during assembly or production calibration, usually with a coaxial motor-to-motor fixture.
In automotive angle sensing, Hall is the more widely used technology, and for good reason. Integrating the Hall elements and conditioning circuitry on one die produces compact, reliable packages, while differential architectures and Hall’s lower intrinsic sensitivity give strong immunity to external fields. That counts for a lot in electrified vehicles, where high-current conductors are packed close together. The MT652x family uses 3D Hall sensing to detect field changes in the XY, XZ or YZ planes for valves and actuators. Meanwhile, the MT6511 employs a differential Hall architecture to improve immunity to stray magnetic fields. For ride-height sensing, the planar Hall NSM3219 uses a two-wire PSI5 current interface that provides strong interference immunity, supports PCB-less sensor designs and cuts wiring and overall system cost.
Further down the stack, Hall switches and latches span low-voltage consumer, 24 V industrial and automotive requirements up to 60 V, with speed-and-direction outputs, two- and three-wire interfaces, programmable options and 3D sensing, while xMR switches serve battery-powered equipment. The NSM903x shows how much now fits in one device: planar and vertical Hall elements for X, Y and Z detection, on-chip CORDIC processing for 360° angle calculation, 3D and angle-switch modes, low-power operation, an interrupt function and I2C, for joysticks, wearables, smart crowns and position switches.
Where the Portfolio Is Deployed
In vehicles, the portfolio reaches across body systems (windows, sunroofs, tailgates, seats, wipers and headlamp adjustment), thermal management valves, powertrain current measurement from BMS main circuits and traction inverters down to on-board chargers, DC-DC converters and PFC stages, and chassis functions such as steering angle, vehicle height, pedals, wheel speed and electric power steering. Industrial deployments center on current sensing in photovoltaic, energy-storage and charging systems and on closed-loop feedback in servo and stepper systems. Consumer uses range from appliance motors to earbuds, smart crowns and wearables, where low-power Hall and TMR parts protect battery life.
Functional safety follows the product architecture, not the sensing principle. Depending on the device, NOVOSENSE provides on-chip diagnostics, signal-plausibility checks, fault-status outputs and dual-channel or redundant outputs, backed by safety documentation and development support. Examples run from ASIL A for the MT72xx and NSM101x Hall switches and latches, through ASIL B(D) for the NSM41xx wheel-speed sensors and ASIL C for the NSM3219, to ASIL D for the MT6521 and MT6511 angle sensors. “Functional-safety capability is not determined directly by whether a product uses Hall, AMR or TMR technology,” NOVOSENSE notes. The same reasoning answers the common hesitation about TMR in safety-relevant positions. TMR already has years of volume production in automotive angle sensing, industrial level sensing and low-power switches, and NOVOSENSE qualifies its automotive TMR parts to standards such as AEC-Q100, evaluating the element, ASIC, package and interconnects together.
Where Magnetic Sensing Goes Next
According to NOVOSENSE, robotics is producing the most concentrated set of new problems. Humanoid and collaborative robot joints must balance angular accuracy, compact design, hollow-shaft routing, field immunity, in-system calibration and cost at once. Two gaps stand out. High-accuracy calibration still depends on a motor-to-motor fixture, which is manageable for a standalone motor and difficult once that motor is buried inside a joint, and customers want to calibrate simply by turning the joint during final assembly or maintenance. Robot builders also want single-chip encoders that support multiple industrial protocols and store algorithms, configuration and calibration data on-chip, eliminating external MCUs, memory and extra PCBs.
Mature markets are moving too. Portable medical and consumer devices keep pushing for lower power, lower noise and faster response, automotive switch applications increasingly require functional-safety support, and the move to 48 V architectures raises voltage-withstand requirements. Over the next two years, NOVOSENSE plans to broaden its inductive encoder and TMR portfolios across more accuracy levels, sizes and installation arrangements, extend TMR into angle and position sensing, integrate more algorithms, memory and communication protocols, and develop ultra-low-power TMR and inductive switch and proximity solutions. Outside China, the company has set up offices and local support teams in Germany, Japan and South Korea, where customers put heavy weight on long-term reliability data, functional-safety documentation, supply continuity and local engineering support.
The thread running through all of this showed up when NOVOSENSE described how its customer conversations have changed. As the portfolio grew, discussions gradually shifted from “where can this product be used?” to “what solution does this system require?” For engineers juggling current, voltage, resolution, power and mechanical constraints in the same design, that second question is the right place to start.
Meet NOVOSENSE at electronica 2026, November 10 to 13, at Messe München, Hall C5, Booth 159. NOVOSENSE is advancing innovation across automotive electronics, renewable energy & power supply, industrial control, and consumer electronics with a comprehensive portfolio of isolators, interfaces, drivers, sensors, signal chain, and power management ICs.

articles.title: Shiprocket turns profitable in Q2 FY27 with Rs 674 Cr revenue
articles.text:
Shiprocket turns profitable in Q2 FY27 with Rs 674 Cr revenue
Shiprocket reported a net profit of Rs 60 lakh in Q2 FY27, compared with a loss of Rs 20.3 crore a year ago, as revenue grew 35% to Rs 673.6 crore.
Shiprocket, an ecommerce enablement platform for MSMEs, turned profitable in the second quarter of FY27, reporting a net profit of Rs 60 lakh for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, against a net loss of Rs 20.3 crore in the corresponding period last year.
The company's revenue from operations increased 35% year-on-year (YoY) to Rs 673.6 crore during the quarter. Adjusted EBITDA stood at Rs 14.2 crore, compared with a loss in the year-ago period.
Shiprocket's core business revenue grew 25% YoY to Rs 461.5 crore, while its emerging business revenue increased 61% to Rs 212.2 crore. The emerging business, which includes cross-border shipping, omnichannel fulfilment, hyperlocal delivery, marketing technology (Martech) and ecommerce enablement solutions, contributed 31% to overall revenue, compared with 26% a year ago.
Within the emerging business, Martech revenue grew 102%, while the omnichannel business registered 79% growth during the quarter.
Shiprocket attributed the growth in its omnichannel business to brands using its platform to replenish quick commerce dark stores. Its appointment-based delivery services allow brands to schedule deliveries and access real-time purchase order visibility from platforms such as Blinkit and Zepto.
The company's contribution increased 43% YoY to Rs 130 crore, accounting for 19.3% of revenue. The core business generated adjusted EBITDA of Rs 59.1 crore, up 29% YoY, with its adjusted EBITDA margin improving to 12.8% from 12.4%. The emerging business narrowed its adjusted EBITDA margin loss to 21.2% from 31.5%, while its contribution margin improved to 15.4% from 10.1%.
Shiprocket's trailing 12-month gross merchandise value (GMV) stood at Rs 37,398.7 crore, generated through 233 million unique transactions. The platform served more than 2.36 lakh active merchants during the period.
The number of merchants using its emerging business products increased 75% to 62,025 on a trailing 12-month basis. During the quarter, 17,281 new merchants joined through emerging products, more than three times the 5,396 additions reported a year ago.
“Indian commerce is splitting across more channels every year. A small brand today sells on its own website and on Instagram, replenishes quick commerce dark stores, and is starting to be found through AI search. For a large company, every new channel means a new team. For a small seller, it means friction. Shiprocket is building the infrastructure that removes this friction, so that any MSME in India can sell, ship and grow on the same footing as India’s biggest brands, every channel a switch away on one dashboard," said Saahil Goel, Managing Director and CEO of Shiprocket.
"Growing 35% with positive Adjusted EBITDA and operating cash flow shows we can build it from our own operations. We are in the business of making other people a business, and our ambition is simple: to see the next generation of great Indian brands built on Shiprocket,” he added.
“PAT turned positive this quarter on three drivers. First, scale in Core: transactions grew 31% and Adjusted EBITDA grew faster than revenue. Second, the Emerging engine kept firing: Martech and Omnichannel, our fastest-growing lines, more than doubled Emerging contribution on 61% revenue growth. Third, a stronger balance sheet: IPO proceeds retired all our borrowings, which cut finance costs, and the surplus now earns interest income," said Tanmay Kumar, CFO of Shiprocket.
"We generated Rs 55.1 crore from operations in the first half, more than twice last year, and we are debt-free. Emerging now brings merchants onto the platform on its own, not only through cross-sell from Core. Around 17,300 merchants joined Shiprocket through our Emerging products this quarter, more than three times the number a year ago,” he said.
Shiprocket also reported net cash from operating activities of Rs 55.1 crore in the first half of FY27, compared with Rs 23.8 crore in the corresponding period last year.
Following the receipt of proceeds from its initial public offering (IPO) during the quarter, the company repaid its outstanding borrowings of Rs 242 crore, ending the first half debt-free.
The company also introduced several AI-powered features during the quarter, including Aitlas, which helps brands track their visibility in AI search, personalised marketing journeys, enhanced checkout features and AI-powered shipping analytics. Its platform currently handles more than 14 billion API hits a month.

articles.title: Attention à ce que vous partagez sur iCloud, Apple pourra supprimer votre compte si le contenu est « nuisible »
articles.text:
La première bêta d’iOS 27.3 est arrivée chez les développeurs dans la semaine du 3 novembre, escortée d’une page d’assistance publiée le même jour. La page prévient que les éléments partagés via iCloud avec l’option « Toute personne disposant du lien » seront « vérifiés par Apple à la recherche de contenu nuisible ». La mesure s’applique à partir de la version 27.3 d’iOS, d’iPadOS, de macOS et de visionOS, dont la version finale est attendue courant décembre.
Ce que vous signez avec un lien public
L’option visée transforme une photo d’iCloud Photos ou un fichier d’iCloud Drive en lien ouvert, consultable sans invitation ni compte, directement depuis la feuille de partage du système. La page le pose sans détour : le contenu devient accessible à quiconque détient l’adresse, « y compris Apple ». La bêta ajoute d’ailleurs un avertissement inédit au moment de créer un tel lien, encore affiché en anglais dans cette première mouture.
La page rappelle aussi qu’un élément partagé de la sorte « n’est plus chiffré de bout en bout, même si le propriétaire ou les participants ont activé la Protection avancée des données ». La règle précédait cette mise à jour ; Apple la couche simplement noir sur blanc au moment où il s’octroie un droit de regard. Les autres canaux échappent au contrôle : le partage restreint aux « personnes que vous choisissez », sur invitation ou approbation, comme l’envoi d’une copie du fichier restent en dehors du périmètre décrit.
Compte désactivé, autorités prévenues : l’éventail des sanctions
Un contenu jugé nuisible déclenche tout l’arsenal : Apple « se réserve le droit de déplacer, refuser, modifier, retirer ou supprimer le contenu à tout moment ». La sanction peut remonter jusqu’au compte, bloqué ou désactivé, avec interdiction d’en rouvrir un avec la même adresse e-mail ou le même numéro de téléphone. Les forces de l’ordre peuvent être saisies « si nécessaire ». La page ne décrit, à ce stade, ni notification au propriétaire ni voie de recours.
Le mot « nuisible » ne reçoit, lui, aucune définition. Ni catégories visées, ni méthode d’analyse, humaine ou automatisée, ni réponse sur le sort des liens créés avant la mise à jour. La page s’arrête là, et Apple n’a rien précisé depuis sa publication, malgré les sollicitations. Les conditions d’utilisation d’iCloud interdisaient déjà les contenus illégaux ; la page annonce désormais une vérification en bonne et due forme.
Apple avait annoncé en 2021 un système de détection d’images pédocriminelles dans les photothèques iCloud, avant d’y renoncer le 7 décembre 2022 sous la pression des défenseurs de la vie privée. Dans l’intervalle, une plainte collective réclamant jusqu’à 32,8 milliards de dollars lui reprochait précisément son inaction ; une juge fédérale l’a rejetée en juillet au nom de la section 230. L’inspection refait surface quatre ans plus tard, cantonnée cette fois aux partages publics.

Vos enceintes connectées KEF peuvent désormais se transformer en satellites home cinéma
KEF accélère dans le home cinéma en permettant à sa barre de son XIO d’accueillir ses fameuses enceintes connectées LSX II, LSX II LT et Coda W comme enceintes surround sans fil. De quoi renforcer l’immersion sonore, sous certaines conditions.
KEF fait enfin évoluer sa barre de son XIO avec une mise à jour logicielle qui permet d’y associer des enceintes arrière issues de son catalogue. L’ajout de véritables canaux derrière la position d’écoute permet de considérablement renforcer l'immersion en home cinéma, puisque les effets arrière sont désormais diffusés directement vers l’auditeur, et non plus seulement reproduits par traitement virtuel ou réflexion acoustique.
La fonction est disponible avec les LSX II, LSX II LT et Coda W. Pour les propriétaires de ces enceintes actives connectées, l’intérêt est de pouvoir les réutiliser comme canaux arrière dans un système construit autour de la XIO. Il n’est pas nécessaire de les relier à la barre par un câble audio traversant la pièce, car la transmission passe par un récepteur sans fil KEF KW2 RX.
Bien sûr, pour KEF, cette nouvelle fonction est aussi un moyen d’inciter les possesseurs d’une barre de son XIO à investir dans des enceintes connectées, et inversement. L’adaptateur KW2 RX était jusqu’alors réservé à l’association d’un caisson de basses KEF KC62, KC92 ou KUBE, sans la contrainte des câbles.
La transmission sans fil passe par un récepteur KEF KW2 RX optionnel
Si la mise à jour est gratuite, tant pour la barre que pour les enceintes, cette configuration nécessite d’investir dans un récepteur KW2 RX, vendu 179 €. Heureusement, un seul adaptateur suffit pour associer une paire d’enceintes actives compatibles, mais il faudra malgré tout passer à la caisse, alors que de nombreuses enceintes connectées pouvant faire office de satellites communiquent directement avec la barre de son.
La configuration s’effectue depuis l’application KEF Connect, qui guide l’utilisateur dans l’association des enceintes. La barre de son transmet le signal au récepteur KW2 RX sur une bande radio de 2,4 GHz, avec une latence de 57 ms et une résolution allant jusqu’à 24 bits/48 kHz. Celui-ci se connecte aux entrées mini-jack 3,5 mm ou optique des enceintes. À noter que cet adaptateur doit être alimenté sur secteur à l’aide d’un câble USB-C inclus, ce qui complique un peu la mise en œuvre.
KEF ne détaille pas les formats sonores pris en charge, mais en l’absence de canaux latéraux et verticaux sur ses enceintes actives, il est probable que la hauteur des effets Dolby Atmos et la cohérence entre l’avant et l’arrière de la scène sonore soient limités. Pour l’heure, KEF ne prévoit pas non plus la possibilité d’ajouter une seconde paire d’enceintes actives, en frontal ou sur les côtés de la position d’écoute.
KEF LSX II
Une compatibilité vouée à s’étendre d'ici la fin de l'année
KEF prévoit d’élargir progressivement la liste des enceintes compatibles. Les LS50 Wireless II rejoindront le dispositif en décembre 2026, tandis que les LS60 Wireless et LS LUXE sont annoncées pour courant 2027.
Pour les utilisateurs déjà équipés en KEF, cette évolution permet donc de faire évoluer leur installation en conservant leurs enceintes, plutôt que de repartir sur un système surround séparé. Elle reste néanmoins réservée aux modèles compatibles et implique l’achat du KW2 RX.

articles.title: La IA ya está amenazando los cartuchos de Nintendo
articles.text:
Macronix es uno de los mayores fabricantes de chips de memoria no volátiles del planeta. Esta compañía taiwanesa produce memorias NOR Flash, NAND Flash y ROM, aunque sus ventas difieren mucho de un tipo a otro de circuitos integrados. En el tercer trimestre de 2026 sus ingresos por chips ROM cayeron un 39% interanual. Sin embargo, durante este periodo su facturación por la venta de memorias NOR y NAND aumentó un 158% y un 768%, respectivamente.
Las memorias NAND Flash se usan en las unidades SSD y algunos dispositivos electrónicos, así como en sistemas embebidos y soluciones de almacenamiento industrial. Son muy demandadas actualmente por los centros de datos. Los chips NOR Flash se emplean en equipos de comunicaciones, electrónica industrial, coches y dispositivos electrónicos. También son muy demandados por los centros de datos.
Las memorias ROM, sin embargo, se utilizan para almacenar el firmware y otros datos permanentes en dispositivos electrónicos, coches, placas base de PC, equipos industriales y sistemas de telecomunicaciones. También se usan en los cartuchos de videojuegos. Ante la enorme diferencia de demanda que hay de sus chips NOR, NAND y ROM, Macronix ha tomado una decisión: va a dejar progresivamente de fabricar memorias ROM. Y son las que usa Nintendo en sus cartuchos para Switch y Switch 2.
Por el momento el formato físico de Nintendo está a salvo
Macronix no va a abandonar poco a poco la producción de chips ROM porque hayan dejado de ser viables; va a volcarse en la producción de memorias NOR y NAND porque su capacidad de fabricación es limitada y puede obtener una rentabilidad mayor fabricando estos últimos chips. Esto es todo. Esta compañía tiene sus propias plantas de procesado de obleas de 8 y 12 pulgadas, pero el, por el momento, insaciable apetito de los centros de datos para inteligencia artificial (IA) está alterando sus prioridades. Al igual que las de muchas otras empresas.
La reducción del número de proveedores podría incrementar los costes de fabricación de los cartuchos
Entonces, ¿qué pasará a corto y medio plazo con los cartuchos de Nintendo? Por el momento todo parece indicar que no sucederá nada. Macronix es un proveedor importante de memorias ROM para la compañía de Kioto, pero no es la única empresa a la que compra este tipo de semiconductores. Nintendo también es clienta de la japonesa ROHM y de su filial Lapis Semiconductor, por lo que de momento el suministro de chips ROM parece estar asegurado.
No obstante, la próxima ausencia de Macronix en el mercado de estos circuitos integrados introduce una dificultad adicional en la cadena de suministro de Nintendo y una mayor dependencia de los fabricantes que continuarán produciendo estos componentes. Además, la reducción del número de proveedores podría incrementar los costes de fabricación de los cartuchos, por lo que cabe la posibilidad, aunque por el momento es solo una hipótesis, de que los juegos en formato físico de Switch y Switch 2 terminen encareciéndose.
Sospecho que a muchos jugadores la posibilidad de que Nintendo finalmente decida abandonar el formato físico nos hace estremecer. Esperemos que este momento no llegue. O, al menos, que tarde mucho en llegar. Lo peor que podría pasarnos es que Lapis Semiconductor decida a medio plazo seguir los pasos de Macronix y también abandone el mercado de los chips ROM. No obstante, estos semiconductores son necesarios, por lo que es inasumible que todos los fabricantes de chips dejen de producirlos. Nintendo, estamos en tus manos.

articles.title: Apple veut des salariés dopés à l’IA, mais commence à couper les crédits
articles.text:
Apple réduit les sommes que certains salariés peuvent consacrer chaque jour aux outils d’intelligence artificielle. L’entreprise continue pourtant de pousser ses équipes à les intégrer dans leur travail.
Utiliser davantage l’IA pour gagner du temps, oui, mais en surveillant le compteur. Chez Apple, les assistants capables d’écrire du code ou de débusquer des erreurs ont désormais droit à un encadrement budgétaire plus serré. Selon les informations de Mark Gurman pour Bloomberg, certains ingénieurs ont déjà vu leur enveloppe quotidienne diminuer. Et d’autres réductions sont à l’étude.
De 300 à 200 dollars par jour, avec de nouvelles baisses dans les tuyaux
En octobre, Apple aurait abaissé de 300 à 200 dollars le plafond quotidien de dépenses de certains ingénieurs utilisant des modèles d’IA. Pour certaines équipes, l’entreprise préparerait une nouvelle baisse, susceptible de ramener cette limite à 100 dollars.
Hors ingénierie, de nombreux services disposent déjà d’un plafond de 100 dollars par jour. Apple aurait envisagé de le réduire jusqu’à 25 dollars pour certaines équipes. Les salariés ayant besoin d’une enveloppe supérieure pourraient toutefois demander une dérogation à leur direction.
Ces montants financent les jetons consommés par les modèles, ces unités de données traitées à chaque requête. Une longue session de programmation, avec des corrections successives et beaucoup de code à analyser, peut rapidement faire grimper la consommation. Les salariés d’Apple ont notamment accès à Claude, ChatGPT et Gemini.
Attention toutefois à ne pas confondre budget autorisé et facture réelle. D’après Bloomberg, certains employés soulignent que peu de leurs collègues atteignaient l’ancien plafond de 300 dollars. Réduire cette limite d’un tiers ne signifie donc pas qu’Apple économisera automatiquement un tiers de ses dépenses.
L’IA reste encouragée, mais son utilisation doit coûter moins cher
Le changement est intéressant au regard des consignes précédentes. Les salariés d’Apple sont depuis plusieurs mois poussés à utiliser davantage l’IA, notamment avant de demander des renforts humains. Le budget de 300 dollars par jour était déjà évoqué à l’époque.
La volonté de transformer les méthodes de travail reste bien présente. Certaines équipes seraient désormais orientées vers des modèles moins coûteux ou fonctionnant directement sur les appareils. Pour les utilisateurs les plus gourmands, les prochaines réductions pourraient surtout multiplier les demandes de dérogation.
Les derniers comptes publiés par Apple donnent une idée du contexte : les dépenses de recherche et développement ont atteint 45,8 milliards de dollars sur l’exercice 2026, soit environ 32 % de plus qu’un an auparavant. Les dépenses d’exploitation ont progressé d’environ 22 %, à 75,5 milliards de dollars. Ces chiffres couvrent toutefois un périmètre bien plus large que l’IA.
Apple a refusé de commenter ces informations. Le montant des économies attendues reste inconnu, tout comme l’étendue des nouvelles restrictions qui seront finalement appliquées.

articles.title: Laser statt Funk: Griechischer Satellit schickt Daten per Lichtstrahl zur Erde
articles.text:
Laser statt Funk: Griechischer Satellit schickt Daten per Lichtstrahl zur Erde
Griechenland hat eine optische Datenverbindung aus dem All zur Erde in Betrieb genommen. Der Satellit Ermis-3 stellte aus einer niedrigen Erdumlaufbahn eine Laserverbindung zur Bodenstation HolOGS-1 auf dem Berg Holomondas in Nordgriechenland her. Dabei handelte es sich zunächst um einen Test.
Das Projekt wird von der Europäischen Raumfahrtagentur ESA unterstützt. Ermis-3 ist ein sogenannter 8U-Cubesat, also ein würfelförmiger Kleinsatellit aus acht standardisierten Modulen. Laut ESA kam die Verbindung schnell zustande. Damit sei eines der Hauptziele der Mission erreicht: das präzise Ausrichten, Erfassen und Verfolgen des Ziels, in der Fachsprache „Pointing, Acquisition, Tracking“.
Technik aus mehreren europäischen Ländern
Bei dem Test kam ausschließlich europäische Technik zum Einsatz. Den im März 2026 gestarteten Ermis-3 entwickelte die National and Kapodistrian University in Athen, das Bodenterminal stammt von der Aristoteles-Universität in Thessaloniki. Die Übertragungstechnik lieferte das litauische Unternehmen Astrolight. Getestet wurden die Systeme am Europäischen Raumfahrtforschungs- und Technologiezentrum ESTEC der ESA in den Niederlanden.
ESA-Manager Frederic Rouesnel sagte, das Ergebnis zeige, dass Europa durch die Zusammenarbeit von Industrie, Wissenschaft und Institutionen Innovationen hervorbringen könne. Die ESA habe Programmmanagement, technische Überwachung und ingenieurtechnische Unterstützung beigesteuert.
Hohe Datenrate, aber anspruchsvolle Technik
Bei der optischen Kommunikation überträgt ein Laser die Daten. Der Vorteil: Die Datenrate liegt deutlich über der von herkömmlichem Funk. Dafür ist das Verfahren aber komplizierter: Der Satellit rast mit mehreren tausend Kilometern pro Stunde um die Erde und muss den Laserstrahl dabei exakt auf den Empfänger richten.
Das Zeitfenster für die Verbindung ist zudem kurz. Hinzu kommt das Wetter: Wolken können die Verbindung blockieren, Turbulenzen in der Atmosphäre verschlechtern die Signalqualität. Dennoch verspricht die Technik neue Impulse für souveräne Drahtlosverbindungen auf der Erde.

articles.title: Android permitirá backup automático de fotos e vídeos no Windows • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Android permitirá backup automático de fotos e vídeos no Windows
Novidade do Android usará a ferramenta Quick Share para permitir que fotos e vídeos sejam enviados automaticamente para o Windows.
Quando o assunto é backup de fotos, normalmente pensamos em serviços nas nuvens, como o Google Drive, o OneDrive e o Dropbox. Mas usuários do Android poderão ter, em breve, a opção de transferir fotos e vídeos automaticamente de seu celular ou tablet para um computador com Windows.
Ainda não há um anúncio oficial a respeito. A novidade foi descoberta por veículos como o Android Authority nas notas de lançamento do sistema operacional para novembro de 2026, no tópico que aborda o Google Play Services versão 26.43.
Mesmo sendo curta, a nota deixa claro que o backup envolverá o Quick Share, ferramenta que já permite compartilhamento de arquivos entre dispositivos Android e PCs. Mas esse compartilhamento é manual. O recurso que o Google está preparando envia fotos e vídeos do Android de modo automático para o computador. Ao que tudo indica, arquivos de áudio também poderão ser enviados.
Os detalhes sobre como o backup automático funcionará ainda não foram revelados pelo Google, mas uma análise feita pelo Android Authority em abril, quando o recurso foi descoberto, indica que a configuração começa pelo Quick Share instalado no Windows, requer que o celular ou tablet esteja fisicamente próximo para o “pareamento” e exige o uso de uma Conta Google.
Ainda não há previsão para a disponibilidade geral, muito menos uma lista de aparelhos compatíveis. Mas, como o recurso foi mencionado em notas de lançamento recentes do Android, é de se presumir que a sua chegada oficial ocorrerá em um futuro próximo, embora de modo progressivo — há boas chances de que comece pelos celulares Google Pixel.
Se faz sentido? Bom, backup local ainda é backup. Pelo menos para quem tem um HD ou SSD específico para esse fim, um recurso que automatiza o backup do conteúdo gerado no celular certamente será bem-vindo. Essa também é uma forma de ter acesso rápido às suas fotos e vídeos, é claro.

articles.title: Un camión con USD 11,4 millones en equipos de Nvidia desapareció en California y la policía perdió su rastro
articles.text:
Un camión con seis palés de equipos de Nvidia, valuados en USD 11,4 millones, salió de Oakland, California, el 29 de agosto rumbo a Fort Worth, Texas, y desapareció en el camino. La policía de Oakland investiga el caso y, hasta ahora, no anunció arrestos.
El robo se conoció el 4 de noviembre por un informe del diario East Bay Times, que retomaron el sitio Hoodline y el diario New York Post. Según esas versiones, el vehículo llevaba el logo de una empresa de transporte de alimentos y retiró la carga en la ciudad de la bahía de San Francisco tal como estaba previsto.
Después, el camión y sus conductores se esfumaron. Los investigadores siguieron el vehículo, que hizo varias paradas de varias horas, y perdieron su rastro en el condado de San Bernardino, en el sur del estado. La desaparición no se denunció hasta comienzos de septiembre.
Las autoridades describieron a los responsables como aparentemente sofisticados, según Hoodline. Los informes no precisan qué productos ni qué modelos de chips viajaban en los palés, ni cómo se organizó el retiro de la carga.
Un nuevo caso en una serie de robos de equipos de IA
No es el primer ataque contra cargas de Nvidia en la zona de la bahía de San Francisco. Según Hoodline, que cita al diario The Mercury News, en 2025 la policía de Fremont y Union City investigaron robos de cargamentos de la empresa por más de USD 7,5 millones. Creen que algunos sospechosos viajaban desde el sur de California.
En septiembre, dos remolques con logos de Nvidia y de PlusAI, una empresa de camiones autónomos, desaparecieron de un depósito en Fremont. Llevaban unos 18.000 kilos de arena, una carga simulada para pruebas, y la policía los recuperó. Wired informó que no hubo arrestos, según la vocera de la policía de Fremont, Amy Gee.
En agosto, Wired publicó otra investigación, que resumió Tom’s Hardware: ladrones habrían inutilizado a dos vehículos de escolta privada y se llevaron camiones con equipos para centros de datos que viajaban de Silicon Valley al sur de California. Ninguno de los dos camiones apareció.
Gerardo Pachuca, exdetective del Departamento del Sheriff de Los Ángeles y hoy consultor en delitos de carga, dijo a Wired que otro conductor chocó por detrás a una escolta y huyó, y que a la otra la hicieron girar con una maniobra que usa la policía. “Es lo peor que he visto”, afirmó sobre el robo de cargas en Estados Unidos.
Los robos bajan en cantidad, pero las pérdidas suben
La firma Verisk CargoNet, que analiza robos de carga, registró 677 incidentes en Estados Unidos y Canadá en el segundo trimestre de 2026, un 26% menos que un año antes. Las pérdidas estimadas pasaron de USD 135,7 millones a USD 304,6 millones, según un análisis del 6 de agosto que cita Hoodline.
CargoNet señaló que los envíos de equipos informáticos para empresas pueden valer millones de dólares y viajar como carga seca común. Tom’s Hardware agregó que los servidores de Nvidia con restricciones de exportación se venden en China a cerca del doble de su precio minorista en Estados Unidos.
Los investigadores que consultó Wired creen que los conductores fueron cómplices en los dos casos de agosto y que los números de registro de los transportistas habían cambiado de manos hace poco. Es un fraude que permite contratar fletes con el registro federal de una empresa legítima.
Hoodline aclara que el FBI no clasifica el caso de Oakland dentro de ese tipo de fraude y que no hay datos que lo vinculen con el robo de los remolques de Fremont. Sobre el camión de Oakland, lo único confirmado es que se perdió su rastro en San Bernardino y que no hay arrestos.

articles.title: Gamers go to ridiculous lengths to "improve" GTA VI with Nvidia's DLSS 5
articles.text:
While the upcoming Grand Theft Auto VI won’t be available on PC this month, some gamers are making ridiculous preparations to use their PC graphics cards to apply Nvidia’s DLSS 5 technology to the console exclusive.
On an explicitly unmoderated GTAVI subreddit, user RevolutionaryBus8208 lays out a proposed setup, which runs a PlayStation 5 through a 4K capture card to a PC. From there, the video signal is run through Veyra, an open source tool that can apply DLSS 5’s AI-powered “neural rendering” to video content. The result—which also uses DLSS frame generation to increase the 30 fps source to a 90 fps output—is then piped back to a 4K TV, theoretically adding some of the benefits of a beefy PC graphics card to a console-exclusive game.
To demonstrate the potential of this setup, RevolutionaryBus8208 used Veyra to upscale the Grand Theft Auto VI Extended Look trailer posted in August. The resulting DLSS-ified version looks a bit better in places, with sharper background elements, subtler shadows, and more believable light scattering on some surfaces. But it also seems a bit washed out compared to the original video’s deeper blacks and arguably suffers from an unnaturally smooth “soap opera effect” in some scenes.
There ain’t nothing for free
While the upscaled version causes some occasional graphical artifacts and glitches from the frame generation process, it’s still an interesting proof of concept that shows just how far DLSS 5 has come from some of the early horror-show memes that circulated on the Internet earlier this year.

articles.title: AMD Brings FSR Upscaling 4.1.2 to Xbox Consoles
articles.text:
Thursday, November 5th 2026
AMD Brings FSR Upscaling 4.1.2 to Xbox Consoles
Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S consoles are finally getting machine learning-based upscaling technology with the latest FSR Upscaling 4.1.2. Microsoft's Game Development Kit (GDK) now officially includes FSR Upscaling 4.1.2 in two models. One is the full-scale upscaling model based on the INT8 data type, and the other is a new and efficient Lite INT8 model. Both models are compatible with both consoles, but the key point is that game developers have the flexibility to choose which model to implement. Depending on the demands of a game, the appropriate model can be applied to achieve optimal upscaling performance.
For Xbox handheld devices, the AMD FSR SDK 2.4 adds FSR Upscaling support for the Ryzen AI Z2 Extreme and Ryzen Z2 A processors, which power the ROG Xbox Ally, ROG Xbox Ally X, and ROG Xbox Ally X20 handhelds. This is achieved using an efficient INT8 model. Since these devices run Windows, developers can integrate FSR Upscaling 4.1.2 through the standard AMD FSR SDK.Keep in mind that FSR Upscaling 4.1.x only recently arrived for AMD's RDNA versions below RDNA 4. RDNA 4 supports native processing for 8-bit floating point data, allowing FSR 4.1 on RDNA 4 to run on FP8 data types. To enable the FSR 4.1 Upscaling model on RDNA 3, AMD must convert this to 8-bit integer data, as RDNA 3.5 APUs and RDNA 2 GPU IP powering Xbox consoles use INT8 data types without FP8 support.

articles.title: Meta says US users can now video chat with their Muse AI avatar | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Muse Voice, a feature that lets users call and video chat with Meta’s consumer AI agent, Muse, is now available to everyone in the U.S., the company announced on Thursday.
First introduced at Meta’s Connect developer conference in September, the video-chatting feature involves new AI models, Muse Realtime Avatar and Muse Realtime Voice technology, which help power the digital avatar that chats with the user.
While other AI competitors offer voice chat features, Meta’s Muse offers a cute, animated avatar (nicknamed Jolly), which users interact with as they ask questions or request tasks to be handled on their behalf. Users can also customize the avatar as they choose, changing it to something that looks more like a person, animal, or some other character.
The company believes that anthropomorphizing Muse in this way could make consumers feel more connected to their AI agent — a connection that could grow even stronger as they begin to engage in live conversations with it.
As the Muse avatar speaks, Meta says it will use “subtle expressions and gestures” that match the tone of the conversation.
The news of the rollout was announced via blog post and on X by Meta’s chief AI officer, Alexandr Wang, who shared a demo of his Muse in action. The video saw Wang joking around, referencing his love of posting memes on X, which he told his Muse may have gotten him in trouble with his boss. His Muse, a fluffy white dog, responds with a suggestion to add disclaimers to those memes that could be misinterpreted as Meta endorsing anything risqué. (Ha!)
The added support for video chats and calls comes just before Meta’s plan to launch a Tamagotchi-like wearable device for its Muse AI agent before year-end. When the device arrives, the digital avatar will appear on its small screen, letting users talk to the agent, which can then reply or carry out tasks for them.
Meta says the real-time conversations are supported on mobile, web, and Mac and will later come to its AI Glasses and the upcoming “Muse Charm” hardware device.

articles.title: Smart glasses 'not only have the potential to erode safety and privacy... but raise really important questions about consent': the UK is the latest country to consider restricting or controlling the sale of smart glasses — here's what you need to know
articles.text:
Putting the 'ban' in Meta Ray-Ban: the UK is considering placing restrictions on smart glasses sales as 'the government is already looking into options' to curb the secret filming of women
'The benefits of smart glasses must be weighed against the harms'
- The UK is the latest country to consider restricting the use and sale of smart glasses
- Safeguarding minister Satvir Kaur said "the government is looking into options to restrict smart glasses in certain settings and restricting the sale to certain users"
- During a debate around the technology, concerns were raised around the discreet filming of women and girls
As the adoption of smart glasses increases across the world, so too have restrictions and bans on the technology from businesses and governments alike. Australia has banned the tech in public spaces such as pools, gyms and government buildings, and now the UK government is also considering implementing restrictions.
The devices have become unpopular in many circles, even earning the nickname 'pervert glasses' after some men began using them to secretly film women and girls, then posting the captured videos online. Some private businesses, such as the Wetherspoons British bar chain, have also banned the use of the devices.
In a debate at Westminster Hall titled 'Smart glasses and violence against women and girls', UK safeguarding minister Satvir Kaur said (as reported by The Guardian): “the benefits of smart glasses must be weighed against the harms they can cause. The government is already looking into options to restrict smart glasses in certain settings and restricting the sale to certain users.”
This might be similar to Australia's ban on the technology being used in public spaces. Kaur also highlighted that “other settings, such as healthcare and education, have existing safeguarding or professional policies that are relevant to smart glasses and any kind of digital recording." Kaur seemed to be hinting that where limitations on recording on smartphones already exist, this would extend to smart glasses and similar tech, but we could also see wider smart glasses-specific rules in future.
Anna Sabine, the Liberal Democrat MP who opened the debate, reportedly said: “Women are reporting waking up after nights out to find videos of themselves have gone viral online, filmed without their knowledge or consent by men wearing smart glasses... these devices not only have the potential to erode safety and privacy in public spaces, but raise really important questions about consent.”
Analysis: More restrictions will surely follow
Kaur did also highlight the useful aspect of smart glasses, such as helping visually or hearing-impaired people understand their surroundings. For those people, she said "smart glasses have been a game-changer, helping them navigate the world around them.”
Our writer Kevin Lynch, who has a hearing impairment, reviewed the Nuance Audio smart specs equipped with directional microphones, which he said were 'genuinely impactful'. It's likely any incoming legislation would allow for this usage.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
However, there's no getting around the harmful uses of smart glasses too. A secondary cottage industry of Amazon sellers hocking black stickers, sized to cover the LED recording light, or offering to drill it out entirely, has sprung up online. This is all to enable people to record footage without letting others know they're doing so.
With the invasive potential of smart glasses to target women and post the footage online, companies like Meta are left with a clear stigma they'll have to shake before smart glasses can be seen as cool.
Prosecutors in Paris have also opened probes into smart glasses-related sexual harassment offenses, according to the French national newspaper Le Monde. I predict Australia won't be the only country to adopt legislation that restricts the sale or usage of smart glasses in 2027.

articles.title: Nintendo Switch 2 sales dropped by 41% from last year due to console's price increase — pressure to release more big games to make up for shortfall
articles.text:
Nintendo Switch 2 sales dropped by 41% from last year due to console's price increase — pressure to release more big games to make up for shortfall
Nintendo is going to need more games to convince gamers to buy the Switch 2.
Nintendo Switch 2 sales have dropped 41% in the second fiscal quarter compared to the same quarter last year, as reported by CNBC and as predicted by Kantan Games CEO Serkan Toto at the beginning of June, selling only 2.67 million units from July to September. Nintendo is still sticking to its forecast of 16.5 million units sold by the end of the fiscal quarter, but is under pressure from investors to release more big hits to sell more Switch 2 units to hit its goal.
In Japan’s second fiscal quarter running from July 1 to September 30, Nintendo increased the price for the Switch 2 in the US, Canada, and Japan after an initial price hike in Japan earlier this year. Serkan Toto, CEO of Kantan Games Inc., which tracks and analyzes the Japanese game industry, expected that the price increase would lead to a decrease in sales. Despite the prediction coming true, Nintendo is assuring its investors that it would hit its forecast of 16.5 million units sold by March 31, 2027, the end of Japan’s current fiscal year.
Toto also stated, “Nintendo’s only real blockbuster this fiscal year is the Ocarina of Time remake. It’s not enough to make investors happy, especially after the device is now as expensive as it is.” The remake, set to release tomorrow, disappointed many fans, with its visuals being uncanny and overly photorealistic, instead of being true to the original art style with updated audiovisuals. The game also seems to have limited offerings to expand on the original Ocarina of Time, even missing the more difficult Master Quest mode, which many veterans were looking forward to. Overall, the remake may not generate as much excitement as Nintendo expects, with fans viewing it as more of a reskin than a release worthy of the hype. This could potentially dampen the Switch 2 sales Nintendo was hoping the remake would drive, but we will have to see how well it performs after its release.
It also doesn’t help that Macronix, one of Nintendo’s ROM chip manufacturers, recently stopped ROM chip manufacturing to focus its capacity on high-demand NOR and NAND flash chips for AI data centers, even banking on the memory price hikes for short-term gain. Currently, Nintendo is pressured to release more big games to make the Switch 2 more attractive, with new Pokémon games planned for 2027 — Who knows, maybe Nintendo might cave in and finally accept Palworld onto its platform.

articles.title: Nvidia, Municipal Leaders Frame AI as Critical Urban Infrastructure - EE Times
articles.text:
BARCELONA, Spain — At the Smart City Expo World Congress, executives from Nvidia and municipal officials from Europe and the U.S. made the case for AI as an indispensable component of civic infrastructure.
With a keynote by Paolo Guglielmini, Nvidia’s VP for EMEA, and an executive panel moderated by Michael Lake, CEO of Leading Cities, the summit emphasized the need for local governments to establish centralized computing facilities—termed “AI factories”—to turn vast volumes of urban data into civic operational decisions, maintain sovereignty over sensitive municipal data, and retain technical talent rather than see it move to private technology centers.
Municipal data gap and architecture
In a keynote titled “From AI Factories to Intelligent Cities,” Guglielmini described what he called a structural bottleneck in modern municipal governance: the disparity between the raw data cities collect and the fraction they analyze to guide civic operations.
“Your organizations, your city’s municipalities, and regions have never had so much data available to you,” said Guglielmini, pointing to continuous streams from water utilities, air quality monitors, traffic sensors, mobile devices, GPS trackers, and satellite imagery. “But the gap between the data that’s available and the data that we use for decision-making has never been this great.”
To close that operational gap, Guglielmini proposed a five-layer architectural model for civic technology: energy, compute hardware, foundational infrastructure, software models, and end-user applications. He noted that while cities invest heavily in hardware, much of the economic value is created at the application level.
“Economic opportunity will happen where compute resides,” Guglielmini said. “Talent will stay where compute infrastructure is built. The lion’s share of startups created today are AI-native startups, and entrepreneurs and innovators will always follow where infrastructure is built.”
Addressing the technical friction within city halls, Guglielmini said legacy administrative systems often hinder modernization. “Very often, the organizations you are within have a lot of legacy,” Guglielmini said. “We have data that is nested. We have silos. We have applications built over tens of years. AI is perfect to build that layer on top that harnesses the power of data.”
From digital twins to language agents
To illustrate how localized computing can translate into municipal operations, Guglielmini detailed three distinct deployments across European regions.
In the Doubs department in eastern France, regional authorities built digital replicas of more than 500 public buildings, according to Guglielmini. Rather than relying solely on structural geometry, the digital mock-ups integrate real-time utility records, maintenance histories, and environmental metrics. “This is not about pure geometry,” Guglielmini said. “These are mock-ups that are enriched with data maintenance, data records, and utility records. Simulating cities and urban planning into the future has never become so affordable, so quick, and so valuable.”
In Palermo, Italy, municipal authorities established a center of excellence that uses a real-time AI model to process feeds from cameras and multiple types of sensors. The system combines urban monitoring with traffic management, emergency response dispatching, and municipal waste tracking. “Palermo went off and built a center of excellence that is incredibly capable of fusing sensor data from a multiplicity of facets and really shorten the time to emergency response,” Guglielmini explained.
In Barcelona, municipal technology developer 1 Million Bots deployed an agentic service platform built on “Laia,” a specialized language model developed at the Barcelona Supercomputing Center. The model was trained specifically to handle regional administrative procedures in Spanish and regional languages, including Catalan, Galician, and Basque.
“Laia is a model that is highly specialized and highly sovereign for the Spanish language, and for all the [languages] that are important to address the largest possible population of your citizens,” Guglielmini said. He emphasized that local hosting keeps public data secure: “The city is in control of the applications, in control of the data, and in control of the permitting and permissions of who gets to see that data.”
Moving from pilot projects to reality
Following the keynote, Michael Lake, president and chief executive of Leading Cities, convened an executive panel titled “By the City, for the City: Making AI Work.” Lake organized the discussion around three core principles: Purpose, Power, and Proof.
“Technology doesn’t fail because it’s bad,” Lake said. “Technologies and communities fail because the system that it needs to survive is not ready for it.”
Charbel Aoun, director of smart cities and spaces for EMEA at Nvidia, criticized municipalities’ tendency to treat AI as a series of disconnected software pilot projects rather than integrating them into their operations—a pattern panel members characterized as “death by a thousand pilots.”
“Most of the pilots end up being a lessons-learned paper,” Aoun said. “What we need to prove is the value and the adoption.”
Aoun argued that cities should treat computing capacity as foundational civic infrastructure, comparable to electrical grids or water lines. “AI is becoming critical infrastructure,” Aoun noted. “If we achieve that point, then we need to learn from the broadband mistake and from previous mistakes. Cities can own it, rent it, or partner, but they need an AI factory foundation.”
U.S. cities focus on productivity and public safety
Panel members from American cities described pragmatic approaches designed to establish public trust and streamline labor-intensive municipal tasks.
Mayor Keith A. James of West Palm Beach, Fla., said his administration chose public records processing as its first application. Municipal staff members handle extensive paperwork under strict legal timelines, making document retrieval a natural fit for automation.
“Cities tend to be very labor-intensive or paper-intensive,” James said. “You want to show the residents the AI working, and you want to begin with realistic applications. Our project involves public records requests. It helps our residents because we respond efficiently, and it takes some of the burden off our staff.”
In Tampa, Fla., Mayor Jane Castor said public safety departments have led municipal technology adoption because of immediate operational demands. Tampa recently deployed an automated drone response system linked directly to its real-time crime center, allowing aerial units to reach emergency scenes ahead of ground vehicles.
To prevent department silos, Tampa is also deploying “Iris,” a software platform that consolidates data from water quality, wastewater, solid waste, purchasing, and permitting into a single executive dashboard.
Castor emphasized that clear boundaries are vital to maintaining public confidence. “You have to share information with your community so that trust is there,” Castor said. “They shouldn’t feel like there’s a surveillance state in your community.”
European AI strategies in universities and communities
European municipal leaders highlighted frameworks that link technology deployment directly to academic institutions and geographic equity.
First Deputy Mayor Jakub Mazur of Wrocław, Poland, detailed how his administration replaced ad hoc software trials with a citywide strategy anchored by the Wrocław University of Science and Technology and its 25,000 students. The city deployed an AI-assisted enrollment system that handles 95% of school placements for local families, while encouraging technical graduates to remain in the regional economy.
Mazur stressed that decisions affecting citizens must remain accountable to elected officials, not automated systems.
“We need to own it because the city is responsible for data and the decision-making process,” Mazur stated. “We are democratically elected; we can be voted out. The algorithm cannot be voted out.”
For Rome, Italy, Deputy Mayor Valeria Baglio outlined a strategy focused on neighborhood-wide inclusion. Rather than concentrating digital investments in tourist-heavy central districts, Rome’s strategy extends digital public services across outer residential areas.
Rome’s initiative operates through “CTE Roma“, or Houses of Innovation, a municipal network linking city government, regional universities, startup incubators, and living labs. “We are working to bring digital services closer to residents across all districts, so that innovation isn’t just focused around central stations or downtown hubs,” Baglio said.
Building infrastructure for long-term value
To conclude his keynote, Guglielmini said that building municipal computing infrastructure doesn’t necessarily require a multi-gigawatt capital investment right away. He urged city officials to consider a modular rollout approach.
“Your AI journey can start from something very small—something portable and powerful,” Guglielmini said, noting that numerous European technology enterprises began operations using compact desktop supercomputing units. “Adding the right level of ambition is fundamental, but getting started with a use case that is really transformational for your communities and thinking about it in modular terms is fundamental to get going.”
Looking ahead, Guglielmini said he expects the next decade of urban technology to focus less on experimentation and more on deploying permanent, on-the-ground computing assets to support urban productivity and growth.
“Infrastructure build-out for the next 10 years is going to mean building intelligence that is at your fingertips to help you run your cities more effectively and economically,” Guglielmini said. “Focus on the use cases that are most transformational for where you are, bring together the right ecosystem, and look at the resources you have available to build compute capacity that serves your community.”

articles.title: Prévu pour durer 2 ans, il en aura tenu 22 : le télescope Swift de la NASA s’est désintégré dans l’atmosphère
articles.text:
Le télescope spatial Swift de la NASA a effectué sa rentrée atmosphérique mercredi 4 novembre à 13 h 39, heure de Paris, au-dessus du nord de l’île de Sumatra, en Indonésie, où il était alors 19 h 39. L’agence spatiale américaine l’a confirmé à partir des données de suivi de l’US Space Force. Le satellite d’environ 1 450 kg est retombé pile au milieu de la fenêtre de deux heures que l’armée américaine avait annoncée le matin même.
 Space-Track has confirmed that Swift has reentered Earth’s atmosphere on November 4, 12:39 UTC ± 1 min and has been registered as decayed.
See more details here: https://t.co/pRkdzNQUSj https://t.co/UXeSaVwdwo
— The Aerospace Corporation (@AerospaceCorp) November 4, 2026
« La NASA s’attendait à ce que la majeure partie du vaisseau se consume lors de son passage dans l’atmosphère, mais certains composants pourraient avoir survécu à la rentrée », précise l’agence. Avant la chute, elle évaluait à environ une chance sur 2 100 le risque qu’une personne soit blessée par un débris quelque part sur Terre, un niveau plus élevé que le seuil d’une chance sur 10 000 retenu par les règles américaines de limitation des débris spatiaux, mais qui reste faible. Comme l’orbite de Swift était peu inclinée, les éventuels fragments ne pouvaient retomber qu’entre 20,6 degrés de latitude sud et 20,6 degrés de latitude nord. Aucune victime n’a été signalée et aucun débris retrouvé au sol n’avait été rapporté jeudi.
Un sauvetage inédit qui a tourné court
Swift ne disposait d’aucun système de propulsion pour corriger son orbite. Pendant le maximum solaire, l’activité du Soleil a dilaté la haute atmosphère et augmenté le freinage du télescope, accélérant sa chute bien plus vite que prévu. Pour tenter de le sauver, la NASA avait signé un contrat de 30 millions de dollars avec la start-up Katalyst Space, dont le vaisseau robotique LINK a décollé le 3 juillet pour agripper Swift et le remonter sur une orbite plus haute. Fin juillet, LINK a perdu le contrôle de son orientation après la panne de deux de ses roues de réaction, et la NASA a abandonné l’opération le 19 août. « Dès le départ, c’était une mission à haut risque et à fort potentiel », a rappelé Shawn Domagal-Goldman, directeur de la division astrophysique de la NASA, cité par Aerospace Corporation.
Le télescope a malgré tout repris ses observations pendant quelques semaines. Le 20 octobre, descendu à 275 km d’altitude, il ne parvenait plus à compenser le freinage de l’atmosphère et a basculé en mode de sécurité. L’équipe de l’université d’État de Pennsylvanie, qui l’exploitait, a alors mis fin à ses opérations selon la NASA.
Une mission de deux ans qui en aura duré vingt-deux
Lancé le 20 novembre 2004 depuis Cap Canaveral, Swift devait à l’origine fonctionner deux ans pour étudier les sursauts gamma, les explosions les plus puissantes connues dans l’Univers. Sa force tenait à sa réactivité : il pouvait pointer ses télescopes vers une explosion fugace en une minute environ et alerter les observatoires du monde entier pour qu’ils prennent le relais.
En près de 22 ans, il a observé plus de 2 000 sursauts gamma et plus de 1 400 supernovae, et ses données ont nourri environ 7 000 publications scientifiques, selon la NASA. L’agence le décrit comme un « outil polyvalent pour explorer l’Univers », qui a aussi permis d’étudier des galaxies alimentées par des trous noirs supermassifs, des comètes ou des astéroïdes du système solaire. Sa construction, son lancement et son exploitation auraient coûté au total environ 500 millions de dollars en tenant compte de l’inflation.

articles.title: Sans attendre le Black Friday, le compresseur Xiaomi Mijia 2D est à 30,94 € pour le 11.11
articles.text:
Regonfler un pneu de vélo, de moto ou de voiture sans dépendre d’une station, c’est surtout savoir s’arrêter à la bonne pression. Le compresseur Xiaomi Mijia 2D, qui coupe tout seul à la valeur choisie, est à 30,94 € sur AliExpress : nous l’avions vu moins cher cet été, et nous vous disons pour quel usage il vaut ce prix.
Le Xiaomi Mijia 2D est un compresseur d’air sans fil au format compact, pensé pour regonfler les pneus d’une voiture, d’une moto, d’un vélo ou d’une trottinette, et même des ballons. Sa batterie de 2000 mAh se recharge en USB-C, ce qui évite de dépendre de la prise 12 V du véhicule. AliExpress affiche le compresseur Xiaomi Mijia 2D à 30,94 € au lieu de 45,91 €, soit près de 15 € de moins, et le code CLU03 est à saisir au moment de payer.
L’offre s’adresse d’abord à celles et ceux qui veulent un appareil de dépannage à garder dans le coffre ou dans un sac, plutôt qu’un outil d’atelier.
Le compresseur Xiaomi Mijia 2D est affiché à 30,94 € au lieu de 45,91 € sur AliExpress, avec le code CLU03 à renseigner lors de la commande.
Pourquoi choisir le Xiaomi Mijia 2D ?
- Il s’arrête à la pression voulue : Vous réglez la valeur souhaitée, le compresseur gonfle puis coupe seul une fois la cible atteinte. Plus besoin de surveiller l’écran.
- Six modes préréglés : Voiture, moto, vélo ou ballon disposent chacun d’un réglage, avec un mode dédié aux trottinettes électriques. Passer d’un équipement à l’autre ne demande pas de tout reparamétrer.
- Jusqu’à 150 psi, mesure à ±1 psi annoncée : La pression maximale, soit environ 10,3 bar, couvre un pneu de voiture comme celui d’un vélo de route, gonflé bien plus fort. La précision annoncée compte surtout sur les pneus fins de vélo.
Du coffre de la voiture au garage à vélos
Au quotidien, l’intérêt du Mijia 2D tient à l’association d’un écran numérique et de l’arrêt automatique. Vous fixez l’embout sur la valve grâce à l’adaptateur à connexion rapide, vous choisissez le mode, et l’appareil s’occupe du reste. La lampe LED intégrée aide à trouver la valve à la tombée de la nuit, sur un parking ou au bord d’une route. Le port USB-C permet de le recharger avec le chargeur de votre téléphone.
Il convient aux cyclistes qui contrôlent leur pression avant chaque sortie, aux motards, et aux automobilistes qui veulent compléter un pneu un peu bas sans chercher une station. En revanche, sa batterie de 2000 mAh le destine à un dépannage occasionnel plutôt qu’à un usage professionnel intensif, comme nous le relevions lors de notre précédente offre. Si vous devez souvent remettre en pression plusieurs gros pneus à la suite, un compresseur branché sur la voiture vous évitera de surveiller la batterie.
Face au Compressor 2 et aux autres solutions
Sur le papier, le Mijia 2D reprend les grandes lignes du Xiaomi Portable Electric Air Compressor 2 que nous avons souvent relayé : même pression maximale de 150 psi, même batterie de 2000 mAh, six modes préréglés et éclairage LED. Nous n’avons en revanche pas pu vérifier son autonomie en nombre de pneus pour cette version, là où celle du Compressor 2 était annoncée jusqu’à dix. Face à une pompe à pied, il apporte la mesure numérique et l’arrêt à la bonne valeur ; face à un compresseur 12 V, il gagne en liberté ce qu’il perd en endurance. Son vrai rival reste donc le Compressor 2, à comparer au prix du jour.
✅ Les points forts
- Arrêt automatique à la pression choisie
- Six modes préréglés, dont un pour les trottinettes
- Recharge en USB-C, sans câble propriétaire
- Lampe LED pour les contrôles de nuit
- Adaptateur de valve à connexion rapide
❌ Les limites
- Batterie de 2000 mAh pensée pour le dépannage, pas pour enchaîner les gonflages
- Autonomie en nombre de pneus non vérifiée pour cette version
- Déjà vu moins cher : 21,31 € en août
- Vendu sur AliExpress : délai de livraison à contrôler sur la fiche
Avant de valider votre panier, vérifiez que le Xiaomi Mijia 2D s’affiche toujours à 30,94 € sur AliExpress et pensez à saisir le code CLU03.
À 30,94 €, le Xiaomi Mijia 2D reste un achat cohérent pour qui veut un gonfleur autonome capable de s’arrêter seul à la bonne pression. Il couvre la voiture, la moto, le vélo et les loisirs avec un seul appareil. Ce n’est toutefois pas son plus bas prix : en août, nous l’avions repéré à 21,31 € chez AliExpress. Le prix barré de 45,91 € est donc à lire comme une référence du vendeur plutôt que comme son tarif courant.
Si vous n’avez aucun gonfleur et que vos pneus perdent régulièrement de la pression, l’offre mérite d’être examinée sans attendre le Black Friday, dont rien ne garantit qu’il fera mieux. Si vous possédez déjà un Compressor 2 en état de marche, le remplacer n’a guère de sens : les deux fiches se ressemblent trop. Pour un usage de dépannage, sa fiche coche les cases qui comptent : mesure, arrêt automatique et éclairage.
