articles.title: Pour 40 € de plus, ce pack Switch 2 inclut le remake de Zelda: Ocarina of Time
articles.text:
Vingt-huit ans après sa sortie sur Nintendo 64, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time revient. Nintendo a annoncé ce remake lors du Nintendo Direct du 9 juin 2026, et le jeu sort ce jeudi 5 novembre, uniquement sur Switch 2. Si vous avez encore la première Switch, vous ne pourrez pas y jouer. Dans notre test, Zelda: Ocarina of Time obtient la note maximale, 10/10.
Le jour même de la sortie, Joybuy, le site de vente en ligne du géant chinois JD.com, vend le pack Nintendo Switch 2 et The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time à 469,99 € au lieu de 489,98 €. Comme Joybuy vend la console seule 429,99 €, le remake de Zelda vous revient à 40 €.
Le prix public conseillé de la console est de 499,99 € depuis le 1er septembre 2026, contre 469,99 € à son lancement. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time est vendu 69,99 €, soit 569,98 € pour l’ensemble. C’est 100 € de plus que le tarif de Joybuy.
Que vaut la Switch 2 avec le remake d’Ocarina of Time ?
La Switch 2 reprend le principe de la première Switch : une console hybride qui se joue en mode portable ou branchée sur un téléviseur via sa station d’accueil. Elle embarque un écran LCD de 7,9 pouces en 1080p, qui peut monter jusqu’à 120 Hz. Elle a 256 Go de stockage et affiche jusqu’à la 4K une fois branchée à la télévision. Les Joy-Con 2 s’aimantent sur les côtés et peuvent aussi servir de souris. L’écran fait l’impasse sur l’OLED : les noirs sont moins profonds que sur la Switch OLED.
Côté jeu, Nintendo a refait Ocarina of Time de zéro, avec de nouveaux graphismes, une bande-son retravaillée et une jouabilité modernisée. Eiji Aonuma, qui avait travaillé sur l’original, produit le remake. Pour la carte d’Hyrule, Nintendo a même rappelé l’artiste qui l’avait dessinée sur Nintendo 64. Le micro intégré de la Switch 2 sert enfin à quelque chose : vous pouvez jouer les mélodies de l’ocarina avec les boutons, ou les fredonner directement dans la console.
À ce prix, le pack Switch 2 et Ocarina of Time est-il une bonne affaire ?
Avec 19,99 € d’économie, ce pack ne sera pas la promotion de l’année. Il a toutefois un autre avantage : il arrive pile le jour de la sortie du jeu, alors que les réductions sur les nouveautés Nintendo sont particulièrement rares. Si vous attendiez un titre fort pour franchir le pas et acheter une Switch 2, Ocarina of Time pourrait bien vous convaincre : le jeu a décroché la note maximale dans notre test. Nintendo a également choisi une période stratégique pour cette sortie, à quelques semaines seulement de Noël.
L’offre reste donc intéressante, surtout si vous comptiez acheter les deux produits séparément. Vous jouez au remake dès sa sortie, pour 40 € de plus que la console seule. Les 19,99 € économisés (100 € sur le prix public conseillé) ne sont pas négligeables, d’autant que le pack permet de s’équiper en une seule fois, juste avant les fêtes de fin d’année.
Attention à ne pas confondre ce pack avec la Switch 2 édition Zelda, sortie le 29 octobre pour les 40 ans de la saga. Malgré l’intitulé employé par certaines enseignes, cette console collector ne contient pas le jeu, qu’il faut acheter à part.

articles.title: Groundcover automates Kubernetes sizing. Engineers set the bounds.
articles.text:
Groundcover automates Kubernetes sizing. Engineers set the bounds.
On Tuesday, groundcover launched Autonomous Infrastructure in beta to continuously adjust CPU and memory requests for Kubernetes (K8s) Deployments based on production data.
Built on technology from Wand, the K8s resource optimization platform groundcover acquired in September, the beta uses data already collected from groundcover’s eBPF sensor to inform resource allocation decisions, while giving engineers a direct view into how those decisions could affect infrastructure costs and workload performance.
Shahar Azulay, CEO and co-founder of groundcover, tells The New Stack about the balance the company is trying to get right: “The goal isn’t simply to reduce resource requests as much as possible. It’s to find the right balance between efficiency and stability across the entire environment.”
That can mean reducing requests for workloads consuming far less than they’ve been allocated, but it can also mean increasing requests when a workload needs additional resources to operate reliably. The objective is not simply a smaller infrastructure footprint. It’s an environment that continuously receives the resources it needs, without paying for capacity it doesn’t.
How to get there? Azulay says teams need “a continuous feedback loop that uses real production telemetry to identify when workloads are over- or under-provisioned and safely adjust them.”
Does nobody know a good way to right-size K8s workloads?
It’s not for lack of trying. There are already a lot of different ways to tackle the burden of right-sizing K8s workloads.
For example, scheduled rightsizing applies changes at chosen intervals, so it may not respond between scheduled updates. In-place resizing can change resources on running pods, although some changes require container restarts. Automated tools can also generate and apply recommendations within policies engineers set.
When asked why he thinks K8s rightsizing continues to trip people up, Azulay tells The New Stack the challenge lies in striking the right balance between cost efficiency and application stability:
“Resource requests are typically set at deployment time, when teams are making their best estimates before a workload has experienced real-world production traffic,” he explains. “The challenge is that workloads are constantly changing, but resource configurations often aren’t.”
“The challenge is that workloads are constantly changing, but resource configurations often aren’t.”
After initial deployment, teams may simply let sleeping workloads lie, i.e., they don’t revisit original resource requests for reconfiguration. While workloads may keep spinning along just fine, this approach means teams risk unknowingly leaving them over- or under-provisioned—with costly consequences.
For organizations running hundreds or thousands of workloads, keeping those configurations accurate becomes an ongoing engineering task. Teams must analyze utilization, identify opportunities, test new settings, and revisit them as traffic and application behavior change. Even with the expertise, they may not have the time to do it continuously.
Azulay describes over-provisioning as “the safer choice because nobody wants to risk performance issues or outages.” But that extra peace of mind can come with unnecessary infrastructure costs; in a 2025 study published in Applied Sciences, researchers found that optimizing K8s resource allocation improved a combined performance-and-cost score by approximately 50% compared to the conventional maximum resource allocation approach.
Under-provisioning carries different risks. Requests help Kubernetes schedule pods, and CPU requests influence how CPU time is shared under contention; setting them too low can leave workloads short of CPU time. Limits work differently: CPU limits cause throttling, while exceeding a memory limit can trigger an out-of-memory (OOM) kill. Low memory requests can also increase eviction risk when a node is under memory pressure.
There’s also a relationship between workload requests and the cost of the cluster itself. Node autoscalers such as Karpenter can provision or remove nodes based on the resources workloads request, but they don’t determine whether those requests accurately reflect what each application needs. If workloads consistently request too much, the autoscaler may maintain more capacity than necessary. Right-sizing those requests gives the node autoscaler a more accurate basis for allocating infrastructure.
What if the answer to done-right right-sizing is sitting in your production data?
Groundcover thinks so. That’s why its new Autonomous Infrastructure draws on the groundcover eBPF sensor, which is already collecting telemetry across applications and infrastructure. The beta uses that production history to recommend CPU and memory requests for Kubernetes Deployments. Brand-new Deployments remain in a learning state until enough data is available.
But the approach isn’t simply to observe a spike in resource consumption and increase requests afterward. By the time a reactive system responds, the performance impact may already have occurred. Instead, groundcover’s optimization engine analyzes workload behavior over time, including usage patterns and resource contention, to anticipate capacity requirements and prepare workloads for expected changes in demand.
That distinction matters for workloads with recurring traffic spikes. The goal is to have enough resources available when demand arrives, without permanently allocating for peak consumption.
When engineers open the beta, they get a direct view of how much CPU and memory each workload requests versus what it uses, plus the number of under-provisioned workloads and estimated monthly savings if they apply changes. Groundcover’s product page says dollar estimates use default list prices that administrators can adjust with their own prices and discounts. These estimates do not establish that a cloud bill will fall by the same amount; realizing savings also depends on whether freed capacity lets teams reduce billed infrastructure.
An important part of the experience is that customers can see those opportunities before enabling autonomous optimization. Because groundcover already collects the necessary telemetry, existing customers can evaluate potential savings without deploying a separate monitoring agent or conducting another data-collection exercise. They can inspect recommendations, understand their expected impact, and decide which workloads, if any, to optimize.
Rather than setting resource requests at deployment time and letting them run on autopilot, engineers can use Autonomous Infrastructure to put real-time telemetry to work and continuously adjust resources based on production behavior. And because groundcover already collects the necessary telemetry, teams running a supported sensor version don’t need a separate agent or a new data-collection period for existing Deployments with sufficient history.
Why the answer lies in the context
When asked how real-time production data can improve K8s right-sizing, Azulay tells The New Stack it comes down to understanding how workloads affect one another in production.
While some resource optimization tools size each workload on its own, he claims that approach doesn’t tell the whole story.
“Kubernetes workloads don’t operate in isolation. They share nodes, compete for available resources, and can directly affect one another’s performance.”
Instead, to find the optimal balance between efficiency and stability, Azulay says engineers need tools that consider the entire environment:
“Kubernetes workloads don’t operate in isolation. They share nodes, compete for available resources, and can directly affect one another’s performance.”
For example, lowering CPU requests changes how a workload shares CPU under contention and can let the scheduler pack more workloads onto a node. A recommendation based only on one workload’s usage can therefore miss contention effects across the node.
This is one limitation of approaches that rely primarily on historical utilization for each workload. Two applications with similar CPU consumption may require different resource allocations depending on their traffic patterns, neighboring workloads, and the contention they experience. Applying the same sizing formula to both can leave one over-provisioned and the other vulnerable to performance problems.
To right-size each workload without bruising others, Azulay tells The New Stack resource optimization tools must not only evaluate real-time resource consumption against what’s being requested but consider the traffic patterns, workload behavior, and available resources across the node:
“True optimization requires understanding both individual workload behavior and the broader environment in which those workloads operate.”
Azulay says Autonomous Infrastructure uses that broader context. Leaning on Wand’s optimization engine, the beta uses node-level contention to inform right-sizing recommendations and make adjustments that consider the entire environment.
“It also looks beyond application containers to account for injected sidecars, such as Istio, Linkerd and Vault agents, which can be overlooked sources of resource waste,” Azulay says.
The integration with groundcover also connects resource optimization to the observability workflows engineers already use. Rather than receiving an isolated recommendation from a separate optimization tool, engineers can investigate workload behavior using the logs, traces, metrics, and infrastructure context available in the same platform. That helps them understand why a change was recommended and evaluate its impact on the environment.
The result is a connection between observing infrastructure and acting on what the data reveals. Production telemetry informs optimization decisions, and engineers can use that same observability context to understand what happens afterward.
But are engineers ready to automate right-sizing?
Letting a tool like Autonomous Infrastructure take over K8s right-sizing can sound like a convenient solution. As Azulay tells The New Stack, many teams simply don’t get around to reconfiguring resource requests because of time and resource constraints — and engineers aren’t always sure the changes will improve efficiency without impacting stability.
But that doesn’t necessarily mean engineers are ready to go all in on automated right-sizing, at least for now. In Kube.today’s 2025 community poll on Kubernetes resource management, 56.5% of respondents selected manual tools such as kubectl and dashboards as their primary approach. That result reflects the poll’s respondents, not Kubernetes practitioners as a whole.
Groundcover’s own research, administered by Atomik Research, underlines engineers’ uncertainty about going fully autonomous. In the survey of 500 U.S. technology professionals, 87% say AI or automation is already integrated into observability workflows, but only one-third (34%) call it “fully operational and trusted.”
For those hesitant to hand over the reins for resource optimization, groundcover’s beta might offer some relief.
Per groundcover, Autonomous Infrastructure is “opt-in at every level.” By default, automation is off; groundcover’s launch blog describes opting in a cluster and then enabling individual Deployments.
While the beta may use production telemetry to autonomously adjust resource requests, engineers still set the parameters, defining minimum and maximum bounds for CPU and memory requests. The beta changes requests only, leaving limits unchanged. A declared limit caps the recommendation; a workload constrained by that limit appears as “Bounded.” Groundcover says every policy change is versioned and an audit log records who assigned each workload to a policy and when. A resource used by an HPA or KEDA utilization-based autoscaler is left unchanged. The beta uses in-place resizing when possible and falls back to a rollout when necessary.
For engineers who may be wary of giving a resource optimization tool full access to decide and execute K8s right-sizing, these constraints can ease the transition. Plus, they can easily keep a pulse on what the beta is doing, with groundcover’s view showing how many workloads are managed autonomously in each cluster and namespace.
“…engineers aren’t being asked to trust a black box.”
Perhaps more importantly, engineers aren’t being asked to trust a black box. They can review the reasoning behind recommendations, inspect the expected effects, and choose precisely where to enable autonomous changes. The automation is designed to remain understandable and reversible.
Who will get right-sizing right?
Groundcover says the Autonomous Infrastructure beta is available at no additional cost to its customers running the groundcover sensor on Kubernetes, with a supported sensor version required. The beta covers Deployments and their sidecars; support for other workload kinds is on the roadmap. The company is inviting design partners and plans demonstrations at booth #111 during KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America, Nov. 9–12, 2026, in Salt Lake City.
The question for the next generation of Kubernetes optimization tools may be less about how aggressively they can reduce resource requests and more about how intelligently they can manage them. That means anticipating demand, accounting for contention across the environment, and making changes engineers can understand and trust.
For groundcover, bringing optimization into the same platform that collects and analyzes production telemetry is a step toward that model: infrastructure that doesn’t just report what’s happening, but uses that understanding to continuously improve how it runs.

articles.title: Reddit testet Search Ads, baut neue Feeds ein und plant eine Login-Pflicht – was dahintersteckt
articles.text:
Neue Feeds, Login-Pläne, Search Ads: Warum Reddit gerade so viel an seiner Plattform verändert
Eine Community für Communitys oder doch eine Suchmaschine? Reddit möchte beides sein und wird derzeit einem großen Wandel unterzogen. Schon 2025 erklärte CEO Steve Huffman, Reddit zu einer „Go-to-Suchmaschine“ machen zu wollen. Mit Features wie einer Suchleiste im Home-Feed, Related Answers unter Posts und den KI-gestützten Reddit Answers wurde diesem Vorhaben schon Rechnung getragen. Huffmann sagte dazu vergangenes Jahr:
Reddit is one of the few platforms positioned to become a true search destination. We offer something special: a breadth of conversations and knowledge you can’t find anywhere else. Every week, hundreds of millions of people come to Reddit looking for advice, and we’re turning more of that intent into active users of Reddit’s native search […].
Reddit zählt derzeit 515 Millionen wöchentlich aktive User. Und nach eigenen Angaben gibt die Hälfte der User an, dass Reddit ihnen bei der Entdeckung neuer Dinge hilft. Immerhin hat Reddit auch über 100.000 aktive Communitys und mehr als 27 Milliarden Posts und Kommentare zu bieten. Während die Plattform die Search-Erfahrung sowie die grundlegende Plattformnutzung für die User weiter ausbaut, soll Werbung in der Suche künftig zur Reddit-Experience gehören. Die ersten Tests laufen schon und geben Advertisern Hoffnung. Reddit selbst könnte damit das eigene Geschäft ankurbeln, nachdem es dafür zuletzt kleine Dämpfer gegeben hat.
Wo die User auf Reddit Search Ads sehen
In einem Blog-Beitrag erklärt Reddit, dass neuerdings Search Ads direkt zwischen den Suchergebnissen auf der Plattform getestet werden. Ausgewählte Advertiser haben Zugriff auf die Option. Eine Ausweitung ist geplant, aber noch nicht terminiert.
Mit den neuen Search-Ads können Advertiser basierend auf bestehenden Targeting-Optionen User unmittelbar auf Suchergebnisseiten erreichen – wie diese es von Google und inzwischen auch von ChatGPT gewohnt sind. Dabei erscheinen die Reddit-Search-Ads auf Basis verschiedener Faktoren. Im Zentrum steht die kontextuelle Relevanz zur Suchanfrage, quasi wie bei einer Keyword- oder Keyphrase-Match-Funktion. Reddit liefert zwei Beispiele:
- Wer nach einer Espresso-Station (Tamperstation) sucht, könnte Ads zu Espressomaschinen, zu Tassen oder auch zu Espresso- oder Kaffeebohnen erhalten.
- Wer nach einem Homeoffice-Set-up sucht, könnte Ads für Monitore, Tische oder Bürostühle erhalten.
Die ausgespielten Ads erscheinen mitten zwischen organischen Suchergebnissen auf der Ergebnisseite. Sie zeigen ein Visual, einen CTA‑Button und ein Favicon sowie die Domain und den Namen des Advertisers. Ein Label markiert die Werbung, wenngleich dieses klein im Header anstelle eines Veröffentlichungszeitpunkts steht.
Search-Ads könnten Reddit dabei helfen, das eigene Werbegeschäft auf Basis der umfassenden Nutzung – immer stieg die Zahl der wöchentlich aktiven User im Jahresvergleich um 16 Prozent – zu fördern. Im dritten Quartal 2026 stieg der Werbeumsatz year over year um 54 Prozent auf 847 Millionen US-Dollar an (bei 895 Millionen Gesamtumsatz). Der Gewinn des Unternehmens stieg sogar um 74 Prozent auf 283 Millionen US-Dollar an.
Und doch reagierte die Börse auf die Quartalszahlen mit einem Kurseinbruch. Denn Reddit konnte die Erwartungen bei den User-Zahlen nicht erfüllen und der Ausblick auf das vierte Quartal sorgt ebenfalls für Unmut bei Anleger:innen, weil die Prognosen der Analyst:innen womöglich nicht eintreffen werden. Da kommen große Veränderungen an der Plattform gelegen, um langfristig doch noch mehr User und Advertiser für sich gewinnen zu können.
Neben Search Ads: Neue Feeds und Login-Zwang als maßgebliche Änderungen
Reddit befindet sich nicht nur aufgrund der immer neuen KI-Funktionen auf der Plattform im Wandel. Die Community für Communitys möchte sich für Advertiser, aber auch User attraktiver denn je darstellen. Deshalb führte Reddit kürzlich einen „For You“- und einen „Following“-Feed für mehr Kontrolle über das eigene Plattformerlebnis ein. Damit orientiert sich die Plattform an Tiktok und Instagram. Zuletzt wurden außerdem Video- und Audioversionen von Reddit-Posts getestet, um sich dem durch Tiktoks und Reels geprägten Rezeptionsverhalten anzunähern.
Und damit die User auf Reddit wirklich als aktive User verzeichnet sind, plant das Unternehmen laut Axios eine Login-Pflicht, um umfassende Inhalte rezipieren zu können. Das soll das unerlaubte Content-Scraping einschränken, dem User-Wachstum helfen, aber ebenso das Werbegeschäft stärken. Laut Reddit-COO Jen Wong ist die Aktivität angemeldeter User etwa fünfmal so hoch wie die von Usern ohne Login. Sie generieren dadurch mehr Werbeeinblendungen und sind für das Unternehmen wirtschaftlich besonders wertvoll. Wie Reddit im aktuellen Quartalsbericht erklärt, entfallen schon mehr als 80 Prozent der Monetarisierung auf die App und angemeldete User. Durch die geplanten Einschränkungen könnte Reddit künftig mehr Besucher:innen zur Anmeldung bewegen und deren Interessen für personalisierte Empfehlungen und gezieltere Werbung nutzen. Solch eine Login-Notwendigkeit soll zuerst in den USA kommen.
Mit einem spezifischen Alleinstellungsmerkmal möchte sich Reddit derweil von anderen Plattformen und Suchdiensten unterscheiden. Kevin Klieber, Head of Mid-Market Sales DACH bei Reddit, erklärte gegenüber OnlineMarketing.de:
KI, Suchmaschinen und soziale Plattformen liefern heute unglaublich gute Antworten. Doch Menschen suchen inzwischen nach etwas anderem: Sicherheit für ihre Entscheidungen durch die Erfahrungen anderer Menschen. Genau deshalb ist Reddit heute so relevant. […] Je stärker das Internet von Algorithmen, KI-generierten Inhalten und kuratierten Feeds geprägt wird, desto wertvoller werden authentische Gespräche zwischen echten Menschen.
Der Artikel stammt von Niklas Lewanczik aus der OnlineMarketing.de-Redaktion und wird im Rahmen einer Content-Kooperation auf t3n veröffentlicht.

articles.title: Nigeria’s Mytherapist wants to close the gap between needing therapy and getting it - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Nigerian startup Mytherapist is helping people find qualified therapists, book appointments and attend sessions via video, audio or chat, while also offering tools to support their wellbeing between sessions.
Founded in 2021 by Oluwaseun Raphael Afolayan and Dedoyin Ajayi, Mytherapist launched a pilot in October 2022 before going public and beginning paid therapy bookings in January 2023.
“The idea came from the difficulty of finding reliable, affordable support during the pandemic and the aftermath of the EndSARS protests. That experience affected me and people around me,” Afolayan told Disrupt Africa.
Mytherapist is built around what Afolayan describes as the practical questions people face when looking for help. “Who should I speak to? What will it cost? When are they available? How do I fit a session into my day?” he said.
“We saw a gap between deciding you need support and actually receiving it. Someone may be willing to try therapy but still struggle to identify a suitable professional, understand the price or arrange an appointment.”
Alongside therapy sessions, the platform offers mood tracking, journaling, meditation and breathing exercises. “These give users ways to reflect and support their everyday wellbeing alongside professional care,” said Afolayan.
The startup serves individuals and couples, and also offers access pathways through employers and health maintenance organisations (HMOs).
“Our approach combines therapist discovery, booking and remote sessions with tools people can use between appointments. We also now offer routes through employers and HMOs, so access does not depend entirely on someone paying out of pocket,” he said.
Mytherapist makes money by taking a commission on therapy sessions booked through the platform. It also offers paid corporate wellbeing services and Prime, an optional membership, which provides additional features and benefits.
Traction has been solid. The startup has more than 25,000 users and over 4,000 completed paid bookings, and has onboarded more than 120 therapists, with over 90 active. Afolayan, however, was careful to put those figures in context.
“Those measures represent different things. Users are not the same as paying clients, and bookings are not the same as completed sessions,” he said. “The next stage is improving how reliably people move from signing up to receiving care and returning when they need further support.”
The startup was initially bootstrapped, and in 2024 received a US$5,000 grant from 54Collective, as well as around US$7,500 in combined grants from Wema Bank Nigeria, ABC Health and FATE Foundation. Afolayan cited the launch of paid bookings, the introduction of couples sessions and corporate wellness services, and the addition of Prime as key milestones.
Nigeria remains Mytherapist.ng’s core market, though it has seen users access the platform from abroad.
“We distinguish that cross-border usage from establishing a local operation in another country,” said Afolayan.
“Our priority is to strengthen the care experience and distribution in Nigeria. Any expansion needs suitable professionals, workable payments and dependable delivery, and we’re currently working on expanding properly, while still maintaining low operational costs, with the help of Paystack and the Startbutton Africa team.”

articles.title: Blinkit Ambulance to charge Rs 2,500 for non-emergency cases
articles.text:
Blinkit Ambulance to charge Rs 2,500 for non-emergency cases
Zomato founder Deepinder Goyal noted that a growing share of bookings for its free ambulance service were for routine checkups, hospital visits and hospital-to-home transfers.
Blinkit Ambulance, the free service from the quick commerce company, will now start charging Rs 2,500 for non-emergency transfers.
“Emergency transfers–free, as always. Non-emergency transfers–₹2,500, charged after the trip. Broadly in line with what private ambulances charge. This money goes to the Eternal Foundation, which runs these ambulances and will help us scale them even further,” Zomato founder Deepinder Goyal said in a post on X.
Goyal noted that Blinkit Ambulance was started as a spirit of service, and in the last two years, it has served around 20,000 emergency cases and more than 42,000 cases in total. “We haven't charged a single rupee for any of them. And we want to keep it that way,” he remarked.
The reason for the change is that a growing share of bookings were for routine checkups, hospital visits and hospital-to-home transfers, the post noted. As Goyal remarked that every such booking requires a fully equipped emergency ambulance with paramedics.
“We hope that this charge will dramatically drop the usage of our Ambulances for non-emergency cases. 10-minute ambulances have saved and can save thousands of lives, and we need to keep them available for emergencies that need them the most,” Goyal said.
He also highlighted the challenge faced in providing free ambulance services is the availability of paramedics. However, he further added that they are planning to introduce Blinkit Ambulance to all major cities in the country in the next 2-4 years.

articles.title: Plus de 80 Xiaomi, Redmi et POCO passent à Android 17 : la liste et les dates de la mise à jour
articles.text:
Xiaomi a officialisé cette semaine le calendrier mondial d’HyperOS 4, sa nouvelle interface bâtie sur Android 17. Plus de 80 téléphones et tablettes, siglés Xiaomi, Redmi ou POCO, recevront la version stable d’ici à la fin décembre. Le constructeur échelonne la distribution sur deux mois, du haut du catalogue vers les générations installées.
Votre appareil ouvre-t-il le bal ?
La fournée de novembre rassemble les gammes les plus récentes : séries Xiaomi 17 et 17T, Xiaomi 15, familles Redmi Note 17 et Redmi Note 15, Redmi 17, POCO F8, X8 et M8, entre autres références. Les tablettes Xiaomi Pad 8 sont du premier voyage. L’essentiel des vitrines récentes du constructeur est donc servi d’entrée ; le pliant MIX Flip attendra, lui, la dernière vague.
La mi-novembre enchaîne avec les Xiaomi 15T, les POCO F9, F7 et X7, puis un plein de tablettes : Xiaomi Pad 7 et Pad Mini, Redmi Pad 2, POCO Pad X1 et Pad M1. Les ardoises avancent donc au même tempo que les téléphones, sans vague dédiée en fin de parcours.
Lire aussi : Samsung One UI 9 (Android 17) : une première liste des appareils qui pourraient en profiter
Ces échéances restent des dates de lancement du déploiement : rien ne garantit l’installation le jour même. La diffusion se fait par lots, à un rythme qui varie d’un pays à l’autre, si bien qu’un appareil servi ailleurs peut patienter plusieurs semaines sur un autre marché. Cette distribution par paliers sert d’abord un petit groupe de téléphones avant de s’élargir, une méthode qui permet au constructeur de suspendre la mise à jour en cas de pépin. Sur un modèle éligible, elle se signale par la voie habituelle, dans les réglages du téléphone ; les impatients pourront aussi forcer la recherche de mise à jour depuis ce même menu.
Et si votre téléphone attend décembre ?
La troisième vague, calée sur décembre, ramasse les générations précédentes : Xiaomi 14, 14T, 13 et 13T, MIX Flip, familles Redmi Note 14, Redmi 14S et A7 Pro, POCO F6, X6 Pro et M7, entre autres. Pour les possesseurs de ces modèles, l’attente se compte donc en semaines ; les Xiaomi 13 et les POCO F6, plusieurs générations au compteur, restent ainsi dans la boucle des grandes mises à jour. Les appareils antérieurs à ces gammes ne figurent, eux, dans aucune des trois vagues publiées, et aucune annonce ne les concerne à ce stade.
Android 17 occupe par ailleurs l’automne bien au-delà de Xiaomi. Google a resserré cette année son contrôle sur cette version, au point de faire crier à l’étouffement des systèmes alternatifs comme GrapheneOS. À l’autre bout du spectre, LineageOS 24 installe ce même Android 17 sur des millions de smartphones abandonnés par leurs constructeurs. Entre les deux, les surcouches officielles comme HyperOS 4 restent la voie qui n’exige aucune manipulation.

articles.title: Diana, nómada digital en una furgoneta camperizada de 12m²: “Está mucho mejor equipada que una habitación. No pago ni electricidad ni agua”
articles.text:
Diana ha cambiado su piso por una autocaravana de 12 metros cuadrados. Y en ella ha trasladado toda su casa. “Mi caravana está mucho más equipada que una habitación de alquiler”, afirma. “No pago alquiler, ni luz ni agua”, añade Diana (@soyailenx), que comparte su día a día en redes sociales. Así es como vive esta toledana.
Le permite ser nómada. Además de esto, también puede ahorrar en algunas facturas.
Antes de instalarse en ella había comprado una furgoneta con la intención de camperizarla. Finalmente, la vendió y utilizó ese dinero para comprar una autocaravana de segunda mano. Por tanto, el vehículo en el que vive es distinto de aquella furgoneta con la que había empezado a preparar su vida sobre ruedas.
Trabajar mientras cambia de lugar
Es cantante de orquesta. Y eso implica ir de fiesta en fiesta de los pueblos. Por ello encaja muy bien que tenga su casa en una autocaravana.
Además, ha comentado que quiere buscar una profesión que pueda hacer de manera remota. También quiere monetizar sus redes sociales.
Lo que quería evitar era tener que aglutinar todos los viajes en los días libres. Veía a gente de su entorno quejándose de la rutina diaria. Estaban esperando a que llegaran las dos o tres semanas de vacaciones que tienen cada año. Quería conocer nuevos sitios. Pero sin estar todo el año esperando a ese momento.
Por otro lado, tiene la ventaja de que no tiene que volver a su piso habitual.
Vivir así también exige organizar tareas que en un piso se resuelven de otra manera. Diana tiene que planificar dónde lavar la ropa y cómo gestionar los depósitos de agua del vehículo. Para encontrar los lugares que necesita utiliza aplicaciones gratuitas y se organiza por semanas. Son cuestiones que debe tener presentes mientras se desplaza: llevar la casa consigo también significa ocuparse de sus suministros y de las tareas domésticas durante el viaje.
Dejar de pagar facturas también exige una inversión
Ha supuesto un gran coste inicial. Para comprar una autocaravana equipada hay que desembolsar cierta cantidad de dinero. Incluso podría haber comprado un piso en un pueblo con ese dinero. Sin embargo, este no ha sido el factor que más haya influido en su decisión.
Lo que realmente le interesaba era la movilidad. Que no quedara atada a un sitio.
Aunque parezca que no tiene facturas, no podemos saber exactamente cuál es el ahorro que tiene. No conocemos en detalle todo su presupuesto. No sabemos cuáles eran sus gastos antes y ahora, ni tenemos forma de saber cómo afecta a su balance la compra de la autocaravana.

articles.title: MediaMarkt agota la solución para instalar los 212 GB de 'GTA VI' en Xbox Series sin borrar otros juegos, pero aquí hay otra opción aún mejor
articles.text:
El 19 de noviembre sale a la venta 'GTA VI', uno de los videojuegos más esperados de los últimos años, en consolas PS5 y Xbox Series. Pero unos días antes, el 10 de este mismo mes, los usuarios de ambas plataformas podrán comenzar su predescarga, tal y como ha confirmado la propia Rockstar. Predescarga para la que necesitaremos nada menos que 212 GB libres, una capacidad difícil de alcanzar en modelos como Series S sobre todo si contamos con Game Pass y somos de acumular títulos.
SANDISK Optimus GX C50 512 GB
Por este motivo, muchos usuarios probablemente tendrán que desinstalar alguno de sus actuales videojuegos para hacer hueco a 'GTA VI'. Pero para los de Series X|S hay una estupenda y relativamente económica solución: las tarjetas de expansión oficiales de Seagate y SanDisk.
En este sentido, hoy mismo MediaMarkt rebajó bastante (215,65 euros) el modelo de Seagate en su versión de 1 TB en su outlet, pero rápidamente se agotó. Sin embargo, el SanDisk de 512 GB (132,98 euros), que además viene con un mes de regalo de Xbox Game Pass, está disponible en Amazon a un precio aún mejor y es la opción ideal para instalar el lanzamiento de Rockstar (y varios juegos más) sin eliminar otros títulos.
512 GB de capacidad adicional para Xbox Series, con instalación rápida y sencilla
Tanto el modelo agotado en el outlet de MediaMarkt como este otro de SanDisk, aún disponible en Amazon, son dos de las mejores formas de ampliar la capacidad con que vienen de serie Xbox Series X|S sin complejas instalaciones ni configuraciones. Este último, además, también se puede comprar en versión de 1 TB, aunque su precio no resulta tan interesante (257,99 euros) y tiene un tiempo de envío muy elevado.
Estos SSD oficiales para las consolas de Microsoft se instalan en segundos, gracias al puerto que incluyen Series X y Series S en su zona trasera. Y hacen las veces del almacenamiento interno, permitiendo así seguir disfrutando de tecnologías como Quick Resume o instalaciones de videojuegos rápidas.
Este es precisamente una de sus mayores ventajas frente a otros SSD y HDD externos: la posibilidad de instalar títulos en el propio SSD manteniendo el rendimiento. Un aspecto clave si pensamos jugar a 'GTA VI' en Series X o Series S (sobre todo en esta última) y no queremos eliminar otros juegos para hacer sitio a esos 212 GB para los que no todas las consola están preparadas.

articles.title: La directora del FMI advirtió que la IA afectará al 60% de los empleos de las economías avanzadas
articles.text:
La directora gerente del Fondo Monetario Internacional (FMI), Kristalina Georgieva, afirmó que la inteligencia artificial afectará al 60% de los empleos en las economías avanzadas en un plazo de tres a cinco años. Lo dijo el 3 de noviembre en Madrid, durante la Conferencia Internacional de Banca organizada por el Banco Santander.
Georgieva comparó el fenómeno con “un tsunami lento, pero un tsunami al fin y al cabo”, según la crónica de Europa Press. A nivel mundial, el organismo estima que la IA alcanzará al 40% de los puestos de trabajo.
Afectar no equivale a eliminar. La directora explicó que algunos empleos mejorarán y pagarán más, otros desaparecerán y muchos se redefinirán. La ejecutiva mencionó que en Estados Unidos ya se observa una caída de los empleos rutinarios, a menudo de nivel inicial y ocupados por jóvenes, mientras crece la demanda de empleos de servicios poco cualificados.
“El impacto neto en el empleo es ligeramente positivo, hasta ahora, pero la estructura del empleo es muy diferente”, señaló.
Una cifra que el FMI anticipa desde 2024
El 60% no es un dato nuevo. El FMI lo publicó en enero de 2024, en un análisis sobre el impacto de la IA en el mercado laboral. Ese texto explicaba que alrededor de la mitad de los empleos expuestos podría beneficiarse de la IA, mientras que en el resto la tecnología ejecutaría tareas clave y podría reducir la demanda de trabajadores, los salarios y la contratación.
Ese mismo análisis estimaba una exposición del 40% en los mercados emergentes y del 26% en los países de bajos ingresos. Por eso concluía que las economías avanzadas enfrentan más riesgos, pero también más oportunidades.
Georgieva repitió la cifra en Dubái, el 3 de febrero de 2026, y en Dublín, el 21 de septiembre. En Medio Oriente señaló que uno de cada diez anuncios de empleo en economías avanzadas ya exige al menos una habilidad nueva, y que los puestos de calificación intermedia son los más presionados.
Deuda e inversiones cruzadas, los otros riesgos
En Madrid, la directora describió el auge de la IA como una de las dos grandes fuerzas que moldean la economía mundial. Advirtió que, sin mecanismos de control, los riesgos podrían superar a los beneficios. Identificó tres: la estabilidad financiera, la deuda y el empleo.
Sobre la estabilidad financiera, dijo que, si este nuevo pilar de la economía se tambalea, “habrá graves problemas”. Añadió que las tecnologías tienden a sobrestimarse a corto plazo y a subestimarse a largo plazo, lo que podría provocar una retirada masiva de inversiones.
Sobre la deuda, señaló que cada vez más inversiones en IA se financian con préstamos, a menudo a largo plazo y con mucha inversión circular. “Yo invierto en ti, tú inviertes en mí, todos estamos muy contentos, excepto que si algo sale mal, eso sería un gran problema”, resumió.
Georgieva también dijo que los beneficios se concentran en pocos países integrados en la cadena de valor de la IA, como Estados Unidos, China e India. Europa, según ella, aún no está en ese grupo, con la excepción de Países Bajos.
En el mismo coloquio, la presidenta ejecutiva del Santander, Ana Botín, defendió que las reglas de la IA sigan el principio de “mismo riesgo, mismas reglas”. Planteó la pregunta de si un agente que accede a la cuenta de un cliente debe cumplir las mismas normas, y qué implica eso para la liquidez y la privacidad.

articles.title: AI Agents Got Root on Linux via 948 Kernel Flaws in OpenAI Research
articles.text:
OpenAI says an autonomous pipeline powered by an unreleased cyber model built working root exploits for 948 unique Linux kernel vulnerabilities during a single run that cost $1.2 million in API credits.
The mid-October scan targeted the most recent code in the kernel’s master branch. AI agents first narrowed the kernel down to security-relevant areas that low-privileged users can reach, then flagged 2,308 potential bugs and confirmed 1,724 of them.
Exploits were tested on virtual machines running an unmodified desktop Linux setup with common protections such as KASLR, SMEP and SMAP turned on. In total, the agents came up with 1,169 working local privilege escalation (LPE) exploits, along with 291 proofs of concept for information leaks.
OpenAI says the 948 figure reflects the number of separate patches created for the bugs behind those exploits. Before anything went to kernel maintainers, its security researchers checked the exploits and fixes, along with the severity the system proposed.
“To the best of our knowledge, the agents in this pipeline discovered and used at least 10 novel Linux exploitation techniques,” the company said. Kernel exploitation experts outside OpenAI weren’t familiar with them either, and the full technical details are being kept private for safety reasons.
Spread across the 948 exploits, the $1,213,430 bill comes to roughly $1,279 apiece. An earlier scan in late July, powered by GPT-5.6 Sol, yielded 166 unique LPEs at a cost of $513,690.
OpenAI puts the haul in perspective: at the $20,000 and $70,000 that Pwn2Own and TyphoonPWN have historically paid for Linux kernel privilege escalation exploits, the 948 bugs would be worth $18.9 million to $66.3 million, or 16 to 55 times what the scan cost.
OpenAI notes that the October scan uncovered more than five times as many new LPEs, even though the kernel had gone through three months of hardening in between.
The company also pointed the pipeline at an adapted version of Google’s kernelCTF, whose target kernel is hardened and exposes less attack surface. Over 112 hours and about $33,000 in API credits, it delivered 21 LPE exploits.
Acting on advice from the kernel community, OpenAI says it has already submitted hundreds of reports and patches for critical flaws. It will send fixes for the remaining bugs in stages, working with partners in its Patch the Planet initiative.
“Within 10 days while the scan was running, we observed over 100 Linux LPEs had been patched or had staging patches from other contributors, with ~300 more being publicly discussed,” OpenAI noted.
The company also warned defenders: “For the near and medium term, having access to a low-privileged account on an operating system, that isn’t up-to-date on its latest available patches should be considered functionally equivalent to root access for a well-resourced threat actor.”
To contain the damage when a flaw does get exploited, OpenAI points to layered defenses, including sandboxing and isolation technologies such as Firecracker and gVisor.
OpenAI raises bug bounty rewards
OpenAI separately announced on November 2 that it is increasing payouts in its Security Bug Bounty program. The goal is to get more outside researchers hunting for flaws that its own testing may have missed.
The company says the midpoint of its payout ranges for medium-, high- and critical-severity bugs is now more than four times higher on average. A researcher who reports a critical flaw in ChatGPT, Codex, the API Platform or another core product can now earn as much as $30,000.
The cap for exceptional critical bugs in those products stays at $100,000, but bonuses can now push a single payout to $172,000. OpenAI is adding bonuses for high-quality reports, a five-tier loyalty program for researchers who keep finding valid bugs, and extra multipliers for flaws reported during priority campaigns.

articles.title: Nvidia's RTX Spark GPU priority control is quietly showing up on regular GeForce PCs
articles.text:
In a nutshell: Nvidia built a new GPU priority control for its RTX Spark laptops, allowing owners to keep games running smoothly while an AI agent churns away in the background. Now, the same setting is showing up in the Nvidia App on some standard GeForce RTX PCs, too. Nvidia hasn't said a word about bringing the feature to those systems, however. 
 
 
The option, called GPU App Prioritization, sits under System > Advanced in Nvidia App version 11.0.9.585. Reddit user Warkratos first spotted it and posted screenshots on r/nvidia. They showed several presets for splitting GPU priority between the app in focus and whatever is running in the background.
By default, the foreground app gets 80% priority, while background tasks receive the remaining 20% Favoring the foreground increases that split to 90/10, while a custom setting reportedly allows users to go as far as 95/5. That means someone playing a game while exporting a video or running a local AI model could decide which workload gets the bigger slice of GPU resources.
That's essentially the same as the Resource Management control Nvidia added to its RTX Spark laptops on October 28. At the time, the company pitched it as a way to give background AI agents more or less access to the GPU. On those machines, the feature also only works when hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling is enabled in Windows.
On GeForce cards, however, availability appears to vary considerably. One RTX 5090 owner confirmed that the option appeared after updating. Another user with an RTX 5070 Ti, the same app version, and hotfix driver 621.12 found no such option.
Nvidia's release notes for the update don't mention the feature at all, listing new DLSS overrides and game optimization profiles instead. For now, it's unclear whether this is a staged rollout, something tied to specific drivers, or simply a setting that slipped out before Nvidia intended to announce it.
Anyone curious can update the Nvidia App and check under System > Advanced. Nvidia hasn't confirmed whether the GeForce implementation requires hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling, but given that the RTX Spark version does, it's worth making sure the feature is enabled in Windows' graphics settings, too. Just keep in mind that nobody has independently tested how much of a difference the setting actually makes yet.

articles.title: Food delivery startup Wonder files for IPO as it explores its next big bite | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Food delivery startup Wonder is moving closer to becoming a publicly traded company after confidentially filing for an initial public offering (IPO). The company announced the filing on Thursday, marking a major milestone following years of fundraising, acquisitions, and expansion.
Wonder has yet to reveal how many shares it plans to make available or the expected price range.
Founded in 2018 by entrepreneur Marc Lore, Wonder has evolved from a food delivery concept into a broader food technology business. Its model goes beyond traditional delivery apps, with the company operating food hall-style locations where customers can order meals from multiple restaurant brands through a single platform. The company handles everything from meal preparation to delivery, pickup, and dine-in service.
Lore, who previously founded Jet.com and Diapers.com, has made no secret of his plans to take Wonder public. Those ambitions gained further attention in July, when the company announced it had raised more than $650 million in a funding round that valued it at around $9 billion. Investors include Accel, GV, AllianceBernstein, and ARK Invest.
Meanwhile, Wonder has been busy expanding its footprint and strengthening its business through acquisitions. The company has outlined ambitious growth plans, including a major push into Texas, where it aims to open more than 100 locations by the end of 2027.
Additionally, Wonder has acquired meal-kit company Blue Apron, restaurant delivery platform Grubhub, media company Tastemade, and kitchen robotics company Spyce. The latter acquisition gives Wonder access to automation technology that could help streamline food preparation and improve how food is served.
Wonder is also branching out with Wonder Create, its platform focused on letting food entrepreneurs and social media influencers develop new food concepts, restaurant brands, and menu items. The platform leverages AI to design and launch restaurant brands in less than a minute.
Another notable move is its $425 million partnership with DoorDash to expand its campus dining business, which operates at 450 colleges and universities and other locations.
Despite its growth, a move into the public markets will bring new challenges. Wonder is operating in an increasingly competitive food delivery landscape, going up against established names such as DoorDash and Uber Eats.

This $79.98 TP-Link wireless router with Wi-Fi 7 tech is back down to its lowest-ever price — Archer BE3600 unlocks multi-gigabit networking, ideal for gaming or 4K streaming with 33% off
Give your wireless network a quick upgrade
There's a budget-friendly TP-Link router on sale and it's back down to the lowest ever price we saw it at over Amazon's sales event last month. Right now, the TP-Link Archer BE3600 wireless router is down to $79.98, a 33% saving compared to its list price.
● Check out this deal on Amazon
You won't be surprised to find that this is one of the best Wi-Fi routers you can pick up on a budget, but that's before this discount. You'll see in our TP-Link Archer BE3600 review why this is such a good deal, as this router adds Wi-Fi 7 support to your network cheaply and easily, albeit with a few caveats. Those aside, you're still getting strong performance for 2.4 and 5 GHz with this router.
This TP-Link Archer BE3600 router is one of the best-value routers you can buy right now, offering some Wi-Fi 7 support and 2.5G LAN accessibility.
The BE3600 is not a flashy gaming router, but a no-nonsense option with a standard design that looks very much how you'd expect. It's a flat, rectangular box with four antennas that help deliver good wireless coverage. It has one 2.5 Gbps WAN port to hook it up to your internet connection, as well as an extra 2.5 Gbps and three additional 1 Gbps ports for your home devices.
You've also got one USB 3.0 port, which you can use to connect a printer or external hard drive to use across your network. As far as configuration is concerned, TP-Link's setup is easy to complete using the router's admin page through your browser.
On paper, this is a Wi-Fi 7 router, but there's a compromise you'll need to be aware of. Unfortunately, it doesn't support the full Wi-Fi 7 spec, as it's missing the 6 GHz band. While that is a downside, you do get excellent performance at 2.4 GHz, which is still the dominant Wi-Fi band and one that'll prove useful for any legacy devices you have, especially at close range.
The price is what sells this router, because you'll struggle to find specs and speeds this cheap from other brands. If you're settling for an ISP-issued router, or you need a secondary repeater to cure some Wi-Fi not-spots, then this TP-Link Archer BE3600 (also known as the BE230) is worth considering for its $79.98 sale price. This limited-time deal might not be around for too long, however, so pick it up while you can.

articles.title: Duro revés judicial para 'The Pitt' por parecerse demasiado a 'ER'
articles.text:
The Pitt, una de las series más aclamadas de los últimos años, acaba de sufrir un duro revés judicial. ¿El motivo? Parecerse demasiado a ER (Urgencias en España, ER Emergencias en Latinoamérica), la aclamada producción televisiva que también tuvo a Noah Wyle como protagonista y que se emitió desde 1994 hasta 2009.
Variety reporta que un tribunal falló de forma unánime contra una apelación que había presentado Warner Bros Television, que aseveraba que ER y The Pitt eran shows sin ningún tipo de relación entre sí. No obstante, los jueces consideran que existen pruebas suficientes para permitir una demanda que inculpa a la serie de HBO Max de ser un reboot no autorizado.
La acusación en cuestión llega de parte de Sherri Crichton, la viuda de Michael Crichton, el creador de ER. La misma argumenta que The Pitt viola los términos contractuales originales de Crichton y Warner Bros, que determinaban que cualquier obra derivada de la serie original tendría que recibir la autorización de este o sus herederos.
Vale aclarar que la demanda no es nueva. Crichton la presentó en agosto de 2024, cuando The Pitt ni siquiera había debutado en el catálogo de HBO Max. Según la esposa del creador de ER, John Wells y Noah Wyle querían realizar una secuela de la serie original, pero terminaron cambiando de dirección cuando no obtuvieron su aprobación.
No obstante, considera que existen muchos elementos en común entre ambos títulos para todavía considerar a The Pitt como un reboot o un proyecto derivado, sin contar este con el visto bueno explícito del creador de ER. Sherri Crichton sostiene que esto viola los términos del acuerdo original de su esposo Michael con Warner Bros.
El parecido con ER, un gran drama para The Pitt
De acuerdo con el tribunal que falló contra la apelación de Warner Bros Television, existen "similitudes claras y numerosas" entre The Pitt y ER. Por ejemplo, el uso de una sala de urgencias como escenario principal, el uso de terminología médica específica en el guion, el ritmo de los episodios, la representación gráfica de heridas y lesiones, y hasta la presentación de personajes jóvenes y recién salidos de la facultad de medicina.
Ahora que la justicia ha fallado contra WB, la demanda de Crichton por The Pitt podrá avanzar hacia el juicio. De todos modos, está abierta la puerta a que las partes alcancen un acuerdo extrajudicial. Sea como sea, el culebrón todavía no ha escrito su última página.
Noah Wyle y John Wells han reconocido públicamente que su primera idea era desarrollar una secuela de ER, pero que ello no fue posible y por eso decidieron darle una vuelta de tuerca con The Pitt. Originalmente, la demanda les acusaba también de violar las condiciones contractuales estipuladas por Michael Crichton a sabiendas de lo que hacían, aunque eso sí ha sido desestimado por los jueces.
Más allá de la batalla legal entre los responsables de The Pitt y la familia del creador de ER, la serie de HBO Max no correría peligro. Las dos primeras temporadas fueron impactantes y cosecharon aclamación tanto del público y la prensa, como también de la comunidad de trabajadores de la sanidad.
En agosto pasado, HBO Max lanzó el primer tráiler de la tercera temporada de The Pitt. Si bien todavía no tiene fecha de estreno confirmada, sí es un hecho que llegará en enero de 2027.

articles.title: Adding Network Security To AI, HPC, And Data Centers
articles.text:
The location of security functions such as MACsec or IPsec has become a key architectural decision.
AI and HPC are transforming data center networking. Modern infrastructures typically consist of a front-end network connecting users, storage, and management systems, and a back-end network interconnecting GPUs and compute nodes. At the largest scale, AI clusters span multiple locations, relying on scale-across networking to create a unified infrastructure.
While most modern data centers use leaf-spine architectures, implementation choices are influenced by more than technical requirements. Existing vendor relationships, product availability, supply-chain considerations, and total cost of ownership all play important roles. Consequently, organizations pursuing similar objectives often implement the network based on their business priorities, operational constraints, and upgrade strategies.
AI and HPC infrastructures process valuable data and represent significant financial investments. Protecting these environments requires controls for:
At the same time, security mechanisms must support the fundamental goals of AI infrastructure:
The industry benefits from more than a decade of operational experience with technologies such as MACsec and IPsec in high-speed networks. The primary challenge today is determining where and how those capabilities should be implemented.
Modern AI networks operate at hundreds of gigabits per second and are rapidly moving toward multi-terabit speeds. At these performance levels, network security must be implemented in following way:
Fig. 1: Hardware-accelerated network security architecture with data plane and control plane.
One of the most important architectural decisions is the location of security functions such as MACsec, IPsec, or emerging Ultra Ethernet security mechanisms.
Integrating security directly into the switch ASIC allows encryption and authentication to become part of the packet-forwarding pipeline.
Advantages:
Challenges:
Alternatively, security functions can be implemented in external PHY devices (like the line-card retimer/gearboxes) or security-enabled pluggable modules.
AI and compute systems rely on specialized transport protocols, including InfiniBand, RoCEv2, Ultra Ethernet Transport (UET). Unlike fabric-level security, transport security is typically associated with a specific user, job, or workload and therefore operates as an end-to-end service. Security must remain transparent to the underlying fabric while preserving the low latency and high throughput required by accelerated computing.
For this reason, transport security is integrated into (Smart) NICs and closely coupled with hardware-accelerated transport processing and often support multiple transport and security protocols simultaneously to accommodate diverse communication requirements.
Fig. 2: Network security in the AI NIC.
Modern infrastructures deploy multiple security layers simultaneously based on topology, trust boundaries, and workload requirements:
These mechanisms are largely complementary rather than competitive. MACsec is commonly used for link-level protection, IPsec secures routed traffic across networks, and transport-level security protects AI and HPC communication flows.
Advances in optics are expanding deployment options for network security. MACsec is now being integrated directly into 800G and 1.6T optical modules, enabled by use of silicon technologies optimized for low-power packet processing.
Looking ahead, chiplet-based switch and NIC architectures, together with near-package and co-packaged optics, may create new opportunities for security integration. Dedicated I/O chiplets could become a natural location for encryption and authentication functions while preserving valuable compute and switching resources.
Network security is now a fundamental requirement for AI, HPC, and cloud-scale data centers. Protecting traffic at terabit speeds demands hardware-based implementation capable of maintaining line-rate performance while meeting cost and power targets.
The industry offers multiple deployment options, including switch ASICs, external PHYs, optical modules, SmartNICs, and future chiplet-based architectures. This flexibility allows data center designers to balance security, performance, power efficiency, and system cost according to the needs of their infrastructure.
Rambus addresses these challenges through a broad portfolio of industry-proven network security silicon IP supporting rates up to 1.6T, and 3.2T in the future. Customers can balance security features, throughput, power consumption, and integration effort to deploy network security capabilities that meet the performance, cost, and time-to-market requirements of their silicon devices. articles.title: What Makes a Quantum Company Valuable? - EE Times
articles.text:
Ahead of the World Quantum Festival 2026 in Cannes, France, quantum investors weighed technical bottlenecks, commercial timing, and customer adoption, with healthcare offering a revealing test.
Nardo Manaloto, managing partner of Qubits Ventures, asked the founder of an unnamed startup for a commercial roadmap. The startup was building a photonic quantum computer and had said it would need a decade to deliver its ultimate product. Manaloto wanted to know what the company could sell along the way.
The startup proposed a sequence beginning with a photon detector, followed by a chip, before progressing toward the computer itself. For Manaloto, each intermediate product must solve a customer problem and have commercial value on its own while advancing the company’s long-term technology roadmap.
“The roadmap also extends to the business side,” he told EE Times.
That requirement captures a central challenge in quantum investment. Scientific progress can make a technology promising, but building a valuable company also calls for judgments about customers, financing, and timing.
Finding the bottleneck
Owen Lozman, managing partner of Copenhagen-based quantum investment fund 55 North, draws on his experience in semiconductor investing. He looks for startups that can solve an industry bottleneck by the time customers urgently need a solution.
“Generally in deep tech, we’re not looking for, ‘Does the invention work?’ but, ‘Does it solve a problem at the time at which it’s going to be needed by the customer?’” he told EE Times.
In quantum, that can mean helping system developers move from laboratory assemblies to reliable, reproducible equipment. Lozman cited 55 North’s investment in Monarch Quantum as an example: Optical modules that can be manufactured consistently become increasingly important as quantum companies professionalize their supply chains.
Lozman distinguished three types of quantum businesses, each with different commercial challenges and measures of progress:
- Component suppliers: They must supply reliable, reproducible equipment as quantum computer builders scale production. Investors can examine revenue growth, production costs, and profitability. Lozman said he favors technologies serving multiple qubit architectures and several potential customers.
- Quantum computer developers: They must move from demonstrating individual qubits to building useful, scalable systems. Investors assess their technical differentiation and approach to scaling, including whether they must build manufacturing capacity themselves or can use existing semiconductor infrastructure.
- Software and applications companies: They must understand customer problems and prepare solutions for when suitable quantum hardware becomes available. Investors look for evidence of customer willingness to pay and a credible fit between the product and customer needs. Timing matters: Expanding before the hardware is ready can leave a company burning cash without sufficient revenue.
Value before revenue
Early sales provide evidence of demand, but they are not the only way a quantum company can become valuable. “In a lot of deep tech, the revenue is rarely the exit trigger,” Lozman said, referring to what prompts an acquisition or another opportunity for investors to cash out. “Technology is often the exit trigger.”
A system developer may lack a capability that a smaller company has developed. Bringing them together could create substantially more value than either business holds separately. Manaloto likewise sees value in defensible intellectual property, specialized engineering capabilities, strategic partnerships, and technologies that address critical industry bottlenecks—even before substantial revenue arrives.
Some companies pursuing complete quantum systems may ultimately merge or become component suppliers themselves, Lozman said. Their technology could remain important even if their original business model changes.
For applications companies, however, timing creates a particular danger. They need close customer relationships and a clear understanding of product requirements, but expanding before suitable hardware exists can leave them spending heavily without the expected revenue.
“If you’re a year or two early and you’re burning too much cash, it’s very, very difficult to sustain your company,” Lozman said. “Survivability will be a key kind of KPI for a lot of the assets in this space.”
Manaloto’s demand for intermediate products addresses that financing challenge. The objective is to build revenue and company value while progressing toward the final technology. But an intermediate product still needs a customer and a credible market.
Healthcare’s data opportunity
Healthcare is an application area that particularly interests Manaloto. His experience includes work with Kaiser Permanente’s innovation group and technology fund, where he encountered the difficulties of detecting disease earlier and obtaining useful biological information.
He sees opportunities in quantum sensing instruments that could reveal additional information about cellular processes. Unlike applications that depend on future quantum computers, some sensing businesses could commercialize instruments and measurements sooner, he argued.
Qubits Ventures has invested in Probius Bio, a Stanford spinout developing a quantum electrochemical spectroscopy platform. Manaloto described a system that captures molecular vibrational signatures from biological samples and converts those measurements into biochemical datasets that could support biomarker discovery, drug development, and biological research.
He is also evaluating an investment in an unnamed company developing diamond-based quantum sensing technology to investigate free radical activity and oxidative stress within living cells. Such measurements could help researchers and pharmaceutical companies study cellular behavior, disease mechanisms, and drug responses, he said.
For Manaloto, the opportunity extends beyond selling instruments. The greater potential lies in translating biological measurements that have been difficult to obtain into information that researchers, pharmaceutical companies, and eventually healthcare providers can act on. Research applications could provide an initial market before diagnostic or therapeutic uses are established.
“What do I do with that data? How do I translate it? How can pharma use it?” Manaloto said.
Those questions expose the distance between producing an unfamiliar measurement and delivering a useful product. A researcher needs to understand what the measurement reveals about the biological sample. A clinician needs evidence that it informs a decision. The technology must fit the way they already work—or offer enough benefit to persuade them to change their practices.
Integration with existing systems and compliance requirements add further work before a healthcare organization becomes a repeat customer, Manaloto said.
Capturing the benefit
Lozman identified another hurdle: The company selling a sensor may be separated from the organization receiving its greatest economic benefit. “It’s hard making money out of a sensor,” he said. “It’s hard to get people to recover the value if the buyer and the beneficiary are not close in the value chain.”
A measurement could improve a downstream process while leaving the instrument supplier struggling to capture a sufficient share of the benefit. The business model must connect the product’s price to an outcome the customer recognizes and will pay for.
In pharmaceutical research, Lozman sees potential opportunities in instruments that simplify drug discovery, improve toxicology assessment, or support better clinical-trial endpoints.
Qualification can be slow. Drawing on his experience across electronics and healthcare, Lozman noted that customers have strong reasons to protect processes that already work. A new technology must solve a sufficiently important problem to justify its introduction.
The same caution can benefit a company once its product is established. “Once you’re in, it’s very hard to get displaced,” Lozman said.
Both Manaloto and Lozman will attend the World Quantum Cannes Festival on November 17–18, where quantum technology providers, investors, and potential customers will meet to discuss applications and commercialization. For investors, those conversations offer an opportunity to hear how prospective users define their problems—and what they might be willing to pay to solve them.
For quantum investors, that’s where scientific promise must lead: a capability that solves a consequential problem, reaches the market at the right time, and gives its developer a defensible business. The roadmap to that outcome can matter as much as the eventual machine.

articles.title: Amazon jubelt, Nvidia verliert: Was die US-Wahl mit dem KI-Boom macht
articles.text:
Börse nach den US-Wahlen: Big Tech jubelt, KI-Zulieferer verlieren
Der überraschend deutliche Sieg der Demokraten bei den US-Midterms teilt die Börse in Gewinner und Verlierer. Insgesamt reagierten die Börsen am Mittwoch aber erleichtert auf den Ausgang der Wahlen in den USA, da die Ergebnisse eindeutig ausfielen und auch von Präsident Donald Trump schnell anerkannt wurden.
Der US-Index S&P 500 stieg um 1,6 Prozent. Der industrielastige Dow Jones verzeichnete den stärksten Kursanstieg nach einem Wahlausgang seit über 40 Jahren und stieg am Mittwoch um 3,0 Prozent auf über 1500 Punkte. Auch der deutsche Leitindex DAX schloss gestern mit einem deutlichen Plus von 2,22 Prozent.
Big Tech gewinnt, KI-Infrastruktur verliert
Allerdings wirkte sich der Wahlsieg der Demokraten nicht für alle positiv aus. So schloss der Technologieindex Nasdaq 100 am Mittwoch zwar ebenfalls mit einem Plus von 0,91 Prozent. Bei den Tech-Aktien differenzieren Anleger jetzt aber offensichtlich stärker.
Vor allem die Aktien von Rechenzentrumsanbietern kamen unter Druck, da auch in Texas und Ohio Demokraten das Gouverneursamt eroberten und der Neubau von Rechenzentren nun auf stärkeren Gegenwind treffen dürfte. Wahlgewinnerin Gina Hinojosa in Texas kündigte bereits an, neue Genehmigungen so lange zu blockieren, bis es Schutzgesetze und Mitspracherechte für Anwohner gibt. In Texas sollen rund ein Viertel der bis 2030 geplanten neuen US-Rechenzentrumskapazität entstehen.
Zu den Verlierern an der Börse gehörten daher vor allem die Aktien von Neocloud-Unternehmen wie CoreWeave und Nebius, die um rund neun beziehungsweise sechs Prozent nachgaben. Beide bauen mit Fremdkapital Rechenzentren.
Amazon und Microsoft standen gestern dagegen auf der Gewinnerseite, mit einem Kursplus von jeweils mehr als 6 Prozent. Auch Alphabet legte nach deutlichen Verlusten der letzten Woche über drei Prozent zu. Bei ihnen wird die erwartete Bremse beim Ausbau von Rechenzentren positiv bewertet, da dann mehr Gewinne in den Unternehmen verbleiben.
Die extrem hohen KI-Investitionen der Big-Tech-Unternehmen hatten Anleger zuletzt eher verunsichert. So planen Amazon, Microsoft und Alphabet, allein in diesem Jahr zusammen über 740 Milliarden Dollar für Rechenzentrumskapazitäten auszugeben.
Seit Meta am 21. Oktober die Quartalszahlen der großen Cloud-Konzerne eröffnet hat, ging es für die „Magnificent Seven“ bergab: Ein Bloomberg-Index, der die sieben Tech-Riesen bündelt, hat bis Dienstag 5,9 Prozent verloren. Seit Jahresbeginn steht die Gruppe damit nur noch 4,1 Prozent im Plus und hinkt dem S&P 500 und dem Nasdaq 100 hinterher. Wenn nun aber alle Tech-Unternehmen gleichermaßen gebremst werden, entfällt der Zwang zu einem weiteren Wettrüsten, um beim KI-Ausbau mithalten zu können.
Verkauft wurden am Mittwoch auch Aktien von Firmen, deren Wachstum stark vom Infrastrukturausbau abhängt, darunter die Papiere der Chiphersteller Nvidia und AMD.
Auch SpaceX kam unter Druck, die Aktie büßte zum Börsenschluss 3,8 Prozent ein. Musk war im Wahlkampf als Großspender für die Republikaner aufgetreten und hatte allein in Texas 224 Millionen und insgesamt mindestens 474 Millionen Dollar in die Midterms gesteckt. Sowohl SpaceX als auch Tesla haben ihren Unternehmenssitz in Texas.
Nun fürchten Anleger wohl strengere Auflagen für den Ausbau von KI- und Satelliteninfrastruktur sowie politischen Gegenwind bei einer möglichen Fusion von SpaceX und Tesla. Ein angekündigter Deal mit Qualcomm für das Bodennetz von Starlink Mobile konnte die Kursverluste von SpaceX gestern noch eindämmen.
Öl- und Rüstungsaktien unter Druck
Neben KI-Aktien mussten gestern auch Rüstungs- und Öl-Aktien Rücksetzer hinnehmen. So verlor die Aktie des Rüstungskonzerns Lockheed Martin gut sieben Prozent. Dahinter steckt die Sorge der Anleger, der neue Kongress könnte über seine Haushaltsrechte künftig Militärausgaben infrage stellen.
Auch der Energiesektor im S&P 500 gehörte zu den Verlierern und rutschte um 4,8 Prozent ab. Während Unternehmen aus erneuerbaren Energien Kursgewinne verbuchten, gab es bei den großen Ölkonzernen deutliche Rücksetzer. Trump gilt als Gegner von Wind- und Solarprojekten und Freund der Öl- und Gasindustrie. Mit dem Sieg der Demokraten im Kongress könnte seine Energiepolitik nun auf mehr Widerstand stoßen.
Der Preis für die Ölsorte Brent rutschte um 8,7 Prozent auf 94,42 Dollar, da Anleger auch darauf setzten, dass der Machtwechsel das Ende des Iran-Kriegs beschleunigt.

articles.title: CERT-In warns of security vulnerabilities in Tata Motors' connected vehicle apps
articles.text:
CERT-In warns of security vulnerabilities in Tata Motors' connected vehicle apps
The vulnerabilities affect specific versions of the apps used by internal combustion engine (ICE) and electric vehicle (EV) owners, raising fresh concerns around cybersecurity risks in connected vehicles.
The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) on Wednesday flagged multiple high-severity vulnerabilities in specific versions of Tata Motors' iRA 2.0 and iRA.ev connected vehicle applications, warning that they could expose sensitive user credentials, enable user impersonation and allow unauthorised access to vehicle-related information and services.
The vulnerabilities affect iRA 2.0 versions 26.7.3 and below, and iRA.ev versions 26.7.2 and below. The applications cater to Tata Motors' internal combustion engine (ICE) and electric vehicle (EV) customers, respectively, and provide access to connected services such as remote vehicle commands, vehicle status, health monitoring and trip information.
CERT-In identified four vulnerabilities involving hardcoded credentials, inadequate URL validation, exposure of authentication tokens in application logs and improper implementation of SSL certificate pinning.
According to the advisory, these flaws could allow attackers to extract credentials and access backend services, obtain authentication tokens to impersonate users, or intercept and modify communications between the applications and their backend systems.
In response to the advisory, Tata Cars in an official statement, said, “As part of our proactive cybersecurity practices, we continuously monitor our systems for potential vulnerabilities and work closely with CERT-In, sharing relevant findings transparently."
They added that the vulnerabilities which were identified have been addressed through software updates and enhanced security measures in the latest versions of iRA 2.0 (version 26.8.2) and iRA.ev (version 26.9.1) – were rolled out in August and September 2026, respectively.
"The update rollout has been completed for all active users, and we are proactively reaching out to remaining customers who are yet to complete the updates to ensure their transition to the latest versions."
The company also said, "Our assessment has indicated customer data and vehicle-related information remain secure – with no evidence of any unauthorised access to or compromise of customer credentials, personal information or vehicle-related data. We continue to actively monitor our systems to maintain the security and protection of our customers.”
The vulnerabilities flagged by CERT-In come amid growing cybersecurity concerns around connected vehicles globally. In recent years, security researchers have identified flaws in connected-car platforms operated by automakers such as Kia and Subaru that could potentially expose customer information and enable unauthorised access to vehicle functions.
In another instance, researchers discovered vulnerabilities in Bluetooth software used in vehicles manufactured by Mercedes-Benz, Volkswagen, and Skoda, which could potentially allow remote code execution through infotainment systems. These incidents highlight the growing security risks as automakers increasingly rely on mobile applications, cloud infrastructure and connected services to offer digital features to vehicle owners.

articles.title: Constantine : un nouveau film est en route, Keanu Reeves enfin de retour ?
articles.text:
Le média américain Deadline a révélé ce mercredi 4 novembre 2026 que DC Studios avait recruté Francis Galluppi pour écrire un film consacré à John Constantine. Le cinéaste s’est fait connaître avec son thriller policier The Last Stop in Yuma County (2023). Sam Raimi, créateur de la saga Evil Dead, l’a ensuite choisi pour écrire et réaliser Evil Dead Wrath, septième film de la série et son premier long-métrage pour un grand studio. Avec son futur Constantine, DC Studios replonge dans l’occulte, le terrain de jeu du personnage surnommé Hellblazer.
Un projet encore à l’état d’ébauche pour Constantine
Le projet n’en est qu’au tout début. D’après les sources de Deadline, le film est en développement très précoce chez DC Studios. Aucun réalisateur ni aucun acteur n’y est rattaché, et aucune date de sortie n’a été fixée.
Créé en 1985 par Alan Moore, Steve Bissette et John Totleben dans les pages de The Saga of the Swamp Thing (numéro 37), John Constantine s’est imposé comme le détective de l’occulte par excellence. C’est un Britannique désabusé, magouilleur et gros fumeur, qui fréquente aussi bien les démons que les anges déchus.
L’ombre de Keanu Reeves et le grand ménage du DCU
Cette annonce relance les questions sur la suite de Constantine, le film culte réalisé par Francis Lawrence en 2005, dans lequel Keanu Reeves incarnait une version de l’exorciste à Los Angeles. Deadline ne dit pas si Keanu Reeves ou cette suite sont concernés. On ne sait donc pas si Francis Galluppi écrit une nouvelle version du personnage, peut-être rattachée au DCU que reconstruisent James Gunn et Peter Safran, ou s’il reprend le projet Constantine 2.
Clayface dépasse déjà les 90 millions de dollars (environ 80 millions d’euros) de recettes mondiales pour un budget de production d’environ 40 millions de dollars. Avec ce succès et l’arrivée de cinéastes venus du film de genre comme Galluppi, DC Studios mise de plus en plus sur l’horreur et le polar noir. Le cinéaste doit d’abord livrer Evil Dead Wrath, attendu dans les salles américaines le 7 avril 2028.
