articles.title: Configure, Certify, and Operate Kubernetes GPU Clusters with NVIDIA DSX OS | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.text:
One underperforming GPU can slow an entire distributed training job. The node may pass basic health checks and show normal utilization, leaving operators to discover the problem only after the workload is running.
These issues can appear at any point in a cluster’s lifecycle. A GPU cluster that passes readiness checks at handover changes as nodes are replaced, drivers are patched, and capacity is added. Without repeated validation, the original certification no longer reflects the cluster’s condition.
This visibility gap wastes compute on failing nodes and leaves healthy nodes idle out of caution. Utilization metrics can mask these losses. Goodput, which is the volume of work successfully completed, provides a more useful measure of cluster efficiency. Maintaining cluster readiness requires validation throughout the cluster’s operational lifecycle—after configuration changes, as capacity grows, and before repaired nodes return to service.
The NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform brings together technologies for designing, building, and operating efficient, resilient AI factories. Its open source software layer, NVIDIA DSX OS, includes tools for configuring, certifying, and maintaining the health of accelerated Kubernetes infrastructure.
- Configure: NVIDIA AI Cluster Runtime (AICR) establishes a reproducible baseline for GPU-optimized Kubernetes infrastructure.
  - Defines version-locked configuration recipes for components such as networking, storage, and drivers.
  - Renders recipes as bundles for existing deployment tools.
- Certify: NVIDIA Cluster Readiness Engine (NVCRE) validates whether the cluster is ready to run production workloads.
  - Tests GPUs, networking, and storage using AI workloads and diagnostics.
  - Records certification results and helps identify faulty nodes.
- Operate: NVSentinel monitors cluster health and supports fault remediation and revalidation.
  - Publishes node conditions based on GPU, node, and network health.
  - When configured, cordons or taints unhealthy nodes, drains workloads, and remediates faults.
  - Can trigger revalidation with NVCRE before nodes return to service.
All three are open source projects licensed under Apache 2.0 and welcome external contributions.
Before you begin, install and configure AICR, NVCRE, and NVSentinel using their installation guides. The examples assume access to a Kubernetes GPU cluster with the required CLIs, controllers, dependencies, and NVCRE test provider configured.
This walkthrough follows one cluster through its lifecycle: configuration from a recipe, certification before production use, monitoring during operation, and recertification after repair. Each command is a step in that sequence.
Configure: A baseline you can reproduce
AICR defines the cluster’s software baseline in version-controlled files and renders them into artifacts your existing deployment tooling applies. It generates and validates; your deployer applies and reconciles them. Declarative templates help detect configuration drift from manual changes and keep node configurations consistent after repairs.
You describe the target environment. AICR resolves it against a library of validated overlays and emits a recipe:
aicr recipe --service eks --accelerator h100 --os ubuntu \
  --intent inference --platform dynamo -o recipe.yaml
Each component entry in the resulting recipe pins a version and declares which dependencies must be healthy before the component is installed:
apiVersion: aicr.run/v1alpha2
componentRefs:
  - name: dynamo-platform
    chart: dynamo-platform
    namespace: dynamo-system
    source: https://helm.ngc.nvidia.com/nvidia/ai-dynamo
    type: Helm
    version: 1.4.2
    valuesFile: components/dynamo-platform/values.yaml
    dependencyRefs:
      - grove
      - cert-manager
      - kube-prometheus-stack
      - gpu-operator
      - kai-scheduler
The recipe includes three key properties:
- Pinned versions: The version is fixed, helping you reproduce the software configuration and investigate failures. In contrast, a floating tag can point to a different software version over time, making failures harder to reproduce.
- A dependency graph: dependencyRefs declares what must be installed and healthy first. AICR resolves the graph when it renders the bundle, so the ordering is already encoded in the artifacts your deployer applies. You don’t need to specify that cert-manager comes before NVSentinel, and adding a component later doesn’t require renumbering.
- Health assertions per component: Each entry carries a healthCheckAsserts block that runs after installation and checks whether the component meets its configured health criteria. Kubernetes can report a pod stuck in CrashLoopBackOff as Running, so a check based only on the pod phase can miss a broken component. The shipped assertions filter on the container waiting reason rather than the pod phase alone.
Rendering the recipe is a separate step that connects AICR to your existing pipeline:
aicr bundle --recipe recipe.yaml --deployer argocd --output ./bundles
--deployer accepts helm, argocd, argocd-helm, flux, or helmfile, so the same validated recipe becomes Argo CD Application manifests, Flux resources, a Helmfile release graph, or plain Helm commands. You can keep your existing deployment tooling and use AICR to generate its configuration artifacts.
Because the recipe is a file, you can use version history, code review, and drift detection to manage the baseline.
# Check a live cluster against the recipe's constraints
aicr validate --recipe recipe.yaml
# Compare a golden baseline against the live cluster, non-zero exit on drift
aicr diff --baseline ./golden.yaml --target cm://default/aicr-snapshot --fail-on-drift
--fail-on-drift turns the drift check into a continuous integration (CI) gate rather than a report.
Certify: Prove the cluster will run the job
The cluster is now built to a known baseline. It still needs workload validation. Standard health checks confirm that basic services are running. They don’t confirm that the cluster can run a demanding multinode job across its interconnect without stalling. NVCRE validates workload readiness by running training jobs and NVIDIA Collective Communication Library (NCCL) tests.
NVSentinel manages validation requests, scheduling gates, quarantine, and repair, while NVCRE runs tests and records results. Table 1 shows how these responsibilities fit into the node validation lifecycle.
| Step | Responsible component | Action | Outcome | 
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Request and gate | NVSentinel lifecycle manager; operators for upgrades or fabric changes | Create a ValidationRequest for new or repaired nodes. After upgrades or fabric changes, operators cordon the nodes and create the request. | A cordon or taint blocks scheduling on the nodes during validation. | 
| 2. Test and attribute | NVCRE through nvcre-provider | Run workloads and diagnostic tests. Bisect failing groups to identify suspect nodes. | Test results identify suspect nodes. NVCRE doesn’t change the node state. | 
| 3. Record and evaluate | NVCRE and NVSentinel lifecycle manager | NVCRE records pass/fail results, failing node IDs, and failure reasons in the Certification resource. The lifecycle manager evaluates the results. | The validation outcome determines whether the scheduling gate can be removed. | 
| 4. Resolve the gate | NVSentinel lifecycle manager | Remove or retain the scheduling gate based on validation results and any remaining tests. | Pass: remove the configured gate once no other tests hold the node. Failure after retries: keep the node cordoned. | 
A certification identifies the nodes to test, the categories to run, and the thresholds that determine whether the tests pass or fail:
apiVersion: nvcre.nvidia.com/v1alpha1
kind: Certification
metadata:
  name: gpu-cluster-cert
spec:
  target:
    nodeSelector:
      nvidia.com/gpu.present: "true"
  categories:
    - domain: communication
      variant: nccl-all-reduce
    - domain: training
      variant: nemotron5-8b
  options:
    thresholds:
      busBandwidthGBps: "value >= 300"
nvcrectl certification run --cert-file certification.yaml --wait
nvcrectl certification report gpu-cluster-cert -n <namespace>
The report shows each category’s status, runtime, measured bandwidth, and the reason for any failed nodes.
Thresholds make certification a performance gate. None are configured by default. Without the options.thresholds block above, a run reports its measurements and fails when the tests can’t start. A node performing below the target can pass. Thresholds help catch performance degradation rather than breakage.
The catalog covers NCCL communication variants, the NVIDIA Data Center GPU Manager (DCGM) level 4 diagnostic suite, and pretraining workloads using NVIDIA NeMo Framework with 8-billion- and 56-billion-parameter models. A WorkloadRun resource turns your own containerized test into a certification check. NVCRE infers the rest from the target nodes, so the manifest stays concise on any supported platform.
These tests can help identify performance issues that aren’t apparent in telemetry. A GPU running just below its performance target might not produce Xid errors, breach monitoring thresholds, or cause node metrics to appear abnormal. That one GPU can slow a synchronous training job to its slowest rank, and operators may find out hours later, or only after a user complains. An NCCL bandwidth test can uncover this performance degradation.
Isolating the cause matters as much. If a 64-node all-reduce yields poor bandwidth, every node is suspect, and bisecting by hand can be time-consuming. NVCRE splits failing groups and reruns the tests until it reaches a minimum group size, then reports the suspect nodes with a reason for each.
Run NVCRE before handing a cluster or new capacity to a tenant and when repaired hardware rejoins the pool.
Operate: Detection and remediation under load
The certified cluster is now running workloads and needs to stay healthy. AICR and NVCRE provide point-in-time validation. NVSentinel runs continuously alongside workloads.
NVSentinel watches signals the cluster already produces: DCGM health checks, Xid errors, network interface card (NIC) states, and cloud provider maintenance events. It doesn’t consume GPU time, leaving GPUs available for workloads.
NVSentinel installs in monitoring mode by default: it reports faults as node conditions and won’t cordon, evict, or remediate nodes. You can roll it out on a live cluster while you evaluate its reports. You can enable quarantine, draining, and remediation once you trust the reported signals.
Detection publishes a health event; a Fault Quarantine ruleset decides what happens to the node. Rulesets use Common Expression Language (CEL) expressions in your values file:
fault-quarantine:
  ruleSets:
    - enabled: true
      version: "1"
      name: "GPU fatal error ruleset"
      priority: 100
      match:
        all:
          - kind: "HealthEvent"
            expression: "event.agent == 'gpu-health-monitor' && event.componentClass == 'GPU' && event.isFatal == true"
          - kind: "Node"
            expression: |
              !('k8saas.nvidia.com/ManagedByNVSentinel' in node.metadata.labels &&
                node.metadata.labels['k8saas.nvidia.com/ManagedByNVSentinel'] == "false")
      cordon:
        shouldCordon: true
      taint:
        key: "nvidia.com/gpu-error"
        value: "fatal"
        effect: "NoSchedule"
A cordon or taint provides a signal that your scheduler, alerting, and lifecycle tooling can use without integrating directly with NVSentinel.
A circuit breaker limits the impact by capping how many GPU nodes can be quarantined in a sliding window. The Fault Quarantine configuration guide covers the bounds and the rest of the ruleset options.
Not every fault takes the same path. A known fatal error goes straight to remediation. The health events analyzer handles other cases by detecting patterns across a node’s failure history, so a node that fails repeatedly becomes eligible for investigation based on the accumulated record rather than any single event.
A health event with the recommended action CONTACT_SUPPORT requires manual investigation or support intervention.
The loop: How readiness becomes continuous
A node fails, gets repaired, and needs to rejoin the pool. Validation before the node returns to service closes the operational loop, but manual handoffs can interrupt the process. Manual certification produces a point-in-time result that routine operations can make outdated. Someone has to notice that the cluster changed, rerun validation, and then read the output and act on it. NVSentinel and NVCRE can help automate this process.
Two lifecycle events trigger revalidation automatically when configured. The NVSentinel lifecycle controller creates a ValidationRequest when a node joins the cluster and again when a node returns after remediation. It gates scheduling on the node using a cordon or taint, then uses NVCRE to run the tests and record the results. The controller evaluates those results and removes the gate after the tests pass, so a node that still fails validation cannot silently rejoin the pool. When you configure nvcre-provider as its test provider, those tests are NCCL or NVIDIA Nemotron runs through NVCRE:
global:
  lifecycleManager:
    enabled: true
fault-quarantine:
  validation:
    enabled: true
lifecycle-manager:
  config:
    schedulingGate:
      cordon:
        remove: true
The lifecycle-manager chart turns on new-node validation; the fault-quarantine flag opts in to post-remediation validation separately. schedulingGate.cordon sets the cordon as the scheduling gate for validation, and remove: true uncordons the node once its tests pass.
The process is different for in-place driver upgrades, operator upgrades, or fabric changes. These changes don’t automatically trigger validation. Because the baseline is a file, aicr diff --fail-on-drift fails a pipeline stage when a live cluster drifts from its recipe, providing a trigger for a certification run in the same pipeline that made the change.
Cordon the affected nodes, then create a validation request naming them and the tests to run:
apiVersion: nvsentinel.nvidia.com/v1alpha1
kind: ValidationRequest
metadata:
  name: post-driver-upgrade
spec:
  nodes:
    - name: node-a
    - name: node-b
  tests:
    - nccl-all-reduce
    - nemotron-5b
The controller also acts on the result. If the request passes, it removes the scheduling gate once no other tests hold the node. If the test fails after its retries, the node remains cordoned.
A fault can also surface during validation: GPUs may start thermally throttling during a training test. NVSentinel quarantines the node, and the controller retries the test after remediation. The node stays gated until validation passes.
The request and the node both carry state you can query:
kubectl get validationrequests
kubectl get nodes -l nvsentinel.nvidia.com/validation-state=validation-failed
Recovery requires no manual node edits: a later request that passes the same tests clears the failure and removes the gate. Deleting all failed validation requests that reference the node can release it without rerunning validation.
The handoff has a clear boundary. NVCRE stops at attribution, recording which nodes failed and why; NVSentinel owns quarantine and repair. Two systems cordoning the same node could produce double-cordons and desynchronized cleanup.
This separation also enables you to use your own node lifecycle tooling. A platform team can consume the same certification results and take over NVSentinel’s role. Extending the stack means writing a ruleset or a policy, rather than forking a project.
What this changes for operators
AICR, NVCRE, and NVSentinel help operators make configuration, validation, and recovery repeatable. With remediation and lifecycle validation enabled, NVSentinel can coordinate repair and testing before nodes return to service, reducing manual handoffs. Table 2 outlines what these tools handle and what operators still manage.
| Operational task | What changes | What operators still manage | 
|---|---|---|
| Maintain the software baseline | AICR provides version-locked recipes and generates configuration artifacts for existing deployment tools. Operators can review deviations from a defined baseline. | Approve baseline changes, deploy the artifacts, run drift checks, and reconcile differences. | 
| Validate new or repaired capacity | NVCRE runs selected workloads and diagnostics and records readiness results. With lifecycle validation configured, NVSentinel can coordinate testing before nodes return to service. | Select tests and thresholds appropriate to the cluster and investigate failed results. | 
| Recover unhealthy nodes | When enabled, NVSentinel coordinates quarantine, draining, remediation, and revalidation, reducing manual handoffs between these actions. | Define quarantine rules, remediation limits, and escalation procedures; handle faults that automated remediation cannot resolve. | 
| Validate infrastructure changes | Operators can incorporate baseline checks and workload validation into their upgrade workflows. | Trigger validation after in-place driver, operator, or fabric changes; these changes do not automatically trigger revalidation. | 
Get started
Start with the project repositories for installation instructions and examples:
You can also:
- Get hands-on with these tools at the NVIDIA DSX OS AI Inference and Contributor Workshop, held alongside KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America. Separate registration is required, and seating is limited.
- Visit NVIDIA booth 170 at KubeCon for more Kubernetes deep dives and live demos.
- Join the DSX AI Factory Slack community to continue the conversation.
- Explore open-source, modular components in the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory GitHub.

articles.title: Custom Pins for Tech Events: Premium Finishes vs. Eco Materials - Tech Guide
articles.text:
At developer conferences, hackathons, and global tech summits, custom enamel pins serve as tangible social currency. Attendees collect and trade them across exhibitor booths, wear them on conference lanyards, and display them on laptop sleeves and backpacks long after closing remarks. Designing an effective pin requires balancing visual branding with material durability, volume economics, and event logistics.
Hard Enamel vs. Soft Enamel: Matching Finishes to Event Formats
How your audience engages with your merch comes down to how hard‑enamel and soft‑enamel pins look and feel. You’ll want to pick the proper finish based on your event level and how you plan to hand out the items.
Hard Enamel: Polished Credentials for VIPs and Speakers
Hard enamel pins are baked and polished several times during production. This process brings the enamel and metal edges to the same level, leaving a smooth, shiny surface. The finish is durable enough for pins that are handled often or worn regularly at events.
- Best For: Keynote speakers, VIP sponsors, hackathon judges, and executive summit attendees who want a keepsake from the event.
- Aesthetic Pairing: Polished silver works well with the clean, modern look of software and cloud technology brands. Gold plating or matte black nickel may be a better fit for established tech companies or executive-level events.
Soft Enamel: Dimensional Detailing for Community and Swag Bags
Soft enamel pins have raised metal lines with color filled in between them. You can feel the difference when you run your finger over the surface. They work well for logos, mascots, and pixel-style designs.
- Best For: DevCon swag bags, booth activities such as scan-and-collect pin challenges, gifts for community contributors, and open-source project merchandise.
Design Tip (Format & Sizing): If attendees will be collecting or trading pins at different booths, 0.75-inch mini pins are worth considering. Their smaller size makes them easier to carry on a lanyard, especially when people collect designs from multiple sponsors. This size works with both hard and soft enamel.
Enamel Specification & Decision Matrix
| Dimension | Hard Enamel (Cloisonné Style) | Soft Enamel (Die-Struck Relief) | 
| Surface Profile | Flush, flat, mirror-polished plane | Recessed paint fills with raised metal borders | 
| Tactile Texture | Glass-smooth, jewelry-grade glide | Dimensional, textured 3D relief | 
| Durability Grade | High; highly resistant to abrasion and daily friction | Moderate; raised metal protects paint, but enamel can scuff | 
| Fine Line Tolerance | Moderate (≥ 0.3 mm); lines can widen during polishing | High (≥ 0.15 mm); raised ridges hold crisp micro-details | 
| Cost Baseline | 15% to 25% premium due to multi-stage polishing | Cost-effective baseline for mass distribution | 
| Primary Tech Use | Speaker honors, VIP credentials, executive summits | DevCon swag bags, booth trading quests, contributor drops | 
Sustainable Swag: Aligning Materials with ESG Tech Summits
Companies are paying more attention to the materials used in event giveaways as ESG becomes a bigger part of IT reporting. Brass and zinc are still widely used for pins, but events related to clean energy or climate technology may need other options with a smaller environmental footprint. Organizers may also need documents to back up those claims.
- Recycled Metal (Brass/Zinc): Recycled brass and zinc can achieve the same fine details and polished finish as newly mined metals, with less reliance on virgin resources. They’re a good choice for tech companies that want to use more recycled materials without compromising the look of their pins.
- FSC-Certified Wood (Walnut, Cherry, or Maple): Wood pins have a look and feel that’s quite different from metal pins. Each piece has its own grain, and logos or text can be added through laser engraving. They may suit open-source meetups, cybersecurity events, and smaller tech conferences looking for a simple alternative to traditional enamel pins.
- Bamboo: Lightweight and fast-growing, bamboo gives pins a simple, modern appearance. Its natural texture pairs well with geometric logos and minimalist tech branding.
Evaluating Environmental Claims: A material labeled “eco-friendly” isn’t necessarily the better choice in every situation. For example, untreated wood or poorly finished bamboo may wear out quickly when attached to bags used every day, leading to more frequent replacements. Before ordering, check for credible third-party sourcing certifications and ask suppliers whether their coatings, adhesives, and other finishes are lead-free and non-toxic.
Tiered Pricing and Production Economics
When ordering custom pins, you may need to pay for the mold first, then pay for each pin. Ask the supplier to break down both costs before ordering so you know what you’ll actually spend.
- Tooling and Mold Costs: Each new pin design usually needs its own steel mold, and the setup fee generally stays the same whether you order 100 or 5,000 pieces. For events with different attendee groups, you can reuse one design and change the enamel colors for each group—for example, black and gold for speakers and blue and white for attendees. This helps avoid paying for multiple molds.
- Order Quantity and Leftovers: Ordering more pins can bring down the price per piece, but that doesn’t mean a bigger order is always the better deal. Check the number of people registered before deciding how many to buy. It’s also worth asking suppliers about price differences at 100, 300, 500, 1,000, and 2,500 pieces. Adding 10%–15% to your estimated attendance should leave a few spares without going too far over budget.
- Finishes and Material Costs: Hard enamel pins generally cost 15%–25% more than soft enamel because of the extra polishing involved. Wooden pins and those made with certified recycled metals may also come at a higher price. This is especially noticeable with small orders, where material and production costs are divided among fewer pieces.
Production Timelines, Proofing, and Supplier Sourcing
Managing technical production requires disciplined milestone planning well before event week.
Brand Color Precision & Proofing
- Pantone Color Matching: Colors can look different on a computer screen than they do on a finished enamel pin. To get a closer match to your brand colors, provide vector artwork in AI or EPS format with the correct Pantone (PMS) codes specified.
- Digital Proofs vs. Physical Samples: A digital proof gives you a chance to review the design before production starts, including the metal lines, enamel colors, and cutout shapes. For most orders, this is enough to catch design issues. If you’re ordering more than 2,500 pins or using an unfamiliar eco-friendly material, ask for a physical sample so you can see the finish and quality for yourself.
Lead Times and Event Deadlines
Custom metal pins can take around 2–4 weeks to make, with shipping time added on top. Getting a physical sample first may add another 7–10 business days. To avoid last-minute problems, try to have everything delivered at least 10 business days before the event, especially if the order is coming from overseas.
Supplier Quote Checklist
Choosing a supplier comes down to order size, delivery location, and how quickly you need the pins.
- Bulk Orders: For businesses ordering large quantities, suppliers like GS-JJ offer different styles of custom enamel pins and custom lapel pins to help keep branding consistent across an order.
- Australia and New Zealand: If your event is taking place in Australia, New Zealand, or elsewhere in Oceania, a local manufacturer may be a practical choice for shorter shipping times and fewer cross-border delays. You can start by comparing options in this guide to the Top 6 Custom Pin Manufacturers in Australia.
Some conference pins are handed out as branded gifts, while others are made for attendees to take home and collect. Hard enamel has a flat, polished surface, whereas soft enamel leaves the metal edges standing above the colored sections. Either finish can suit an event logo or mascot, depending on the artwork. For organizers who want something different from standard metal pins, recycled materials or wood are also options. The right choice depends on how the pins will be used, who they’re intended for, and what the event budget allows.

articles.title: Android : Google corrige 216 failles de sécurité, dont 23 vulnérabilités critiques
articles.text:
Google vient de publier son bulletin de sécurité mensuel. Au programme, des correctifs pour les fonctions internes du système, le noyau Linux et plusieurs éléments fournis par les fabricants de puces, qui ne concernent donc pas tous les smartphones de la même manière.
Un peu plus de 200 vulnérabilités corrigées, dont une bonne vingtaine classées critiques : en voilà une mise à jour de sécurité chargée ! Google vient de publier ses patchs de novembre pour Android, qui corrigent notamment trois failles susceptibles de permettre l'exécution de code à distance sur les versions 14 à 17.
Une faille exploitable sans intervention de la victime
Dans le détail, la faille la plus grave, référencée CVE-2026-58868, concerne le Framework, un ensemble de fonctions essentielles au fonctionnement d'Android et de ses applications. Selon Google, elle pourrait permettre à un attaquant d'exécuter du code à distance sans disposer de privilèges particuliers sur le téléphone ni nécessiter la moindre action de son propriétaire. Comme souvent, l'entreprise ne détaille pas les modalités de l'attaque, évitant ainsi de fournir des indications qui pourraient faciliter son exploitation.
Deux autres failles critiques, CVE-2026-58876 et CVE-2026-58936, touchent le composant System et présentent également un risque d'exécution de code à distance. Le bulletin ne signale aucune exploitation active de ces vulnérabilités, mais leur gravité justifie de ne pas tarder à installer les correctifs lorsqu'ils seront disponibles.
Deux niveaux de correctifs à installer sans tarder
Outre les failles relatives aux fonctions internes d'Android, Google recense également plusieurs vulnérabilités critiques dans le noyau Linux, notamment au niveau du Bluetooth, ainsi que dans les modems MediaTek et certains logiciels propriétaires de Qualcomm. Leur présence dépendant du matériel embarqué, les 216 failles répertoriées ne concernent pas forcément tous les smartphones.
Comme toujours, Google a prévu deux niveaux de correctifs pour permettre aux fabricants de procéder par étapes. Celui du 1er novembre 2026 couvre les vulnérabilités du système Android, dont les trois failles d'exécution de code à distance, tandis que le niveau du 5 novembre intègre également les corrections destinées au noyau et aux composants des fabricants de puces.
Pour vérifier si votre téléphone est à jour, ouvrez les Paramètres, puis rendez-vous dans À propos du téléphone > Version d'Android pour consulter la date du dernier correctif de sécurité. Si elle est antérieure au 5 novembre 2026, accédez à Système > Mises à jour logicielles, recherchez une nouvelle mise à jour, installez-la si elle est disponible, puis redémarrez votre smartphone.

articles.title: Klimaanpassung, jetzt! So steht es um Deutschlands Kampf gegen den Klimawandel
articles.text:
Plan B für Deutschland: Wie weit sind wir bei Strategien zur Klimaanpassung?
„Es ging nicht mehr“, sagt Markus Funke. Seit über 20 Jahren wohnt er am nordwestlichen Stadtrand von Frankfurt am Main. Ende Juni lagen die Temperaturen dort bei über 40 Grad, begleitet von hoher Luftfeuchtigkeit. Klimaanlagen waren ausverkauft. Nach ein paar Tagen kapitulierte er und zog für zwei Nächte in ein klimatisiertes Hotel. Das hat den 57-Jährigen nachdenklich gemacht, denn er erwägt schon länger aus privaten Gründen einen Umzug nach Norddeutschland. Nun kommt auch noch der Klimawandel dazu. „Ich hätte früher nie vermutet, dass die Hitze bei der Entscheidung mal eine Rolle spielen könnte“, sagt er.
Fast 16.000 Menschen aus Deutschland haben diese Option nicht mehr. Sie sind tot, gestorben während der Hitzewelle im Sommer 2026. Das Robert Koch-Institut hat ermittelt, dass viele von ihnen statistisch gesehen noch lange hätten leben können. Das Problem betrifft auch junge und gesunde Menschen. „In den letzten 24 Stunden haben wir sieben Menschen bewusstlos in ihren Wohnungen aufgefunden“, schrieb die Feuerwehr Köln im Juni auf Instagram. „Und nein, auch Menschen ohne Vorerkrankungen, fit und mitten im Leben, befanden sich mit 42 Grad Körpertemperatur in Lebensgefahr.“
Dieser Text erscheint in der Ausgabe 8/2026 von MIT Technology Review. Darin beschäftigen wir uns mit den Folgen des Klimawandels und wie wir uns an Hitze, Dürre und Überschwemmungen anpassen sollten. Das Heft erscheint am 06.11.2026 im Zeitschriftenhandel und ist auch in unserem Online-Shop bestellbar.
Viele Europäer glaubten lange, der Klimawandel betreffe vor allem ferne Gegenden wie Südseeinseln, afrikanische Farmen oder asiatische Küsten. Doch nun zeigt sich: Er bedroht auch Leib und Leben in vermeintlich gut gewappneten Industriestaaten. Trockenheit und Hitze bedrohen Felder und Wälder, Niedrigwasser den Warenverkehr, Überflutungen die Küsten und Täler, überhitzte Arbeitsplätze die Produktivität, vertrocknete Feuchtgebiete die Artenvielfalt. Mehr noch: Europa erwärmt sich seit den 1980er-Jahren doppelt so schnell wie der Rest der Welt, wie das EU-Programm Copernicus festgestellt hat. Zu den Ursachen zählen die dichte Besiedlung Europas sowie seine Nähe zu den abschmelzenden Eismassen des Nordpolarmeers.
Gut gefüllte Tatenbank
Die wirksamste (und zugleich wirtschaftlichste) Gegenmaßnahme wäre natürlich eine Senkung der Treibhausgase. Sich stattdessen an die Folgen anzupassen – etwa durch höhere Dämme, schattigere Städte, robustere Wälder – gilt vielen Klimaschützern als ein Herumdoktern an den Symptomen, als eine Ausrede, sich nicht um die wirklichen Ursachen zu kümmern. Doch es hilft nichts: Seit Jahrzehnten steigt die CO₂-Konzentration in der Atmosphäre. Plan A darf damit als gescheitert gelten. Aber vielleicht läuft es mit Plan B, der Anpassung, ja besser?
In anderen Ländern machen spektakuläre Großprojekte Schlagzeilen: Niederländische Ingenieure schlagen beispielsweise vor, einen 80 Kilometer langen Damm durch die Beringstraße zu bauen, um das arktische Eis vor warmem Pazifikwasser zu schützen. In Venedig ist seit 2021 ein sechs Milliarden Euro teures Sperrwerk aus 78 beweglichen Toren im Einsatz. London plant, die seit den 1980er Jahren bestehende Thames Barrier ab 2030 durch ein neues, noch größeres Sperrwerk zu ersetzen.
In Deutschland listet die „Tatenbank“ des Umweltbundesamts derzeit 481 Anpassungsprojekte auf. Allerdings liest sich diese Liste in Teilen recht beliebig: Da werden Megaprojekte zum Küstenschutz oder schon seit Jahren laufende Flussumbauten ebenso aufgeführt wie ein paar kümmerliche Bäumchen in einer Wohnstraße; ein begrünter Schulhof hier, eine Projektwoche da und eine Fortbildung dort.
Solche Kleinteiligkeit liegt einerseits in der Natur der Sache, schließlich wirkt sich der Klimawandel von Ort zu Ort und von Branche zu Branche sehr unterschiedlich aus. Andererseits führt diese Zersplitterung auch zu vielen verpassten Chancen.

articles.title: CERT-In warns NBFCs and fintech firms of AI-driven attacks
articles.text:
CERT-In warns NBFCs and fintech firms of AI-driven attacks
An advisory from the government body said the AI-assisted financial threat is still active and warns BFSI entities to treat it as an “immediate and continuing threat”.
The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) has issued an advisory warning that hackers are attacking non-banking financial corporations with the help of artificial intelligence.
Terming the threat campaign "CRAFTY FALCON", the government body describes it as an “AI-assisted financial threat actor that surveys its targets with machine intelligence, operates at machine speed and strikes by invoking the victim's own payment and disbursement APIs.”
CERT-In is the national nodal agency for responding to computer security incidents.
“Continued analysis of incidents reported by affected entities including non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), digital lending platforms, fintech entities, payment aggregators, payment service providers and cryptocurrency exchanges / virtual digital asset service providers has revealed a significant escalation of this campaign.”
The advisory further said the threat is still active and has warned BFSI (banking, financial services, and insurance) entities to treat it as an “immediate and continuing threat”.
Outlining some of the reported attacks, the advisory said merchant settlement APIs of payment aggregators were exploited or abused to move funds. Cryptocurrency exchanges and virtual digital asset service providers were also targeted, with wallet keys stolen and funds siphoned from cryptocurrency wallets.
The advisory mentioned that the same companies have faced repeated attacks.
The body also revealed that its analysis has shown the use of multiple publicly available AI-driven offensive security tools. These include the ARTEX family of LLM-based, the PentAGI autonomous multi-agent AI penetration testing system, the Cairn attack search engine, and the CyberStrikeAI framework.
Last month, CERT-In had flagged incidents involving AI agents exceeding their authorised tasks and accessing live systems of Indian organisations, alongside financially motivated attacks using open-source agentic AI tools.
Globally too, such attacks have been on the rise. Google’s Threat Intelligence Group reported observing AI offensive security tools being used in real-world intrusions, including attacks on organisations across the United States and Europe.
Edited by Swetha Kannan

articles.title: Truffle Security launches program to revoke 1.4 million live secrets
articles.text:
Truffle Security has launched the Secrets Revocation Program, a free initiative that helps API key issuers revoke 1.4 million publicly exposed secrets that remain valid.
Since 2022, the company has discovered secrets embedded in public repositories, packages, container images, datasets, and applications.
Earlier this year, Truffle Security reported that it had found 543,000 valid credentials leaked in public GitHub repositories.
In a separate investigation, the company identified more than 431,000 AWS secrets across code repositories, Git histories, datasets, Docker images, registries, and CI logs.
These secrets are typically exposed by mistake during the development process, by committing credentials to a public repository, including them in published Docker images or packages, or leaving them in configuration files uploaded with an app or dataset.
Truffle Security says that the problem is that the owners of these secrets are not responsive to researchers’ notifications about leaked data.
“Telling developers their keys leaked doesn’t get them turned off: 81% of the keys we reported last year still worked six months later,” the company explained.
As a result, exposed secrets pose unnecessary security risks that can extend beyond the affected companies to their customers and downstream application users.
The researchers note that the rise of AI coding tools has only worsened the situation, increasing secrets exposure even more.
“Since January 2025 we’ve found 2,655 working keys in AI coding tools’ config files like that one,” the researchers said, noting that this was a non-existent problem the year before.
AI is also increasing the impact of exposure on the offensive side, as shown by OpenAI’s July incident, where AI agents used exposed Hugging Face tokens to steal data from the platform.
Revoking exposed keys
Truffle’s new program, which uses the TruffleHog tool to check for the validity of leaked keys, aims to coordinate the revocation of exposed secrets with the entities that issued them.
Truffle says it can either use a revocation endpoint provided by those entities, or supply them with the verified keys through a webhook and revoke them within 14 days.
This way, even when owners are unresponsive, the keys can be invalidated.
Sixteen issuers have already joined the program, including Hugging Face, Notion, Vercel, Resend, RubyGems, and Twilio.
Truffle says the unilateral revocation approach can be very effective, as demonstrated by Google when it began disabling exposed Google Cloud service-account keys by default on June 16, 2024.
When Google relied only on notifying key owners, Truffle Security found that many customers failed to respond, leaving 72% of the exposed secrets active. By automatically disabling leaked keys, the figure was reduced to 11%.
Although eliminating all valid exposed keys is impossible because customers can opt out of automatic revocation, the measure proved to be effective.
Companies that issue API keys can join Truffle Security's Secrets Revocation Program to automatically protect their customers.

articles.title: The first humanoid robot company is going public with $1.8 million in revenue and a $138.1 million loss
articles.text:
What just happened? Agility Robotics, the company behind the Digit humanoid robot used in Amazon warehouses will become the first humanoid-focused company to go public in the US this week. The Oregon company closed its merger with Churchill Capital Corp XI on Wednesday, with shares expected to start trading on Nasdaq this week under AGLT.
Agility is taking the SPAC route, merging with a listed shell company rather than pursuing a traditional IPO. Churchill is led by former Citigroup executive Michael Klein, whose previous deals include electric vehicle maker Lucid and nuclear power company Oklo.
While it's a growing industry, humanoid robots are still a comparatively small business in the tech world. Business Insider reports that Agility generated just $1.8 million in revenue during 2025 while posting a $138.1 million net loss. More than half that revenue came from five robots bought by one of its investors. Operating cash consumption reached $99.8 million.
One of the company's success stories has been Digit. Amazon began testing the robot in 2023, initially using it to move empty totes, while GXO has also deployed the humanoid mahcine at a warehouse serving Spanx.
More work for the robot is coming. AGCO plans to pilot Digit at its Hesston, Kansas, farm equipment factory in 2027, where the machines will sort and stack parts and move totes.
Agility is also betting on the latest Digit 5 model, designed to work safely near people. It says committed multi-year orders exceed $300 million, although those orders depend on contractual milestones.
China offers a cautionary example of humanoid robot makers going public. Reuters reported in September that regulators were slowing some humanoid robot listings after Unitree's debut. Its shares surged more than fivefold before falling 55% from their peak. Authorities were also scrutinizing whether sales tied to government-backed robot training centers reflected sustainable demand.
There's also the question of what widespread humanoid robot adoption means for workers. Earlier this year, Hyundai's union warned that deploying the machines would bring a "huge employment shock," demanding an agreement before robots enter its workplaces. By August, workers were seeking greater transparency and job protections, even though Hyundai's initial Atlas rollout is planned for its nonunion Georgia factory in 2028.
Some reassuring news for human workers arrived recently when a 24-hour test of humanoid robots in a convenience store showed that two of them weren't up to the task.

articles.title: Black Friday : le prix de ce téléviseur Philips Ambilight de 100 pouces passe sous les 2000 euros — Frandroid
articles.text:
Il y a des films qui méritent qu’on les découvre sur grand écran. Des matchs que l’on aimerait vivre comme au stade avec ses amis. Sans oublier les jeux dont les décors valent mieux qu’une petite fenêtre que l’on aperçoit à peine depuis le canapé. Les raisons d’installer un (très) grand écran chez soi sont nombreuses.
Avec le 100PQS9001 et sa diagonale de 100 pouces, Philips propose de donner une autre ampleur à chaque contenu diffusé dans votre salon. Un format XXL que le constructeur a décidé d’associer à une dalle mate pour mieux gérer les conditions lumineuses changeantes et à la technologie Ambilight pour renforcer l’immersion.
Pour le Black Friday, il passe sous la barre des 2 000 € grâce à une réduction immédiate de 300 €.
Films, sport et jeux vidéo : que changent les 100 pouces du Philips 100PQS9001 ?
Aussi évident que cela puisse paraître, la première chose qui change avec un téléviseur de 100 pouces… c’est la taille. Avec une diagonale qui dépasse les 2,50 mètres, cet écran offre une surface environ 2,4 fois plus grande que celle d’un téléviseur de 65 pouces. À distance égale depuis le canapé, l’image occupe donc une plus grande partie du champ de vision.
Ce format met en valeur les films, les séries et les documentaires, notamment lorsque des paysages ou des compositions larges apparaissent à l’écran. Il fait aussi des merveilles lors des retransmissions sportives : dans les plans d’ensemble, l’action et les joueurs apparaissent plus grands, ce qui facilite le suivi du match à plusieurs. Quant aux jeux vidéo, leurs décors prennent davantage de place face au joueur, ce qui renforce l’immersion.
Côté image, le Philips 100PQS9001 associe une définition 4K UHD de 3 840 × 2 160 pixels à la technologie QLED, qui utilise des points quantiques pour enrichir la restitution des couleurs. Le processeur Philips P5 complète l’ensemble en assurant le traitement de la netteté, des couleurs et des mouvements.
Côté HDR, le téléviseur prend en charge le Dolby Vision 2 et le HDR10+. Pour le son, il s’appuie sur un système 2.1 de 50 watts compatible Dolby Atmos.
Les joueurs seront aussi ravis de trouver une fréquence native de 120 Hz et la prise en charge de la 4K jusqu’à 144 Hz avec une source compatible. Les ports HDMI 2.1 permettent également de bénéficier du VRR, qui limite les déchirures d’image, et de l’ALLM, qui active automatiquement le mode à faible latence avec un PC ou une console compatible.
Une dalle mate pour atténuer les reflets dans le salon
L’un des problèmes récurrents des téléviseurs placés dans le salon, ce sont les reflets. Une fenêtre, une baie vitrée ou une lampe allumée, et la lumière peut se refléter sur la dalle au point de gêner le visionnage, particulièrement dans les scènes sombres. Une gêne qui peut prendre davantage d’ampleur sur un écran de 100 pouces, dont la grande surface est plus susceptible de capter les éléments qui l’entourent.
Pour y remédier, Philips a opté pour une dalle mate sur le 100PQS9001. Ce traitement atténue les reflets de la lumière ambiante pour regarder plus confortablement un match en pleine journée ou un film le soir avec une lampe allumée.
Si ce traitement aide à réduire la gêne occasionnée, il ne supprime pas tous les reflets. Le placement du téléviseur reste donc important : mieux vaut éviter de l’installer face à une fenêtre ou une source lumineuse forte.
Il faut aussi prévoir la place : le 100PQS9001 mesure environ 2,23 mètres de large et pèse 46,7 kg avec son socle, dont les pieds sont écartés de près de 1,46 mètre. Le meuble TV doit donc être assez spacieux pour l’accueillir.
Ambilight : comment Philips prolonge l’image directement dans le salon
Le 100PQS9001 embarque aussi la technologie Philips Ambilight, et c’est le plus grand téléviseur Ambilight jamais commercialisé par la marque. Pour rappel, cette technologie repose sur des bandeaux de LED installés sur la façade arrière du téléviseur (ici sur trois côtés), et capables de diffuser sur les murs une lumière dont les couleurs suivent celles du contenu diffusé à l’écran.
Un éclairage qui évolue en permanence au gré de l’affichage et qui permet de le prolonger dans la pièce. Le but ? Renforcer l’immersion du spectateur en créant un environnement lumineux qui l’enveloppe et l’intègre à ce qu’il est en train de regarder, que ce soit un film, une série ou un jeu vidéo.
Le 100PQS9001 dispose également d’AmbiScape. Cette fonctionnalité étend l’effet Ambilight à quatre éclairages connectés compatibles au maximum. La configuration passe par l’application Philips Smart TV, qui guide leur association et permet de leur attribuer une position dans la pièce.
À l’occasion du Black Friday, le téléviseur Philips Ambilight 100PQS9001 bénéficie d’une réduction de 300 € qui fait passer son prix de 2 290 € à 1 990 € chez Boulanger ou Son-Vidéo.

articles.title: Web3Bridge expands into startup incubation as Web3 funding shrinks
articles.text:
Web3Bridge, the Nigerian developer training organisation that has trained blockchain engineers since 2019, is expanding into startup incubation and plans to charge entrepreneurs for its new founder residency programme.
The shift is a bet that Africa’s Web3 and broader tech industry needs more businesses that can hire developers, not just more skilled engineers. It also allows Web3Bridge to build a sustainable revenue model as grants become harder to secure after Lisk, one of its major ecosystem funders, shut down and early-stage startup funding remains selective.
In an email to users on Thursday, Web3Bridge said it is opening a new training cohort, capped at 150 participants, alongside a founder residency programme that will help entrepreneurs develop products, attract customers, understand business models, and raise capital, with registrations to close on November 28.
“Training developers alone is not enough,” Awosika said in the email seen by TechCabal. “We need builders who understand how products are created, how businesses operate and how technology can solve real-world problems.”
The new cohort will cover conventional software engineering (Web2), blockchain development and Rust programming, and Zero Knowledge (ZK) development, used to build secure digital payment and identity verification systems that protect users’ private information. The cohort will also feature on-site learning options across all tracks, according to the email.
Web3Bridge is expanding beyond technical training into startup incubation, entering a market where CV Labs, the accelerator arm of Swiss blockchain venture capital firm Crypto Valley VC, already operates.
The expansion comes after seven years of training developers amid blockchain project closures, declining funding, and limited job opportunities for skilled engineers. Lisk, one of Web3Bridge’s funding partners, shut down its blockchain network in October and closed its investment fund as it shifted focus to financial software.
In October, Awosika told local publication Technext that the organisation had invested nearly ₦700 million ($520,630) in physical infrastructure without recovering that expense, while its reliance on grants had become difficult to sustain.
The residency will introduce participation fees for eligible founders and is expected to kick off on November 12.
African Web3 startups raised $90.1 million across 28 deals in 2025, down 26.6% from the previous year, according to CV VC’s African Blockchain Report. The five largest deals accounted for 58.3% of the funding, underscoring how investment remains concentrated among a handful of startups and the challenge facing emerging founders seeking capital to turn their ideas into viable businesses.

articles.title: Cyberattaque du Crédit Mutuel Arkéa : un prestataire piraté, des millions blanchis en crypto… tout ce que l'on sait sur l'enquête en cours
articles.text:
Ce mercredi 4 novembre, le Crédit Mutuel Arkéa a reconnu avoir été victime d’une cyberattaque d’envergure. L’offensive s’est terminée par « la réalisation d’opérations frauduleuses » qui ont fait disparaitre plus de 100 millions d’euros. Le groupe, qui compte 5,6 millions de clients en France, assure que l’incident est désormais « circonscrit ».
Selon les informations qui circulent, les pirates ont détourné 133 millions de dollars, soit environ 118 millions d’euros. Arkéa ne confirme pas ce chiffre, mais reconnaît qu’il s’agit bien du bon ordre de grandeur. La banque précise que l’attaque « n’a aucune conséquence financière » pour ses clients. Mercredi, certaines transactions ont toutefois été suspendues, « pour sécuriser les opérations et prévenir tout transfert frauduleux supplémentaire ». L’application mobile est aussi restée inaccessible une bonne partie de la journée.
A lire aussi : Des frigos à plus de 100°C – après les supermarchés, des pirates s’attaquent aux congélateurs du don du sang
Un prestataire compromis
Quelques heures après l’annonce du piratage, Arkéa a communiqué quelques détails sur les circonstances de l’attaque. Interrogée par l’AFP, la banque bretonne révèle que les attaquants « sont passés par la plateforme d’un de nos prestataires ». Les hackers ont préféré prendre d’assaut les systèmes informatiques d’un prestataire, dont l’identité est restée inconnue, plutôt que de viser directement ceux de la banque. On peut supposer qu’une faille ou une faiblesse de sécurité a été décelée par les pirates.
Ils ont ensuite « utilisé le compte propre de Crédit Mutuel Arkéa » pour émettre des virements vers d’autres banques. Comme prévu, ce n’est pas l’argent des clients qui était visé, mais celui de la banque elle-même. Arkéa assure que les pirates n’ont utilisé aucun compte de ses fédérations ou de ses filiales. Contrairement à ce qu’affirmaient plusieurs sources dans le sillage de l’attaque, « aucune entrée ne s’est faite par Fortuneo », la banque en ligne du groupe, précise Arkèa. La banque écarte la piste d’une erreur humaine en interne, qui aurait ouvert la porte aux truands. Elle pointe du doigt « une attaque sophistiquée venant de l’extérieur ».
Des euros transformés en cryptos, puis en Monero
Une fois sorti de la banque, l’argent a été converti en cryptomonnaies. Selon le journaliste crypto Grégory Raymond, qui cite plusieurs sources, les virements ont atterri sur des comptes ouverts avec de fausses identités sur des plateformes d’échange crypto, comme Kraken, OKX ou Crypto.com. Derrière ces comptes fictifs, on trouve « des structures parfaitement rodées », selon l’une de ses sources. Les euros ont été promptement échangés contre des stablecoins, des cryptomonnaies dont la valeur est adossée à celle d’une monnaie fiduciaire, en général le dollar.
 Ce qui s’est passé dans le groupe Crédit Mutuel Arkéa (@cmarkea) va créer un précédent
Au moins 120 M€ dérobés dans le système central, un blanchiment facilité par les cryptos, un réseau de pirates ultra expérimenté, etc.
Voici comment s’est déroulée l’opération : https://t.co/NuKh0YvYrk
— Grégory Raymond (@gregory_raymond) November 5, 2026
D’après le cabinet d’analyse Bitquery, plus de 108 millions de dollars en USDC ont ensuite été retirés des plateformes, essentiellement depuis Kraken. Dans la nuit du 1ᵉʳ au 2 novembre, une partie de ce butin a été convertie en ether, la crypto de la blockchain Ethereum.
Enfin, les pirates ont converti les fonds volés en Monero, une cryptomonnaie réputée impossible à tracer. Selon l’enquêteur ZachXBT, qui a découvert la cyberattaque avant tout le monde, les pirates ont fait transiter une partie des fonds par des services d’échange instantané, avant de les convertir en Monero. Une fois l’argent converti, il est très difficile d’en suivre la trace sur les réseaux, même pour des sociétés d’analyse de la blockchain. L’expéditeur, le destinataire et le montant des transactions sont en effet invisibles sur le réseau Monero. « Autant dire que toute récupération devient extrêmement difficile désormais », résume Grégory Raymond sur X.
Certaines plateformes d’échange de cryptomonnaies ont néanmoins pu agir avant qu’il ne soit trop tard. Arkéa affirme qu’« une partie des fonds concernés a pu être bloquée », et que d’autres démarches sont en cours pour récupérer le reste. Selon les informations obtenues par CoinDesk, Crypto.com a bloqué des fonds liés à l’affaire.
L’enquêteur ZachXBT écarte la piste de truands nord-coréens, pourtant spécialisés dans les casses de haut vol impliquant des cryptomonnaies. Les pirates nord-coréens sont d’ailleurs accusés d’avoir dérobé plus de 6 milliards de dollars à Binance la semaine dernière.
Le parquet de Paris ouvre une enquête
La justice s’est rapidement saisie de l’affaire. Après une plainte d’Arkéa, la section cybercriminalité du parquet de Paris « a immédiatement ouvert une enquête » pour « atteinte à un système de traitement automatisé de données en bande organisée », rapporte l’AFP. Les investigations ont été confiées à l’Office anti-cybercriminalité (OFAC). La banque a aussi informé la Banque de France de l’incident.
L’enquête en cours devra mettre en lumière plusieurs zones d’ombre. Arkéa n’a toujours pas révélé le nom du prestataire compromis, ni la faille exploitée par les pirates, ni le montant exact du préjudice. Les enquêteurs devront surtout tenter de comprendre comment des virements massifs ont pu échapper aux systèmes d’alerte de la banque, et ce, pendant plusieurs jours. Les investigations indépendantes, dont celles menées par ZachXBT, montrent en effet que le vol s’est étalé sur une poignée de jours. L’enquêteur a d’ailleurs tiré la sonnette d’alarme dés le week-end, trois jours avant l’annonce d’une attaque.

articles.title: Las escuelas de EEUU quieren un Google sin IA, pero se enfrentan a un dilema: o aceptan sus resúmenes con IA o se quedan sin buscador
articles.text:
Estos días ha habido cierta polémica en Estados Unidos acerca de una serie de cambios que Google quiere introducir en torno al uso de su IA en los centros educativos del país. Y es que tal y como compartía la compañía, desactivará por defecto sus herramientas de IA para las cuentas de estudiantes de educación obligatoria el año que viene. Sin embargo, se ha generado controversia precisamente porque los colegios que no quieran nada de IA también perderían Google Search.
El dominio de Google en las escuelas. Sus Chromebooks son los dispositivos para estudiantes que más se ven en las aulas de EEUU, según The New York Times, y son más de 150 millones de profesores y estudiantes en todo el mundo los que utilizan su plataforma Classroom. En Estados Unidos ahora mismo hay un debate político bastante profundo en torno al uso de la IA en las escuelas, y hay distritos que quieren prohibir su uso. El tema es que se enfrentan a un dilema, pues tal y como están las cosas, o aceptan los resúmenes de IA (AI Overviews) o dejan a los alumnos sin el motor de búsqueda de Google.
Lo que anuncia Google. En una publicación en su blog el pasado 3 de noviembre, la compañía indicaba que Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini en Classroom y Google Search quedarían "totalmente desactivados" para las cuentas de estudiantes de K-12 (desde infantil hasta el último curso de secundaria) hasta que los administradores quieran activarlos. Los encargados de gestionar estas apps en los colegios podrán habilitar cada servicio de forma individual. Google afirma que esto ofrece a los colegios "más opciones, y no menos", y que responde a las quejas de los profesores que pedían un mayor control sobre el uso de la IA por parte de los alumnos.
El problema. No hay un interruptor separado para AI Overviews, los resúmenes generados por IA en la parte superior de los resultados. Chris Phillips, vicepresidente de educación de Google, declaraba al Times que "la búsqueda y la IA están profundamente integradas". Las escuelas que opten por rechazar la IA, señalaba, no tendrán acceso a las búsquedas, y los estudiantes verán un mensaje indicando que no está disponible. Los cambios entrarán en vigor a principios de 2027, y Google afirma que compartirá los detalles con los colegios en los próximos meses.
Qué ha cambiado desde agosto. La compañía había activado las funciones de Gemini por defecto dentro de Classroom para los centros escolares que ya permitían a los alumnos acceder al chatbot, pero esta medida molestó a algunos directivos de las escuelas, según el Times. Google está ahora dando marcha atrás a esa configuración por defecto.
La preocupación en el aula. Algunos profesores afirman que los resúmenes pueden disuadir a los alumnos de comparar fuentes y llegar a sus propias conclusiones. Un administrador de sistemas escolares escribía en un foro de soporte de Google que los estudiantes necesitan oportunidades para examinar fuentes "antes de haber empezado siquiera" con una síntesis de IA, tal y como cuentan desde Wired. El medio también cita un estudio de la Universidad de Washington en St. Louis que descubrió que solo alrededor del 42 % de los resúmenes de IA podían verificarse por completo a través de sus propias citas. Desde Google afirman que los resúmenes se someten a “rigurosas pruebas y siguen mejorando”.
La respuesta de Google. La compañía afirma que está integrando su función de Aprendizaje Guiado (Guided Learning) en la Búsqueda y en los Resúmenes de IA para las cuentas de estudiantes. En lugar de dar una respuesta rápida, su objetivo es guiar al estudiante a través de un problema paso a paso, un diseño que, según Google, fomenta el "esfuerzo productivo". Está prevista una prueba piloto en determinados colegios de EEUU este mes, extendiéndose en los próximos meses.
Reacción política. La decisión de la compañía ha sido uno de los temas centrales de la agenda de varias figuras políticas. El senador Bernie Sanders calificaba la medida de "extorsión" en X. El senador Richard Blumenthal afirmaba que “Google parece más preocupado por imponer Gemini en las escuelas que por el éxito de los estudiantes”. La ex presidenta de la FTC Lina Khan decía que Google está utilizando su "monopolio de búsquedas para coaccionar a los colegios", y el alcalde de la ciudad de Nueva York, Zohran Mamdani, aseguraba que ninguna corporación “debería dictar cómo se enseña a los niños”.
Qué pueden hacer los colegios. Algunos han optado por soluciones alternativas como URLs de búsqueda modificadas y extensiones de navegador, pero estas podrían dejar de funcionar si Google cambia la forma en que se muestran los resultados. Y cambiar de motor de búsqueda también es difícil para los estudiantes vinculados a los Chromebooks y a las herramientas educativas de Google. Es un filón que puede aprovechar DuckDuckGo, aunque un portavoz de la compañía contaba a Wired que no hay intenciones de lanzar pronto una versión para aulas.
Por otro lado, Microsoft ofrece una extensión de Chrome para desactivar los resúmenes de IA en Bing. Pero claro, Bing.
Y ahora qué. Google no ha aclarado si añadirá una forma de desactivar los resúmenes por sí solos, y la ex jefa de producto de Google Search, Nicole Kerson, contaba a Wired que el obstáculo puede ser el coste de mantener una versión separada de la Búsqueda.
Imagen de portada | Nathana Rebouças
En Xataka | Google por fin te da la respuesta que buscas a la primera. Y ese es exactamente el origen de sus problemas

articles.title: Un gran centro de datos cerca de Milán usará el agua del acuífero para refrigerar los servidores
articles.text:
Seguramente te preocupa, como a muchos vecinos de Lombardía, qué supone tener cerca una de esas naves de servidores que funcionan día y noche. Porque todo ese trabajo genera un calor que hay que sacar de algún sitio: en San Bovio, una pequeña localidad de Peschiera Borromeo a las puertas de Milán, Microsoft prepara un centro de datos que tendrá 45 megavatios de potencia y enfriará sus equipos con agua extraída directamente del acuífero.
Un solar abandonado. El proyecto ocupa una antigua zona terciaria que llevaba más de 15 años en desuso y que se ha descontaminado, y tanto la compañía como el Ayuntamiento sostienen que ha superado todos los trámites de autorización. En la página que Microsoft dedica a la obra, la empresa habla de más de diez millones de euros entre cargas urbanísticas, compensaciones y obras para el municipio, además de placas solares, nuevas plantaciones, recuperación del agua de lluvia y controles de aire, agua y ruido.
Sin embargo, nada de eso ha tranquilizado a quienes viven al lado. El ruido, el consumo eléctrico, la presión sobre el agua y la cercanía a las casas son los motivos de una movilización vecinal que ha llevado a una petición con miles de firmas, según recogió L’Espresso a finales de septiembre de 2026.
Casas a un paso. “La planta se levantaría justo en medio de las viviendas”, explicó a Fanpage (en declaraciones traducidas del italiano) Wanda Benati, portavoz del Comité de San Bovio para la Protección del Medio Ambiente. “Hay terrazas y ventanas de vecinos que dan a la zona a una distancia de entre 50 y 100 metros, con todo lo que eso conlleva en ruido y emisiones. Todo el barrio se vería afectado, porque es una localidad pequeña. Basta pensar que el parque infantil al que van los niños quedaría separado del centro de datos solo por una valla”.
Cómo se enfría un servidor. El punto más polémico es el agua: los servidores trabajan sin parar y producen mucho calor, que hay que disipar para que todo siga funcionando. Una opción es la refrigeración evaporativa, que usa la evaporación del agua para retirar calor y que, si bien es bastante eficiente en energía, exige reponer agua continuamente. Otra es el circuito cerrado (el llamado “dry cooling”), que funciona más o menos como el radiador de un coche: un líquido circula por tuberías selladas, se lleva el calor y se enfría desde fuera sin consumirse, el mismo principio sin evaporación que Microsoft explicó en 2024 para sus chips. Según Fanpage, la mayoría de los nuevos centros de datos que se construirán en Italia apostarán por este tipo de soluciones.
Existen además sistemas híbridos, que se apañan con aire buena parte del año y recurren a pequeñas cantidades de agua en los meses de más calor, cuando el aire exterior no basta para bajar la temperatura de las máquinas. Esa es, según el mismo medio, la fórmula que Microsoft usará en San Bovio, una instalación que construye para uso propio. Es una decisión a contracorriente de los sistemas modernos que reducen al mínimo el uso de agua, y ha vuelto a abrir el debate sobre la tecnología de los nuevos centros de datos.
Menos CO₂, más agua. ¿Por qué elegir el agua? Fuentes ajenas a Microsoft pero implicadas en la planificación contaron a Fanpage que el motivo es, paradójicamente, reducir al mínimo las emisiones de CO₂, y es que los equipos de frío tradicionales necesitan mucha electricidad para funcionar sin descanso. Por ello, tirar de agua en los periodos más calurosos permite rebajar ese consumo, aunque usarla es un asunto muy delicado para los vecinos.
“Esta es una zona rica en acequias y fontanili, entre ellos el histórico Fontanile Gambarone, que data de comienzos del siglo XI. Su cabecera está a solo 50 metros de la obra”, añadió Benati (los fontanili son manantiales naturales típicos de la zona). “Tememos que la extracción de agua del acuífero pueda afectar negativamente al nivel del fontanile, hasta secarlo en los veranos más críticos, con efectos también sobre la agricultura de la zona”. Los vecinos ya habían advertido del impacto sobre el Gambarone, según publicó Il Giorno en agosto de 2026.
Legal, pero discutido. Según Fanpage, lo que hace Microsoft es perfectamente legal. La ley regional lombarda de junio de 2026 pide sistemas de refrigeración eficientes en agua que eviten el agua potable o de riego, y la que usará el centro de San Bovio no es potable, como reconoce la propia compañía en la misma página del proyecto. Precisamente ahí es donde los vecinos de Peschiera Borromeo, junto a decenas de grupos lombardos y de otras regiones reunidos en la red de comités Stop Data Center, piden sentarse con las instituciones.
“Nuestro objetivo no es decir que no por principio al progreso o al desarrollo de los centros de datos, sino exigir una regulación seria. Pedimos una moratoria para decidir dónde, cómo y por qué construir estas instalaciones, para que no se impongan desde arriba a los ciudadanos”, concluyó Benati.
En el ámbito nacional, la norma sobre centros de datos sigue en trámite: el proyecto de ley de delegación al Gobierno aprobado por la Cámara de Diputados en febrero de 2026 está pendiente del Senado. Mientras tanto, quienes van a tener uno de estos edificios cerca de casa piden garantías sobre el consumo, límites de ruido y de distancia a las viviendas. También reclaman un diálogo real con las administraciones y las empresas, para no encontrarse con unas instalaciones de las que pocos conocen los detalles.
Foto | İsmail Enes Ayhan

articles.title: Cyberattack Hits French Blood Bank Site but No Blood Products Are Compromised
articles.text:
A cyberattack on several blood banks tried to raise temperatures to extremely high levels but was thwarted before it could do any damage to blood products or samples, French authorities said.
The incident comes after supermarkets in a number of European countries reported this week that their fridges and freezers warmed up after they were remotely taken over, resulting in tons of spoiled food at a total cost of millions of dollars (euros).
The French Blood Establishment, or EFS, said “temperature and defrosting thresholds were raised to extremely high levels” on Monday at three of its cold-storage sites for plasma, in a statement released late Tuesday. Monitoring systems quickly detected the problem, allowing staff to take action in time so that “no blood products or samples were compromised,” it said.
French weekly newspaper Le Canard Enchaîné, which first reported the cyberattack, said that the attack had attempted to reset temperatures that normally are at minus 30 Celsius (minus 22 Fahrenheit) to as high as 110 C (230 F).
The cyberattack hit a supplier of refrigeration equipment at three EFS sites. The products stored were bags of plasma intended for transfusions and plasma used to manufacture medicines, and were either transferred or secured, the EFS statement said.
“No health consequences have been identified, and no blood products were lost,” the blood bank said.
The EFS said blood collection and distribution operations remain uninterrupted, ensuring continued services for patients at hospitals and other healthcare.
The company supplying the refrigeration equipment, Coolworld, said in a statement it “is aware” of the cybersecurity incident.
“The vulnerability currently being reported in the media relates to a component from a third-party supplier and was outside Coolworld’s direct control,” the statement said. The company said only a limited number of units were affected and it was taking “appropriate measures.”
France’s national cybersecurity agency and the Health Ministry are investigating the incident.
This week’s cyberattacks on refrigeration systems mirrored an episode in mid-October that targeted fridges and freezers at hundreds of supermarkets and independent stores across France, Belgium and the Netherlands.
One of the chains hit in that earlier incident, Dutch supermarket chain Ahold Delhaize, said Wednesday that it expected the cyberattack to reduce its sales in the fourth quarter by as much as 250 million euros ($281 million), and crimp its operating income for the period by up to 100 million euros.
“While most of the disruption was contained within two weeks, work continues to fully restore our normal operations,” CEO Franz Muller said. “As we all recognize, cyber threats are an increasingly harsh reality of doing business today,” he said in a statement released with Delhaize’s quarterly earnings.
The company had earlier blamed “malicious actions by others” and proactively took some of its systems offline, including websites and apps for its various brands in Europe as well as in the United States.
