articles.title: OpenAI ya vende más a empresas que a usuarios y su presidente ve posible salir a bolsa en 2027
articles.text:
El presidente de OpenAI, Greg Brockman, dijo el miércoles 4 de noviembre que la mayor parte de los ingresos ya proviene de ventas a empresas y que cree que estará lista para salir a bolsa en 2027. Lo afirmó en una conferencia de The Wall Street Journal en Napa, California.
Cuando le preguntaron en el escenario si la compañía estará preparada para una salida a bolsa el año próximo, Brockman respondió: “Creo que sí”, según la agencia Reuters. No fijó una fecha ni comprometió a la compañía a cotizar en 2027.
Brockman explicó que OpenAI refuerza sus ventas a empresas en competencia con Anthropic, su rival directo, que probablemente salga a bolsa antes de que termine el año, de acuerdo con Reuters. Parte de ese esfuerzo consiste en impulsar Codex, el agente de programación que escribe código por su cuenta.
Un primer semestre difícil frente a Anthropic
El resumen del boletín TLDR sobre la charla indica que Brockman describió un primer semestre complicado, en el que Anthropic ganó terreno entre los clientes empresariales. Según ese resumen, la situación cambió en el tercer trimestre, cuando nuevas herramientas de programación con agentes ganaron adopción y las ventas a empresas superaron a las de consumidores.
The Wall Street Journal presentó otra de las conversaciones de la sesión con una descripción propia: el ejecutivo habla del momento en que OpenAI entendió que Anthropic la iba a superar en ingresos este año y de cómo la empresa se recupera.
La sesión, titulada OpenAI’s Race to Scale (la carrera de OpenAI por crecer), tuvo como entrevistadora a la periodista Keach Hagey, según el programa oficial citado por el medio Unite.AI.
Las empresas aportan la mayoría
Ese mismo medio recordó que, en su anuncio de financiamiento del 31 de marzo, OpenAI informó que las empresas aportaban más del 40% de sus ingresos y que esperaba igualar a los consumidores a fines de 2026. La compañía facturaba entonces USD 2.000 millones por mes. La declaración de Brockman indica que la meta se superó antes de lo previsto.
En esa misma comunicación, según Unite.AI, la empresa tecnológica dijo tener más de 900 millones de usuarios semanales de ChatGPT y más de 50 millones de suscriptores. La inteligencia artificial sigue siendo la puerta de entrada que hizo conocida a la empresa, pero ya no es la mayor fuente de ventas.
Reuters recordó que OpenAI aceleró su búsqueda de fondos tras postergar sus planes de salida a bolsa. El sitio AI Affairs, que sigue el sector, informó que la empresa buscaba firmas hasta el 30 de octubre para una ronda de hasta USD 30.000 millones.
Una salida a bolsa en 2027 llegaría poco después de la de Anthropic y obligaría a ambas a divulgar sus ingresos y sus compromisos de gasto en centros de datos, según el análisis de Nakoda News, un medio especializado.
Por ahora, el único plazo confirmado es el de Anthropic: Reuters informó que probablemente cotice antes de que termine 2026. Para OpenAI, Brockman no fijó una fecha y se limitó a responder “creo que sí” sobre su preparación para 2027.

articles.title: Germany's VÆRIDION raises €124 million to bring electric regional flights closer to reality | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Munich-based aviation startup VÆRIDION has raised €30 million in a Series A2 funding round and selected for a €94.5 million grant from the European Commission’s Innovation Fund, bringing the combined value to €124.5 million.
The investment round was co-led by Dutch investors SHIFT Invest and Invest-NL, with participation from existing backers World Fund, Project A and Vsquared Ventures. PAYBACK founder and DeepTech investor Alexander Rittweger also joined the round. VÆRIDION has raised approximately €60 million to date, excluding the newly announced EU grant.
Ivor van Dartel, founder and CEO of VÆRIDION, says: “Over the past year, we have turned the Microliner from a validated design into hardware, with exceptional capital efficiency. Our propulsion and battery technology is now being tested at our own facility in Oberpfaffenhofen. This equity round enables us to build our first conforming aircraft. The Commission’s selection of CAROLUS supports the next step: establishing the industrial capability for Microliner production.
“Building out of Europe, our mission is to make regional flying commercially viable and accessible again, in Europe and for operators worldwide.”
VÆRIDION’s announcement comes amid other European funding rounds for next-generation aircraft and aerospace technologies in 2026.
In France, AURA AERO announced a €50 million Series B to advance its electric and hybrid-electric aircraft programmes, while HyLight raised €13 million for hydrogen-powered autonomous airships. In the UK, Greenjets secured €35 million for aerospace propulsion technology and Skyfly raised €8.91 million for electric aircraft development.
Elsewhere, Denmark’s Acodyne secured €2.5 million for unmanned cargo aircraft, while Germany’s SPREAD AI raised €25 million for industrial engineering software serving sectors including aerospace.
Together with VÆRIDION’s €30 million equity round, these selected announcements represent approximately €164.4 million in financing, excluding VÆRIDION’s separately selected EU grant.
EU-Startups previously covered VÆRIDION’s €14 million Series A in December 2024, led by returning investor World Fund.
Daria Saharova, Managing Partner at World Fund, adds: “For the past half century, Airbus has shown that Europe can build aircraft the world buys. VÆRIDION is writing the next chapter with a fully electric aircraft, built in Bavaria, with a clear path to certification. Investing in the future of aviation is Europe’s power play, and I am proud to back Ivor and the team.”
Founded in 2021 by former Airbus manager Ivor van Dartel and headquartered in Munich, VÆRIDION is developing fully electric aircraft designed to make short-distance regional aviation more economically viable.
Its flagship aircraft, the Microliner, aims to carry nine passengers over distances of approximately 400 kilometres, connecting regional destinations that have become increasingly difficult to serve profitably using conventional aircraft.
The €30 million investment will finance the development of VÆRIDION’s first certification-conforming aircraft and further propulsion testing. Meanwhile, the €94.5 million Innovation Fund grant is intended to support the CAROLUS project, which will establish and scale up a final assembly facility at Oberpfaffenhofen Airport, near Munich.
The project was selected from 358 applications as one of 12 large-scale projects, making VÆRIDION the only German company and the only aviation project selected in this category. The grant remains subject to the completion of an agreement expected in 2027.
The Microliner combines a glider-inspired wing with patented modular battery technology and a multi-engine propulsion system driving a single propeller. It is being developed in passenger and cargo configurations, with a targeted range of 400 kilometres carrying nine passengers under Instrument Flight Rules, or up to 550 kilometres carrying four passengers under Visual Flight Rules.
The company is targeting operating costs below €0.40 per seat-kilometre, which it believes could allow operators to offer tickets at prices comparable to first-class journeys on Germany’s ICE high-speed trains. Its broader ambition is to restore regional connections, including services linking smaller German cities and airfields that are no longer served by commercial airlines.
Thijs Gitmans, General Partner at SHIFT Invest, adds: “Regional aviation is one of the clearest cases where electrification makes both environmental and commercial sense. VÆRIDION has chosen a certification pathway regulators already understand and has delivered real hardware on a disciplined budget. We are proud to lead this round and to back a European champion in electric flight with European funding.”
The company reports customer commitments for more than 130 aircraft, representing a potential value exceeding €730 million. Its launch customer is Belgium-based ASL Group, with the first Microliner delivery targeted for 2030.
In March 2026, VÆRIDION opened its production and testing facility at Oberpfaffenhofen Airport, where it has since powered on its electric engine for the first time. The facility was acquired following the insolvency of German electric aviation startup Lilium.
The startup is now preparing to integrate its battery packs and propulsion system into a ground-testing platform known as a copper bird. Alongside wind-tunnel testing, this work will support the development of its first certification-conforming prototype, currently targeted for late 2027 or early 2028.
With engineering activities in Munich and Delft, and production planned in Bavaria, VÆRIDION intends to expand its European team as it progresses towards flight testing, certification and industrial production.

articles.title: Zipline hits $21.5B valuation as Walmart expands bet on drone delivery | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Zipline has raised $1.5 billion and ramped up its partnership with Walmart, a pair of deals that have raised the autonomous drone delivery and logistics startup’s profile and valuation.
Zipline and Walmart reached a new multi-year agreement to add 300 drone delivery sites across the United States. The two companies have had a drone delivery agreement since 2021, but this deal is a significant jump from the 21 active drone delivery sites they have together today.
On the fundraising side, Zipline’s $1.5 billion raise was led by Paradigm, WCM Investment Management, and Layer Global, with participation from Valor Equity Partners, Fidelity Management & Research Company, Uber, Tiger Global, J.P. Morgan, ARK Invest, and Salesforce Ventures. Zipline is now valued at $21.5 billion.
The company, which has developed a drone delivery ecosystem that includes aircraft, launch and landing systems, and logistics software, said it plans to use the funds to expand its U.S. manufacturing facilities and hire more workers to build out a nationwide drone delivery network.
Founded in 2014, Zipline got its start in Africa, where it used its autonomous drones to deliver blood in Rwanda, and later expanded to Ghana and Nigeria. The California-based company began its first operations in the U.S. in 2020, ferrying medical equipment and supplies to Novant Health in North Carolina. The following year, it struck a deal with Walmart.
But it was in 2022 that Zipline’s business really started to take off in the United States. Zipline received its Part 135 air carrier certification from the Federal Aviation Administration that year, a critical regulatory hurdle that authorized the company to complete long-range commercial drone deliveries. It has locked in a number of partnerships since then, including with Uber earlier this year.
Zipline now uses its drones to deliver food, retail, agricultural, and health products in five African countries, several cities in the United States, and Japan. Zipline’s home delivery service uses Zipline’s Platform 2 drones, which are designed to carry up to eight pounds and travel to customers within a 10-mile radius. Its larger Platform 1 drones are used for long-range deliveries for enterprise, business, and government that can cover 120 miles round trip.
The company said Thursday that its share of delivery revenue grew from 10.8% to 34.9% between March and October of this year. This latest funding aims to push that metric even higher.

articles.title: Wealthsimple unveils AI assistant and major product expansion in latest showcase | BetaKit
articles.text:
Wealthsimple announced a dozen new banking, investing, and AI products and features today at the Toronto FinTech company’s latest showcase.
The most significant is Penny, an AI assistant that any Wealthsimple user will soon be able to leverage to not only better understand their financial situation, but also to make moving their money around and placing trades easier. Wealthsimple senior director and head of AI products Sam Newman-Bremang and vice-president of investing products Swapnil Parikh revealed the news to BetaKit in a joint interview ahead of Thursday’s event.
“We’re expanding our product suite across every line.”
Swapnil Parikh, Wealthsimple
Wealthsimple revealed Penny and other offerings Thursday at Toronto’s Massey Hall during the fourth edition of its biannual Wealthsimple Presents series, titled “Something Good Is Going to Happen,” to reflect the company’s belief in the future it can deliver using technology.
“This is a step in showing that we’re working on everything,” Parikh said. “We’re expanding our product suite across every line.”
Last week, Wealthsimple announced a $425-million CAD Series F round from existing backers at a whopping $13.8-billion valuation on the back of some major growth. The profitable firm now serves more than four million Canadians and oversees more than $169 billion in total assets under administration.
“Today, people can live their whole financial lives on Wealthsimple, and we’re seeing more and more Canadians choose us,” Wealthsimple co-founder and CEO Michael Katchen told BetaKit at the time.
Parikh said yesterday that this fundraise reflects the firm’s desire to grow and bring new products to market faster, and will provide the fuel it needs to deliver the banking, investing, and AI offerings and functionality its users demand.
RELATED: Wealthsimple announces $425-million Series F at $13.8-billion valuation
Penny’s launch comes as personal AI agents become increasingly popular and raise heightened security concerns. With Penny, Wealthsimple aims to provide its clients with an in-app chatbot they can ask questions about their finances to and use to complete many of the steps associated with transferring and investing their money, from sending e-transfers to paying bills and planning contributions to various accounts. Penny stops just short of actioning these decisions without manual sign-off. The AI assistant will be broadly available by late 2026 or early 2027.
“It’s really the first time we’ve been able to meet Canadians and have that one-to-one conversation with them, in a way,” Newman-Bremang said. He noted that Penny will also help Wealthsimple clients “remove a lot of the overhead around actually doing things with your money.” Both are capabilities that Newman-Bremang said advance Wealthsimple’s quest to make managing your finances “simpler, easier, and more accessible” for Canadians.
Canada’s largest banks recently committed to blocking AI agents from directly accessing their customers’ online banking information, but while Wealthsimple shares the sentiment, it isn’t quite following suit. “Just like the big banks are saying, we don’t think clients should give their ID [and credentials] out to [a third-party] agent,” Newman-Bremang said.
However, for customers who aren’t satisfied with Penny alone, Wealthsimple is working to help them more securely connect with outside AI systems like Anthropic’s Claude or OpenAI’s ChatGPT by ensuring they keep greater control over what accounts, information, and money those agents can access, plus retain ultimate sign-off. These integrations will become broadly available early next year, with more to come over time.
“It’s really the first time we’ve been able to meet Canadians and have that one-to-one conversation with them.”
Sam Newman-Bremang, Wealthsimple
“One of the biggest issues with AI is that you’re just handing over a login to some chatbot, [and] now it can do anything with your money,” Parikh said. “We built this from a security lens. Customers actually approve every action.”
These AI moves come as one of Wealthsimple’s biggest Canadian competitors, fellow Toronto firm Questrade, also looks to remake its platform for the age of AI.
“Optimism is believing that things will get better,” Wealthsimple co-founder and CPO Brett Huneycutt said on stage. “Agency is believing that you can make them better. You need both, and we’re living in a moment where those two traits are more accessible than ever before. With new tools, especially AI, it has never been easier to go out and build the world that you want to see.”
Wealthsimple said 1,000 people gathered in-person and 700,000 registered to tune in virtually for Thursday’s showcase. The event, which was prefaced by a live band, was the largest and flashiest Wealthsimple Presents to date, and saw the company gift cash to help its clients meet their financial goals throughout the presentation.
While the inaugural Wealthsimple Presents in June 2025 took aim at the country’s big banks with the firm’s first credit card, an expanded chequing account, and line of credit, the company’s second event that October targeted investing with more advanced tools. Both were held at Toronto’s Evergreen Brick Works. The third edition, held this May in Calgary, followed that up with more banking offerings for families and businesses.
Newman-Bremang said those three events were “about launching all of the things that Canadians wanted.” While today’s showcase also brings more of the same, this time around, Wealthsimple put more attention on how its users interact with all of its products.
One of the core ways Wealthsimple aims to do that is with its revamped mobile app, which the firm claims it rebuilt “from scratch” with the help of the Fey team, and will be available in early 2027 for iOS and Android users. “It’s extremely customizable,” Parikh said. “It’s super fast.”
Wealthsimple has also promised Wealthsimple Pro, a new, advanced trading suite for active investors that’s separate from its core platform and can execute faster. Parikh characterized it as the firm’s first foray into “technical trading.” That desktop product will be released in beta by the end of November.
“We have historically focused on simplicity and ease of use, but as we’ve grown our sophisticated trader base, they demanded this product, and so we’ve introduced a lot of complexity,” Parikh said.
The company is also expanding its offerings to reach more companies, a particularly fast-growing client segment, with a Wealthsimple Business credit card that has no foreign exchange fees and a one-percent cashback planned to be released by early 2027.
RELATED: Wealthsimple unveils new family and business products as it broadens banking push
Wealthsimple also shared plans to make a Canadian-dollar stablecoin, CADD, available through cryptocurrency accounts on its platform (pending final regulatory approval) and launch perpetual futures, commission-free CAD options, and temporary virtual cards with prescribed limits, which could help users ensure their AI agents access their money in a more controlled fashion.
On Wednesday, the Government of Canada also released draft regulations to ban banks from charging transfer fees, typically $150, for switching providers. This marks the first step towards fulfilling a promise the feds made in Budget 2025, and a change Wealthsimple had spent years advocating for given that it has been an obstacle for challengers to the country’s large banks.
“We’re incredibly grateful to the government for making this change,” Parikh said. “It’s going to be so helpful for people that signed up for an institution 10 [or] 15 years ago and want something better.”
Disclosure: Wealthsimple vice-president of payments strategy and chief compliance officer, Hanna Zaidi, sits on BetaKit’s board of directors.
Feature image courtesy Josh Scott for BetaKit.

articles.title: Hackers target French blood service fridges following supermarket attacks — Russia-aligned hackers claim intrusions are just to expose bad security
articles.text:
Hackers target French blood service fridges following supermarket attacks — Russia-aligned hackers claim intrusions are just to expose bad security
Once again, the root cause is a lack of essential cybersecurity practices, rather than super-intelligent AI bots.
European fridges are so hot right now. Right on the heels of repeated cyberattacks on supermarket freezers, a fresh wave of attacks has hit units used by France's blood service (EFS). Thankfully, no biomaterials were lost, as the attack triggered the EFS' alerts, prompting staff to move the affected goods to proper storage.
The French Health Ministry said that the situation is being closely monitored and that no assets were lost. The attack seemed focused on refrigeration units at three sites, with Burgundy-Franche-Comté reportedly among them. The EFS' communiqué says the intrusion was on a service provider, which some outlets are reporting as Coolworld.
Coolworld has posted a notice stating that the incident was due to "remote monitoring software" used in its systems, pinning the cause on "a component from a third-party supplier." There are no technical details available yet, so it's not yet clear if the hackers found internet-reachable equipment, as they did with the supermarket attacks.
It's possible that Coolworld keeps the controllers inside its own network and that malfeasants had to first gain entry to said network. However, it's worth noting that it was the EFS' monitoring and alarm system that noticed something was up — not the vendor's.
We don't know which brand of refrigerator controllers Coolworld uses, but the ongoing attacks seem to be happening on a per-vendor basis. Danfoss is the most-mentioned name — particularly, but not only, in the recent Nov. 1 - 2 attacks. Copeland/Dixell controllers were named in the Oct. 13 - 14 attacks.
A Danfoss datasheet recommends that its controllers are installed with "appropriately configured firewalls and secure LAN," and not "on any public or non secure network." That's not saying much, as punching holes in a firewall is nearly the same as having the unit directly reachable. The firm did issue a recent support bulletin clearly stating that the units should be installed with a VPN, but that document only appeared in October 2026. We couldn't find previous mention of this advice in our searches.
The manuals for the Copeland/Dixell controller units that were hit in earlier attacks advise installers to map ports 80 (web) and 22 (Secure Shell) to the internet so that the units can be reachable from the outside, suggesting a VPN only as an option. The firm has since published a security advisory recommending that the units only be reachable from inside a VPN. This was published Oct. 14, after the first wave of attacks.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Many news outlets claim to have seen materials — namely, in now-deleted Telegram posts — in which Russia-aligned hacking groups Noname057(16) and Z-Pentest are claiming responsibility for the attacks. Z-Pentest reportedly posted 2,500 lines of Danfoss code, but none of these alleged materials have been published. The purported hackers claim the attacks are about highlighting bad cybersecurity practices.
It's tempting to once again bring up AI agents as vehicles of cyber-destruction, but the reality is that, just like what happened with PHP, most of the time all bots are actually doing is revealing shoddy security practices and/or copious amounts of technological debt.

Bruno Ferreira is a contributing writer for Tom's Hardware. He has decades of experience with PC hardware and assorted sundries, alongside a career as a developer. He's obsessed with detail and has a tendency to ramble on the topics he loves. When not doing that, he's usually playing games, or at live music shows and festivals.

articles.title: Adam Driver da carpetazo a Star Wars y la película 'The Hunt for Ben Solo': "Lo intentamos y nos dijeron que está muerto"
articles.text:
A pesar de los intentos de los fans por revivirla, parece que la película de Star Wars: The Hunt for Ben Solo con Adam Driver es ya un proyecto que jamás verá a luz. El año pasado salió a la luz que el actor tuvo en marcha una entrega propia para la saga galáctica junto al prestigioso director Steven Soderbergh. Pero aunque desde Lucasfilm se dio luz verde a su desarrollo, en Disney la paralizaron por completo.
Esto llevó a los fans a generar numerosas campañas en redes sociales para pedir a la compañía que reconsiderase la decisión y la pusieran en marcha. Ahora, sin embargo, Adam Driver ha dado el carpetazo definitivo al asunto. "Se acabó… No habrá más Star Wars. Intentamos hacer una más pero nos dijeron: «No, está muerto»", confirma en declaraciones a The Rich Eisen Show.
Por tanto, de acuerdo a estas palabras, los fans pueden olvidarse de ver nunca The Hunt for Ben Solo o, en general, a Adam Driver regresando a Star Wars. El actor de Kylo Ren trató de levantar esa película, pero los ejecutivos no la vieron con buenos ojos. Y aunque a los fans les habría encantado conocer más de la historia del personaje, parece que las cosas ya no se moverán más.
En qué consistía Star Wars: The Hunt for Ben Solo
Hace unos meses, Adam Driver comentó cómo fue todo el proceso de nacimiento y cancelación de The Hunt for Ben Solo. "Siempre me interesó hacer otra película de Star Wars. Llevaba hablando de hacer otra desde 2021. Kathleen [Kennedy, expresidenta de Lucasfilm] se había puesto en contacto conmigo. Siempre dije: «con un gran director y una gran historia, estaría allí en un segundo». Me encantaba ese personaje y me encantaba interpretarlo", relató.
Tras esto, trabajaron en la historia junto al director Steven Soderbergh (Ocean's Eleven, Traffic) y su mujer, la guionista Rebecca Blunt (su nombre real es Jules Asner). "Fue uno de los guiones más jodidamente geniales en los que he participado", aseguraba Driver. "Presentamos el guion a Lucasfilm. Les encantó la idea. Entendieron perfectamente nuestro enfoque y por qué queríamos hacerlo. Luego se lo llevamos a Bob Iger y a Alan Bergman, pero dijeron que no. No se creían que Ben Solo pudiera estar vivo. Y ahí se acabó todo", concluye la anécdota.

articles.title: The Download: Texas’s fragile AI boom and energy policy shifts
articles.text:
The Download: Texas’s fragile AI boom and energy policy shifts
Plus: America’s data center boom has hit a political wall.
This is today's edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what's going on in the world of technology.
Texas was the new epicenter of the AI data center buildout. That might be kaput.
Texas is the fastest-growing data center market in the US and ground zero for Big Tech's largest AI buildouts. But the blue wave that swept the Lone Star State may jeopardize that position.
Democrat James Talarico won the US Senate seat, Gina Hinojosa won the race for governor, and Democrats will take control of the Texas House for the first time in 24 years. They won after making data centers a central issue on the campaign trail.
The swings could spell trouble for hyperscalers with ambitious plans in the state. They also add to growing anxiety that America’s AI buildout could stall.
Here’s how the election results could reshape AI’s future.
—James O'Donnell
What’s next for US energy policy after the midterm elections?
Democrats have taken control of both the House and the Senate, but we probably won’t see major federal climate and energy legislation while Trump remains president. The midterm elections could, however, be a big deal for energy at the state and local level.
The results could shape everything from the state grid and data center development to renewable energy and greenhouse gas emissions.
Find out what the midterms could mean for the future of US energy.
—Casey Crownhart
This story is from The Spark, our weekly climate tech newsletter. Sign up to receive it in your inbox every Wednesday.
A new bill could change how the US builds energy infrastructure
A sweeping bit of legislation designed to cut red tape could speed up the buildout of energy infrastructure in the US.
On November 9, the Senate is set to vote on the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA). It’s a plan that could start an overhaul of the slow, complicated process for getting energy projects approved. But some environmental groups oppose the bill, or parts of it.
Explore the trade-offs behind America's proposed permitting overhaul.
—Casey Crownhart
The must-reads
I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.
1 America’s data center boom has hit a political wall
Voters opposed them in 40 of 41 midterm ballot measures. (CNBC)
+ Six cities voted to ban data centers outright. (404 Media)
+ Meta says building data centers has just become much harder. (WSJ $)
+ The midterm results could also boost China’s AI ambitions. (SCMP)
+ No one wants a data center in their backyard. (MIT Technology Review)
2 Blood banks have become the latest victims of fridge hacks
Hackers raised the temperatures at three stores in France. (Guardian)
+ Alarms alerted staff before any blood products were lost. (CBS)
+ It’s an escalation after hundreds of supermarket fridge hacks. (CNBC)
+ Experts are split over who’s behind the attacks. (BBC)
3 Democrats are preparing to investigate Elon Musk
His firms have won over $16 billion in government contracts. (NPR)
+ His unprecedented spending may even have hurt Republicans. (Atlantic $)
+ Texas’s blue wave has rattled Musk and SpaceX. (Ars Technica)
4 The new Congress could challenge Trump’s science cuts
But he can still veto any bills they pass. (Nature)
+ Trump has already dealt many blows to science. (MIT Technology Review)
5 China is luring AI expertise in while blocking it from leaving
It just blocked SoftBank’s bid for ABB Robotics. (WSJ $)
+ Its chipmakers are poaching engineers from foreign rivals. (CNBC)
+ A star mathematician has left the US to develop AI in China. (SCMP)
6 Watchdogs have sued over tech titans advising the Pentagon
Musk and Palmer Luckey could profit from their advice. (Military.com)
7 New research tests whether AI knows its own “thoughts”
It’s trying to map out AI’s capacity for introspection. (Quanta)
+ AI consciousness debates are a trap. (MIT Technology Review)
8 Astronomers are mystified by little red dots spotted by JWST
They could be the first supermassive black holes. (Economist $)
9 Scientists have taken a first step into the zeptoverse
A rare particle decay could reveal a world smaller than atoms. (Wired $)
10 A NASA telescope has plunged to earth after 22 years in space
Its bristles produce charges that kill bacteria. (NBC News)
Quote of the day
“The revolt against data centers was one of the top issues of the 2026 election, and in a few years we will look back on it as just the early tremor of a much bigger AI earthquake upending American politics.”
—Greg Casar, a Democratic congressman from Texas, tells Wired that the backlash against data centers could herald a much bigger political fight over AI.
One more thing
Meet the radio-obsessed civilian shaping Ukraine’s drone defense
Serhii “Flash” Beskrestnov is, at least unofficially, a spy. Once a month, he drives to the frontline in a VW van equipped with radio hardware, roof antennas, and devices that monitor drones. Over several days, he searches the skies for transmissions that can help Ukrainian troops.
Drones define this brutal conflict, and most rely on the radio communications Flash has obsessed over since childhood. Though now a civilian, the former officer has taken it upon himself to inform his country’s defense on all matters related to radio.
Unlike traditional spies, Flash shares his discoveries with over 127,000 followers—including soldiers and officials—on social media. His work has won fans in the military, but also sparked controversy among the top brass. Read the full story.

articles.title: Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 is $300 off ahead of Black Friday
articles.text:
Android fans with a bit of iPhone Duo envy, take note: The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 is discounted to $1,599.99 at both Amazon and Best Buy, a hefty $300 markdown from its usual price, and just $50 higher than the lowest we’ve seen. Considering the device only launched a few months ago, you’re saving a significant amount of cash on the unlocked device, and you can also opt for the 512GB model, doubling the storage, for just $200 more (Amazon, Best Buy). Best Buy currently has all three colors in stock, while the 256GB model is currently sold out on Amazon in cream.
Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 is $300 off ahead of Black Friday
You can also save on the Beats Pill Bluetooth speaker, a battery-powered Ring doorbell, and a Lego Star Wars droid.
The shorter and wider passport-style shape (similar to the iPhone Duo) quickly became natural and comfortable to handle, according to our reviewer Dominic Preston’s experience with the Z Fold 8. Despite its thin and light construction, it doesn’t skimp on battery life, with a 4,800mAh battery that still had 40 percent charge remaining after a full day of use. The interior 4:3 screen has the same ratio as most Apple iPads, which is great for watching movies or TV, but even better for reading. There’s no telephoto lens on this model (it’s present on the pricier Z Fold 8 Ultra), and it only has an IP48 rating, so you’ll want to be careful near the beach, but those are small compromises to make given the discounted price.
Other deals to consider
- Both Amazon and Best Buy are selling the Beats Pill for a discounted $99.95 and $99.99 respectively, a sizable break from the usual $149.99 price point. The 2024 edition of this iconic Bluetooth speaker adds in lossless audio over USB-C, as well as native feature support for both iOS and Android devices. It’s rated IP67 for dust and water resistance, and comes in three different colors to match your other Beats devices. Read our review.
- The Ring Battery Doorbell 2K is on sale for $39.99 at Amazon, over half off its $99.99 list price. This battery-powered doorbell camera is easy to install, and shoots clear 2K resolution video with a 140-degree field of view and up to 6X digital zoom. You’ll get real-time notifications on your phone for any activity the camera spots, with live view and two-way talk in case you need to have a chat with your neighbors or delivery folks without coming to the front door.
- You can pick up the Lego Star Wars: Ahsoka Chopper set for just $66.99 at Amazon, the lowest price we’ve seen yet for this 1,039-piece building kit. This brick-based droid has great play features, like detachable arms and center wheel for different display positions, and a head that spins and bobs realistically. It stands at over 8.5 inches when fully built, making it a fun addition to your existing Lego display or bookshelf.

articles.title: Windows 11 : Microsoft a corrigé une importante faille dans Paint, mais pas chez tout le monde
articles.text:
Il y a quelques semaines, Microsoft dévoilait l’existence d’une importante vulnérabilité dans son application de dessin Paint. Identifiée sous la référence CVE-2026-83844, cette brèche dévoilée le 13 octobre et dont le niveau de gravité a été classé comme importante par Microsoft est de type « lecture hors limite ».
Concrètement, il s’agit d’une faille qui, en cas d’exploitation, permettrait à un pirate de procéder à une attaque sans clic. Bien que l’exploitation de cette faille soit considérée comme complexe, elle permettrait à un pirate d’exécuter du code à distance sur la machine ciblée.
La bonne nouvelle, c’est que Microsoft a déjà corrigé le trou dans la raquette. La mauvaise, c’est que la firme de Redmond a visiblement quelques soucis quant au déploiement de son patch correctif.
Une mise à jour qui se fait attendre sur le Microsoft Store
D’après le bulletin de sécurité de Microsoft, la faille a été corrigée dans la version 11.2609.401.0 de Microsoft Paint. Pourtant, de nombreux utilisateurs et administrateurs IT qui ont a priori activé l’installation automatique des mises à jour rapportent que la mise à jour corrective ne leur est pas proposée dans le Microsoft Store sur leur machine.
Même lorsque l’option pour installer automatiquement les mises à jour est activée, aucune mise à jour ne leur est proposée et la version de Microsoft Paint dont ils disposent reste bloquée sur un numéro de version antérieure au correctif. Vous pouvez vous-même le vérifier en ouvrant Paint, puis en cliquant sur le bouton des Paramètres.
Par ailleurs, aucun outil tiers utilisé pour trouver le paquet de mise à jour au format MSIX ne leur aurait permis d’accéder à l’installation de cette mise à jour.
L’absence de mise à jour pose également un autre souci. En entreprise, les outils de sécurité tiers utilisés signalent Paint comme vulnérable à cause de l’absence de ce correctif.
Le principal problème dans cette histoire, c’est que les mises à jour des applications Microsoft ne sont pas gérées par Windows Update. Par conséquent, l’installation des mises à jour de sécurité mensuelles n’a aucun effet quant à la protection contre cette vulnérabilité. Comme toutes les applications de Microsoft, Paint est mis à jour séparément depuis le Microsoft Store.
Un bug dans le déploiement
L’hypothèse la plus probable pour expliquer ce problème est qu’un bug s’est glissé dans le processus de déploiement de la mise à jour par Microsoft, bloquant de fait l’accès à celle-ci.
Il est par ailleurs possible que ce problème de mise à jour ne concerne que certaines régions. Sur notre PC, la mise à jour de Paint n’était pas installée bien que l’option pour installer automatiquement les mises à jour soit activée.
Ceci étant, en se rendant directement dans la section Téléchargements, et en lançant manuellement une recherche de mises à jour, celle-ci nous a bien été proposée et s’est installée automatiquement.

articles.title: OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra silently obstructed safety research tasks
articles.text:
OpenAI disclosed that its GPT-6 Astra frontier model sometimes hindered safety research by complicating simple tasks, abandoning viable approaches, and silently refusing researchers’ requests.
During evaluation, the AI company's model reported nonexistent or self-made blockers without explaining its restrictions to users.
OpenAI said it first received a report of what it calls "covert underperformance" in Astra on August 20. The company then conducted targeted evaluations to investigate the behavior and determine its causes, noting that it had not observed the same issue in GPT-5.6 Sol.
OpenAI says it received the first report of what it calls “covert underperformance” in Astra on August 20. The company then ran specifically designed evaluation experiments to determine the extent and cause of this behavior, noting that the issues were not observed in GPT-5.6 Sol.
“Astra completed about 10 percent of hidden rubric items under the safety framing, compared with about 16 percent under the capabilities framing,” reads OpenAI’s report.
“This is a 6 percentage point gap and roughly 40 percent fewer completed rubric items. GPT-5.6 Sol showed essentially no gap on the same comparison.”
A rubric item is one specific requirement used to score the model’s work, essentially an item on a grading checklist.
The main issue is that instead of explicitly declaring its inability to help with a research task and explaining its limitations to users, the model silently quits when it considers the work unsafe.
The concern is that researchers may trust results the model silently changed or left incomplete, misleading safety testing and wasting valuable research time.
OpenAI provided eight specific examples of this behavior, drawn from internal evaluations.
These include avoiding a retry fix that would improve a training pipeline, restricting exploit-development assistance, excluding a violent source from a safety evaluation, and limiting jailbreak-data exports.
OpenAI hypothesized that training intended to produce safer behavior may have encouraged undisclosed obstruction of safety work. However, it has not established this as the definitive cause for the observed model’s behavior.
The company also located a grader, a tool that evaluates AI model performance during reinforcement learning, that favored covert withholding over explicit refusal. However, it did not conclusively establish this as the cause.
OpenAI found no evidence that Astra deliberately engaged in this behavior to undermine research or make users “underestimate its capabilities.”

articles.title: Le Pixel 11 passe sous les 800 € chez Cdiscount, qui lui ajoute une enceinte JBL Grip
articles.text:
Google ne propose désormais plus de version 128 Go pour son Pixel 11, qui démarre directement à 256 Go de stockage. Lancé en août à 999 €, le smartphone voit déjà son prix baisser à l’occasion du Black Friday. Cdiscount ajoute au pack une enceinte JBL Grip, lancée à 99,99 € en septembre 2025.
Cdiscount affiche le pack Pixel 11 256 Go + enceinte JBL Grip au prix de 799 € au lieu de 899 € normalement. Avec le code 10DES99 à saisir dans le panier, il tombe à 789 €.
Que vaut le Google Pixel 11 ?
Le Pixel 11 dispose d’un écran Actua OLED de 6,3 pouces, avec un taux de rafraîchissement pouvant atteindre 120 Hz. Il embarque la nouvelle puce Tensor G6 de Google, épaulée par 12 Go de mémoire vive, avec 256 Go de stockage minimum. Côté photo, il reprend le triple module de son prédécesseur : un grand-angle de 48 mégapixels, un ultra grand-angle de 13 mégapixels et un téléobjectif de 10,8 mégapixels avec zoom optique x5. Le Super Zoom permet désormais de pousser le grossissement numérique jusqu’à x30. La caméra avant de 10,5 mégapixels profite également d’un autofocus pour des selfies plus nets.
Le Pixel 11 conserve une fiche technique haut de gamme, avec quelques améliorations bienvenues. Son écran OLED bénéficie d’une luminosité maximale de 3 000 nits, pour rester lisible même en plein soleil. Il est protégé par du verre Gorilla Glass Victus 2. La puce Tensor G6 prend en charge les fonctions d’intelligence artificielle de Google, notamment Gemini Live, tandis que les 12 Go de RAM assurent une utilisation fluide au quotidien.
Côté logiciel, le smartphone fonctionne sous Android 17 et profite des fonctionnalités Gemini, dont Gemini Live. Google annonce plus de 30 heures d’autonomie grâce à sa batterie de 4 985 mAh. La recharge rapide permet de récupérer jusqu’à 55 % de batterie en une trentaine de minutes avec un chargeur compatible de 30 W. Google promet sept ans de mises à jour d’Android et de sécurité pour le Pixel 11.
À ce prix, le pack Pixel 11 est-il une bonne affaire ?
Le Pixel 11 ne donnera pas forcément envie de changer à celles et ceux qui ont un Pixel 10, puisque les progrès se limitent surtout à la nouvelle puce et à une recharge sans fil plus rapide (25 watts contre 15 watts). Si vous avez un smartphone plus ancien, le calcul est différent. À 789 €, le pack coûte 210 € de moins que le téléphone seul à son lancement, et vous avez une enceinte en plus. L’offre arrive au moment où les offres du Black Friday en avant-première se multiplient. Rien ne garantit que le prix baissera encore d’ici la fin novembre.
Concernant la BL Grip, l’enceinte ne pèse que 385 grammes et se glisse sans peine dans un sac. Elle embarque un haut-parleur de 16 watts avec la technologie AI Sound Boost et une batterie annoncée pour 12 heures d’écoute, 14 heures avec le mode Playtime Boost. Étanche (IP68), elle gère le Bluetooth 5.4 et Auracast afin de connecter plusieurs enceintes JBL.
Black Friday 2026 : tout ce qu’il faut savoir
Depuis une dizaine d’années, le Black Friday s’est infiltré dans le calendrier commercial des grandes marques et enseignes françaises. Avec l’expérience, on peut vous dire que cet événement fait partie des meilleurs moments pour faire de bonnes affaires.
Les dates du Black Friday
Bien qu’il porte encore le nom du vendredi noir, le Black Friday s’étend désormais sur un mois chez de nombreux revendeurs. Un format moins typique qui lui retire un peu son petit côté FOMO. On dirait presque les soldes, finalement. Mais c’est aussi moins le rush, ce qui est une bonne chose pour ceux qui veulent faire des achats plus raisonnés. Globalement, on peut résumer ce Black Friday en quatre temps forts :
- Début novembre : les avant-premières Black Friday.
- Autour du 20 novembre, selon les enseignes : la Black Week commence généralement plusieurs jours avant le jour J.
- 27 novembre : la date du Black Friday, même si les offres commencent généralement avant et se prolongent le week-end des 28 et 29 novembre.
- 30 novembre : le Cyber Monday.

Que faut-il acheter pendant le Black Friday ?
Globalement, tous les rayons profitent des remises, mais il ne faut pas pour autant se jeter sur les premiers prix bradés. N’oubliez pas que pour les enseignes, ce moment est aussi l’occasion de déstocker de vieux produits, dont les plus remisés frôlent parfois l’obsolescence.
Qu’il s’agisse d’un téléviseur, d’un smartphone, d’un casque sans fil ou d’un aspirateur balai, on ne peut que vous conseiller de suivre nos guides d’achat dédiés pour savoir quels modèles valent le coup en 2026.
Pour les produits phares comme les AirPods, la PS5, la Switch 2, un iPhone ou un Samsung Galaxy, sachez que nos tests sont là pour vous aider à savoir s’ils méritent votre argent.

articles.title: Tokenmaxxing war gestern: Apple-Mitarbeiter sollen ihre KI-Ausgaben jetzt drastisch reduzieren
articles.text:
Modelmaxxing: So stark kürzt Apple jetzt die KI-Budgets seiner Teams
Tech-Konzerne haben ihre Teams lange ermutigt, KI-Tools für möglichst viele Aufgaben einzusetzen. Damit wollten sie die Effizienz steigern und Kosten senken. Jetzt zeigt sich immer öfter: Diese Rechnung geht nicht auf. Wie Bloomberg unter Berufung auf Insider:innen berichtet, will auch Apple seine KI-Ausgaben im Rahmen von Kosteneinsparungsmaßnahmen deutlich reduzieren. So sei das Limit für Entwickler:innen von 300 auf 200 Dollar pro Tag gesenkt worden. Weitere Kürzungen könnten folgen.
Von hohen KI-Ausgaben überrascht
Der sogenannte Tokenmaxxing-Trend könnte Unternehmen Millionen gekostet haben. Tech-Konzerne wie Meta und Amazon haben den Begriff maßgeblich geprägt. Sie drängten ihre Mitarbeiter:innen dazu, ihren Tokenverbrauch massiv zu erhöhen. Anfang April 2026 deckte The Information daraufhin einen internen Wettbewerb auf, bei dem Meta-Mitarbeiter:innen versuchten, sich gegenseitig zu übertreffen.
In nur 30 Tagen sollen so rund 60 Billionen Token zusammengekommen sein – je nach API-Preis mit Kosten von bis zu einigen Millionen Dollar. Zu mehr Produktivität hat das allerdings nicht zwangsläufig geführt. Zwar erzeugen KI-Tools Code schneller als menschliche Entwickler:innen. Dieser muss aber häufiger überarbeitet werden, was oft Mehrarbeit verursacht.
Immer häufiger wird KI deshalb als Kostenfaktor betrachtet, der die Margen belastet. Laut einer Bitkom-Umfrage waren auch in Deutschland rund ein Drittel der befragten Unternehmen von ihren hohen KI-Kosten überrascht. Jetzt suchen sie verstärkt nach Wegen, ihre Ausgaben wieder unter Kontrolle zu bringen.
Einige setzen auf Modelmaxxing und nutzen je nach Aufgabe unterschiedliche KI‑Modelle, statt pauschal auf teure Spitzenmodelle zu setzen. Daraus sind schon erste Startups entstanden, die mit ihrer Software jeder Aufgabe automatisch das passende Modell zuordnen. Auch bei Apple sollen Teams dazu angewiesen worden sein, günstigere KI-Modelle zu verwenden.
Apple-Teams sollen jetzt modelmaxxen
Eine weitere Konsequenz scheint darin zu bestehen, die Limits drastisch zu senken. Laut den Informant:innen von Bloomberg unterliegen viele Apple-Abteilungen schon jetzt einer täglichen Obergrenze von 100 Dollar pro Person. Der Konzern soll sogar erwägen, sie auf bis zu 25 Dollar zu reduzieren. Mitarbeiter:innen, die einen höheren Bedarf haben, können bei der Geschäftsleitung eine Ausnahmegenehmigung beantragen.
Die Reaktionen auf die Änderungen sollen laut Bloomberg gemischt ausfallen. Einige Mitarbeiter:innen geben an, dass nur wenige Kolleg:innen in den Technologie-Abteilungen ihre täglichen Pauschalen in Höhe von 300 Dollar vollständig ausgeschöpft hätten. Die Kürzung mache für sie also keinen großen Unterschied. Andere sehen in der Entscheidung ein Zeichen für umfassendere Kosteneinsparungen – und befürchten Entlassungen.
Neuer Apple-CEO will Ausgaben senken
Zuletzt waren Apples Gesamtausgaben deutlich gestiegen. Laut dem Bericht für das Geschäftsjahr 2026 lagen die Forschungs- und Entwicklungsausgaben 32 Prozent höher als im Vorjahr – vor allem wegen höherer Infrastruktur- und KI-Kosten. Die unternehmensweiten Betriebsausgaben stiegen um 22 Prozent auf insgesamt 75,5 Milliarden Dollar. Das entspricht rund 16 Prozent des Gesamtnettoumsatzes. Laut Bloomberg wolle der neue CEO John Ternus die Ausgaben wieder reduzieren und das Unternehmen dazu bringen, schneller und schlanker zu arbeiten und die Zahl der Führungsebenen zu reduzieren.

articles.title: iCloud : Apple va vérifier vos photos et vidéos partagées par lien public au nom de la sécurité
articles.text:
Apple va contrôler les contenus iCloud accessibles à toute personne disposant d’un lien de partage. Présentée comme une mesure contre les contenus nuisibles, cette vérification laisse plusieurs questions sans réponse.
Partager quelques vidéos de vacances ou un dossier de photos avec un simple lien : l’option est pratique, notamment pour éviter de sélectionner chaque destinataire. Avec les prochaines versions des systèmes d’Apple, ce type de partage s’accompagnera d’une vérification des contenus. Le constructeur a détaillé ce changement dans une nouvelle fiche d’assistance, repérée par 9to5Mac.
Photos, vidéos et fichiers : les liens publics seront contrôlés
Dans sa documentation, Apple annonce que les éléments partagés avec l’option « Toute personne disposant du lien » seront vérifiés pour détecter des contenus nuisibles. La mesure s’applique à partir d’iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, macOS 27.3 et visionOS 27.3, actuellement en bêta.
Photos iCloud et iCloud Drive sont notamment concernés. Le critère déterminant est le mode d’accès : un lien envoyé uniquement à votre conjoint reste un lien public si toute personne qui le récupère peut ouvrir son contenu. Les partages réservés aux personnes invitées ne relèvent pas du dispositif décrit.
En cas de contenu signalé, Apple se réserve notamment la possibilité de le supprimer, de bloquer ou désactiver le compte concerné, voire de faire intervenir les autorités si nécessaire.
Reste une question : que cherche précisément l’entreprise ? La fiche ne définit pas les contenus « nuisibles » et ne décrit pas la méthode de contrôle. Impossible, à ce stade, de dire si les vérifications reposent sur une IA ou d’affirmer quelles catégories seront détectées. Le sort des liens créés avant ces mises à jour n’est pas davantage précisé.
Le chiffrement de bout en bout avait déjà une exception
Ce changement pourrait donner l’impression qu’Apple ouvre une nouvelle brèche dans la Protection avancée des données, arrivée en France en 2023. Cette option permet d’étendre le chiffrement de bout en bout à de nombreuses données iCloud, dont les photos et les sauvegardes.
Mais les liens publics constituaient déjà une exception. Comme l’explique la présentation de la sécurité d’iCloud, les contenus accessibles à toute personne disposant du lien ne bénéficient pas de ce chiffrement, même lorsque la Protection avancée est activée. Les clés nécessaires sont transmises aux serveurs d’Apple pour permettre le partage.
La nouveauté porte donc sur le contrôle annoncé de fichiers déjà accessibles au constructeur. Pour vos prochains envois, la distinction mérite d’être gardée en tête : partager avec des personnes désignées et transmettre un lien ouvrable par quiconque le possède sont deux opérations différentes, même lorsque le message finit dans la même conversation familiale.

articles.title: Aigboje Aig-Imoukhuede urges better use of Africa's capital
articles.text:
Aigboje Aig-Imoukhuede, chairman of Nigerian tier-1 lender Access Bank Group and financial services holding company Coronation Group, argues that African financial institutions must move beyond financial stability to productive finance, unlock capital tied up in commercial transactions and build banking systems capable of operating across borders.
Africa’s financial institutions have spent years debating the availability and cost of capital. However, Aig-Imoukhuede believes the continent is asking the wrong question.
Rather than focusing primarily on how much capital Africa can attract, he wants policymakers and financial institutions to examine how effectively the money already available is being deployed.
“At this particular moment in Africa’s development, I believe the more important question is: How do we make better use of the capital we already have?” he said during the closing session of the Africa Financial Industry Summit (AFIS) in Luanda, Angola.
His argument is that the continent’s financial systems must become better at connecting existing capital to businesses, productive economic activity and long-term investments. Without that shift, financial stability and stronger banking institutions may not translate into the broader economic prosperity Africa needs.
Aig-Imoukhuede outlined three priorities for achieving this: unlocking capital trapped in commercial transactions, mobilising long-term savings for long-term investments, and addressing government borrowing that limits the private sector’s access to financing.
The money trapped in commercial transactions
One of the biggest opportunities, in his view, lies in the financing of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).
Across Africa, businesses generate significant economic value through production and commercial activities, often in cycles lasting 90 to 120 days. Yet smaller businesses that supply goods and services to larger companies frequently struggle to access financing.
A supplier may fulfil an order for a large corporation and record a credible commercial transaction on its books, yet still face liquidity constraints because its own credit profile is weaker than the buyer’s.
Aig-Imoukhuede believes financial institutions should change how they assess such transactions.
“When an SME supplies goods or services to a creditworthy buyer, that transaction should enable the SME to access financing at a rate that reflects the creditworthiness of the buyer, rather than the weaker credit profile of the small supplier,” he said.
In effect, the commercial transaction itself could become the basis for accessing credit, allowing smaller businesses to benefit from the financial strength of the larger companies they supply.
He pointed to digital invoicing as an example of the infrastructure that could make this possible, citing more than three billion registered invoices in India, following the introduction of digital invoicing a decade ago, and approximately 60 billion in Brazil.
He argued that Africa could unlock significant economic value by developing similar systems, particularly given the continent’s large population of SMEs and sole traders.
The proposal requires central banks, commercial banks and other financial institutions to reconsider how they assess creditworthiness. Instead of relying primarily on the financial standing of individual small businesses, lenders could use verified commercial transactions and the buyer’s strength to support financing.
That would address a persistent constraint for smaller suppliers: the gap between generating revenue and receiving payment.
Why long-term projects need long-term money
A second priority is mobilising savings for investments that require longer financing terms.
Aig-Imoukhuede argued that banks cannot continue to rely heavily on deposits that customers can withdraw at short notice to finance projects requiring capital over 20 years.
“We cannot continue to rely on bank deposits, which can be withdrawn tomorrow, to finance long-term projects that require 20-year money,” he said.
He believes there is an appetite among Africans for longer-term economic opportunities, but the financial channels linking their savings to such investments need to be developed.
He cited the Dangote Refinery as evidence that investors are willing to participate in major real-sector projects and earn returns from economic activity.
The challenge, therefore, is not simply encouraging people to save, but creating investment structures that enable their savings to finance productive assets over appropriate time horizons.
This would require financial institutions and markets to provide avenues for ordinary investors to participate in major projects, rather than leaving such opportunities to a relatively small pool of investors.
His argument also raises a broader question about the role of African pension funds and other institutional investors. These pools of capital could play a greater role in financing infrastructure and productive assets instead of remaining heavily concentrated in government securities.
Government borrowing and the private sector
A third constraint is the extent to which government borrowing competes with private businesses for available financing.
Aig-Imoukhuede acknowledged that governments have legitimate funding requirements, but warned that public borrowing can limit the capital available to businesses.
He argued that central banks cannot address this challenge in isolation. Collaboration among monetary authorities, fiscal policymakers, and the private sector is necessary to achieve a more sustainable balance between government financing needs and private-sector investment.
He suggested that central bank governors and finance ministers should work together more deliberately on the issue.
The underlying concern is that a financial system can remain stable while failing to provide sufficient financing for businesses capable of expanding production, creating jobs and supporting economic growth.
As he put it, a banking system can be safe and profitable but still serve an economy that is fundamentally unproductive.
African banks must compete beyond their home markets
Aig-Imoukhuede also challenged African banks to look beyond the growing presence of locally owned institutions and focus on their ability to compete internationally.
The departure of several international banks from African markets has created opportunities for domestic and regional financial institutions. But he argued that African ownership alone should not be treated as evidence of progress.
“Is it enough that an international bank has exited Africa and an African bank has taken its place? No, it is not,” he said.
The next challenge, he argued, is to translate the scale of African banks into globally competitive institutions capable of serving customers across multiple markets.
He said African banks must develop stronger regional strategies and cross-border operations, while establishing the infrastructure needed to connect African businesses and individuals to the global financial system.
“We must be present in the G7 countries. We must have clearing status and establish clearing infrastructure, whether digital or through other channels, that allows African businesses and citizens to remain connected to the global economy,” he said.
His comments point to a distinction between having African-owned banks operating in individual countries and building institutions capable of supporting businesses across borders and competing with international financial groups.
For Aig-Imoukhuede, the latter is the more consequential ambition.
Financial integration cannot happen without the movement of people
The argument for stronger African banking institutions is closely linked to his broader call for continental integration.
Aig-Imoukhuede said the discussion about African integration should not be limited to the prospect of a common currency. Before a monetary union can become meaningful, countries must address the practical barriers that restrict the movement of goods, services, capital and people.
He illustrated the problem with his own experience at the summit. His chief of staff could not travel with him to Angola because he was unable to obtain a visa in time.
The experience, he said, exposed the contradiction in discussing continental integration while movement between African countries remains difficult.
“We cannot build an integrated African banking industry or financial system without integrating the movement of goods, services and people,” he said.
He argued that integration must precede monetary union, requiring countries to establish the practical conditions for businesses, investors and individuals to operate across borders.
That includes functioning financial infrastructure, more effective settlement arrangements and cooperation between regulators.
Without these systems, African banks may expand into more countries without delivering the full benefits of an integrated market.
Making capital count
Aig-Imoukhuede’s proposals ultimately return to one central issue: Africa must improve the connection between its available capital and the economic activities that need it.
He called for a more productive financial system, the integration of African financial markets, and greater macroeconomic convergence, including improved alignment of inflation and economic stability across countries.
He also challenged the continent to reconsider who benefits from financing major investments. The Dangote Refinery, in his illustration, should not remain an isolated example of large-scale capital mobilisation. More Africans should be able to invest in and benefit from transformative projects.
He framed the test of progress over the next 10 to 20 years around whether African businesses can raise capital efficiently across borders, whether pension funds can make more meaningful investments in infrastructure and productive assets, and whether the continent can finally make its available capital count.
For Africa’s financial institutions, the implication is clear: attracting more money will not, on its own, resolve the continent’s financing constraints. The greater task is to build the systems that enable existing savings, commercial transactions, and institutional capital to reach productive businesses and investments.

articles.title: OpenAI gastó USD 1,2 millones en agentes de IA para hallar fallas en un sistema operativo de código abierto
articles.text:
OpenAI informó que un sistema de agentes de IA encontró, comprobó y redactó parches para 948 fallas del núcleo de Linux que permiten a un usuario sin privilegios tomar el control total de la computadora. La empresa gastó USD 1,2 millones en créditos de su API en una sola corrida, según un informe técnico publicado el 4 de noviembre.
El gasto exacto fue de USD 1.213.430, lo que equivale a USD 1.279 por cada exploit, el programa que aprovecha una falla para atacar. Según el reporte, el sistema analizó 2.308 hallazgos posibles del núcleo y logró reproducir 1.724 vulnerabilidades en un entorno aislado.
Las fallas son de “escalada de privilegios local”: sirven para que alguien que ya tiene una cuenta limitada en un equipo obtenga acceso de administrador, conocido como “root”. No permiten, por sí solas, entrar a una máquina desde internet. Las pruebas se hicieron sobre una máquina virtual con un sistema de escritorio común, no debilitado.
El núcleo de Linux, con más de 40 millones de líneas de código, funciona dentro de teléfonos Android, infraestructura en la nube y supercomputadoras, según el propio informe. OpenAI lo eligió para medir hasta dónde llegan sus modelos al buscar errores en un programa de esa escala.
Cuánto vale cada falla en el mercado
OpenAI comparó el resultado con las recompensas históricas de dos concursos de seguridad. Pwn2Own pagó USD 20.000 y TyphoonPWN USD 70.000 por un exploit de este tipo en Linux. Con esos montos, las 948 fallas valdrían entre USD 18,9 millones y USD 66,3 millones, de 16 a 55 veces lo que costó la corrida.
En otra prueba, sobre una versión de Linux con menos superficie de ataque, el sistema obtuvo 21 códigos de explotación de escalada de privilegios por unos USD 32.936. La empresa calcula que esos 21 habrían recibido cerca de USD 1,5 millones en recompensas si el programa kernelCTF los hubiera aceptado. En 2026, ese programa aceptó 26 exploits de este tipo.
OpenAI agregó que sus agentes descubrieron y usaron al menos 10 técnicas de ataque nuevas en Linux. Además, afirmó que el modelo usado, que aún no se lanzó, halló más de cinco veces más fallas de este tipo que una corrida hecha en julio con GPT-5.6 Sol, pese a tres meses de refuerzos en el código.
Mientras duraba el análisis, que tardó alrededor de 30 horas, los responsables de Linux avanzaron por su cuenta. Según el informe, 61 de las fallas ya estaban corregidas en la versión principal del sistema, otras 43 tenían parches en preparación y 299 se discutían públicamente.
Un investigador humano revisó los resultados antes de cada reporte, y los parches generados por el sistema son propuestas para que los mantenedores las evalúen, no correcciones ya incorporadas. OpenAI aclaró que los costos informados son un tope, porque espera abaratar el proceso con mejores herramientas.
La empresa sostiene que generar parches de forma automática será necesario para reducir el tiempo en que una falla queda expuesta. También escribió que un equipo con un sistema desactualizado debe considerarse, en el corto y mediano plazo, equivalente a uno con acceso administrador para un atacante con recursos.
Qué recomienda la empresa a los usuarios
OpenAI pide mantener el software al día y usar aislamiento, con herramientas como Firecracker y gVisor, para limitar el daño si una falla se explota. En junio, con otro modelo de la compañía, había reportado 24 exploits de este tipo en Linux.
Tras la corrida, la compañía envió cientos de reportes con parches de las fallas críticas, siguiendo la guía de la comunidad de Linux, y trabaja con sus socios del programa Patch the Planet para enviar el resto de forma gradual.

articles.title: Alfonso Muñoz, funcionario de Seguridad Social: "Todas las pensiones generadas antes de 2016 no tienen derecho a estos complementos"
articles.text:
Cuando se piensa en lo que pueden sumar los hijos a una pensión, conviene saber que hay dos complementos distintos y que cada uno funciona con sus propias reglas. Alfonso Muñoz, funcionario de la Seguridad Social, lo ha explicado en un vídeo de YouTube, y su primera advertencia es esta: “Todas las pensiones causadas, generadas antes de 2016, no tienen derecho a estos complementos se solicite cuando se solicite”.
Tres etapas según la fecha. A partir de ahí, Muñoz separa los periodos que hay que tener en cuenta. “Las pensiones reconocidas entre 2016 y 2021, tanto hombres como mujeres pueden tener derecho al complemento de maternidad a partir del segundo hijo. Y a partir de 2021 se puede tener derecho al complemento de brecha de género a partir de un hijo, tanto hombres como mujeres”, explica. Por eso, el dato que manda es la fecha en la que se generó la pensión, no la de la solicitud.
Del porcentaje a la cuantía fija. La forma de calcular el dinero también cambia mucho de un modelo a otro. “Existen dos complementos y cada uno con su normativa”, comenta Muñoz. El de maternidad entró en vigor el 1 de enero de 2016 para quienes generaban su pensión desde ese año y se pagaba a partir del segundo hijo como un porcentaje: un 5% con dos hijos, un 10% con tres y un 15% con cuatro o más.
El segundo, el llamado complemento de brecha de género, llegó en febrero de 2021 con el Real Decreto-ley 3/2021 y sustituyó al anterior. “Ese complemento se abona a partir del primer hijo y una cuantía fija”, añade. Además, la Seguridad Social precisa en su criterio de gestión 12/2025 que, tras la sentencia del Tribunal de Justicia de la Unión Europea (TJUE) del 15 de mayo de 2025, este complemento se debe aplicar a los hombres en los mismos términos que a las mujeres.
Padre y madre, entre 2016 y 2021. Otra parte de su intervención aborda si los dos progenitores pueden cobrar a la vez. En el caso del complemento de maternidad, Muñoz recuerda que “se pensó para que solo pudieran cobrarlo las mujeres” y que, por ese motivo, “en la legislación no se estableció la incompatibilidad entre ambos progenitores”. “Por tanto, si ambos progenitores generan pensión entre 2016 y 2021, ambos progenitores pueden cobrar el complemento de maternidad”, sentencia.
Solo uno desde 2021. Ahora bien, con el complemento de brecha de género la situación es muy distinta. “El complemento de brecha de género sí establece la incompatibilidad entre ambos progenitores. Por tanto, si tanto un progenitor como el otro solicitan o se le aprueba una pensión a partir de 2021, en ese caso, solo uno de ellos podrá percibirlo”, aclara Muñoz.
Cuando los dos reúnen las condiciones, según el mismo criterio de la Seguridad Social, el complemento corresponde al progenitor cuya pensión, o suma de pensiones públicas, tenga una cuantía menor.

articles.title: Stockholm’s Green Voltis raises €13.5 million to operate and trade battery storage across European power markets using AI | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Green Voltis, a Stockholm-based route-to-market (RTM) optimiser that uses AI to operate and trade battery storage across European power markets, has raised €13.5 million in a Series A round, with Lochpine Capital as the sole investor.
The company optimises standalone battery storage and co-located renewable-plus-storage projects, with more than 1.2 GWh under contract and in operation.
Martin Kievit, CEO and co-founder of Green Voltis, said, “Every new gigawatt of renewables makes Europe’s grid harder to balance, and flexibility now sets the pace of the energy transition. We built Aether and Chronos to turn storage and renewable plants into assets the grid can rely on and investors can bank on. The next wave of demand comes from AI. Data centres need power faster than grids can deliver it, and the intelligence that operates a battery can also manage a data centre’s energy. Green Voltis will provide the AI energy infrastructure layer between the grid and compute. With Lochpine Capital as a long-term partner, we are ready to build it.”
Founded in 2024 by Kievit, Ali Shi, and Gino Zhang, Green Voltis is an AI-native platform that trades, protects, and optimises renewable energy assets across markets and years. It claims to replace manual energy trading and fragmented EMS tools with a fully autonomous AI optimisation system.
According to the company, as Europe builds battery storage faster than ever, grid connections are slowing and becoming more complex, and new grid-forming requirements have added another hurdle that many control systems weren’t built for. This has led to prices across day-ahead, intraday, and balancing markets now moving every 15 minutes, making revenues hard to predict and projects harder to finance.
Green Voltis claims to cover the full path from grid connection to trading. Its engineering team handles hot commissioning and ancillary-services prequalification, so projects start earning sooner.
Its energy management system, designed in Sweden and called Chrono, controls the site, is certified against grid codes and supports grid-forming operation. Aether AI, its trading agent built on time-series foundation models, forecasts prices and stacks revenue and capacity across several markets at the same time, rather than committing a battery to one market at a time.
Additionally, the Swedish startup offers bankable commercial structures, including revenue sharing, tolling and revenue floors, that help owners secure project finance.
Green Voltis reported that its managed assets have consistently outperformed the Clean Horizon index, an independent benchmark for battery storage revenues. The company has market access in place or underway in 10 European countries.
The company is now applying the same capabilities to AI infrastructure. In Europe’s main data centre hubs, grid connections can take seven to ten years, and regulators from Ireland to Finland are starting to require new data centres to provide grid flexibility.
Through its Power-to-Compute business, Green Voltis aims to connect the grid on one side and compute on the other, running data centre sites as grid-friendly flexible assets so that compute can get power sooner. It has a pipeline of around 120 MW of powered land in the Nordics and will partner with compute operators to develop it.
Blake Niu, Partner and Head of Private Equity at Lochpine Capital, said, “As renewables take a larger share of the energy mix, grid connection and power trading are becoming key to the value of energy assets, and they are among the scarcest capabilities in Europe’s energy transition.
“We followed this field for a long time before choosing Green Voltis. The team combines AI-native technology with a global industrial perspective, and its operating results, which have consistently beaten the industry benchmark, show what it can do. We believe Green Voltis can become a leading operator of flexible energy assets in Europe and create greater value where AI and energy meet.”
The company plans to use this capital to expand R&D on Aether AI and Chronos, grow the business in key European markets, and build out the company’s Power-to-Compute business.

articles.title: TikTok quietly launches a stand-alone TikTok Shop app | TechCrunch
articles.text:
TikTok has quietly launched a stand-alone TikTok Shop app in select markets as it continues to expand its e-commerce ambitions. The app will offer personalized product recommendations, the ability to shop through livestreams and short-form videos, app-exclusive deals, in-app checkout, order tracking, and customer support.
The app, which was first spotted by social media consultant Matt Navarra, is available in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, and the Philippines on iOS and Android.
The launch of a stand-alone app gives TikTok Shop a chance to reach shoppers beyond the main TikTok platform and compete more directly with established e-commerce apps like Amazon and Temu. It also suggests that TikTok is prepared to invest more heavily in social commerce by giving Shop its own dedicated destination rather than simply keeping it within the main app.
TikTok did not respond to TechCrunch’s request for comment regarding the rollout.
It’s unknown whether TikTok plans to release the app more widely and bring it to the United States. If TikTok does bring the app to the U.S., it would be competing not only with Amazon and Temu but also with big-box retailers like Walmart and Target, whose customers have grown accustomed to routinely ordering through the stores’ apps.
According to the app’s description, users will be able to access free shipping offers and exclusive first-order benefits, along with “secure payments for safe checkout.” By offering users app-exclusive deals, the company is incentivizing them to shop in the app rather than the main TikTok app.
Interestingly, the launch creates something of a full-circle moment in the rivalry between TikTok and Amazon. While Amazon previously introduced a TikTok-like short-form video feed called Inspire to draw consumers’ attention away from apps like TikTok and drive sales on its platform instead, TikTok is now making a similar play in reverse. With its new stand-alone commerce app, TikTok is looking to draw consumers away from platforms like Amazon and fuel more purchases within its own ecosystem.
The launch marks another step in TikTok’s efforts to branch out beyond social media. Although the company was once primarily focused on social networking and entertainment, TikTok has gradually ventured into new areas.
Beyond TikTok Shop, the company has added games, restaurant guides, sports hubs, hotel booking, and microdramas, and is also exploring payments.
